Hence notable expressions and variants constantly occur, which we leave the reader, less occupied than ourselves, to collect.

Finally, this entire work would be quite small if the divine Scripture, which he could not have had more readily at hand, were separated and removed from it. Therefore this text, pure and uncorrupted, is to be received without any danger. But if the author had been marked by the stain of heresy, it would be a greater reproach to us that a censured man had produced so outstanding a work while we, in the provinces entrusted to us, live mute, stunned, and senseless—especially in this age, when it is most necessary for us to possess the same fortitude of spirit that those bishops had when our present religious dissension, after that of Arius, is greater than any that has ever arisen among Christians.

If there were now any mortal of so holy a life and sacred an order who should denounce his wicked and ruined ruler in such words as this worthy confessor did, even when sent into exile and banishment, what, I ask, would be said of him? He calls him a serpent, a beast and most savage wild animal, a robber, a sacrilegious man, an executioner, a murderer, an idolater, a temple of demons, and a destroyer of religion; a heretic, an apostate, a forerunner of Antichrist, and indeed Antichrist himself. Moreover, he calls the emperor’s edict of peace—promulgated under the pretext of calming disturbances—sacrilegious and deadly.

The whispering heretics who flatter worldly rulers, striving to persuade them that they are bishops of bishops—as is said in this book to have happened [Col. 0764A] to Emperor Constantius—would now cry out that such persons should immediately suffer capital punishment. They would accuse of folly or simplicity rulers who allowed or overlooked such speech, whether it were our Constantius or that great Theodosius whom St Ambrose expelled from the Church. For they are deeply and bitterly offended that kings cannot make themselves as hostile to good men as Herod was to John the Baptist.

Although before this Constantius, except for his father, no emperor had assumed the Christian name, there was danger lest he should become fiercer and more susceptible to provocation. And it is certain that those emperors were supreme rulers of the whole world, to whom our kings, however powerful, cannot seem equal either in strength or authority. But the more supreme kings excel in power, the more they are almost always endowed from heaven with clemency and humanity, because thus it has seemed good to God, best and greatest, to care for and preserve the affairs of his own and of those who belong to them.

But to conclude: the history displayed here portrays our own times, such as they began some years ago, certainly not without the greatest reproach to all France, which had never before endured or fostered any heresy until it emerged now during the childhood and innocence of our king. May Christ our Lord deign to grant so much aid and grace to this Most Christian and most devout king that he may demolish and overthrow shrines, sacred groves, and every idolatry, and repress and extinguish every heresy.

In this matter, Most Blessed Father, your most holy admonitions will be able to afford much assistance, as they ought, together with that good rule of life which you take care to apply to the abuses of our churchmen. As for me, who am nothing but a little worm of the earth and cannot but lament the disturbed order of the Church and that confusion, I do not therefore wish to withdraw from it or advise anything of the kind to another. It is enough for me to work in the Lord’s vineyard according to the smallness of my powers, to leave you a testimony of my devotion toward you and the Most Holy See, and to pray God, best and greatest, for the prosperity of my king, the tranquility of my country, and the peace of the whole Christian world. May Christ preserve you safe [Col. 0764D] and sound for us in that peace for a long time.

At Meaux, the third day before the Nones of January, 1568.

[Col. 0765]

# LETTER OF OUR HOLY FATHER LUCIFER, BISHOP OF CAGLIARI, PANCRATIUS THE PRESBYTER, AND HILARY, LEGATES OF THE APOSTOLIC SEE, TO EUSEBIUS, BISHOP OF VERCELLI (C, S)

[Note: [Col. 0765A] Since the authority of Eusebius, the most holy bishop of Vercelli, was great, it was highly important that he should be present at the Council of Milan in 355, at which the case of Athanasius and the Nicene faith were to be discussed, in defense of religion. Therefore Lucifer, as leader of Liberius’ pontifical legation, invited him by this letter in Liberius’ name to the council, which had already opened. Eusebius nevertheless delayed his arrival for a long time, until Emperor Constantius himself summoned Eusebius to the synod by letter, since the Arians hoped to draw him over to their opinion. Having received these letters, Eusebius both replied to the emperor that he would shortly be present and hastened immediately to Milan. Eusebius’ Letter to Constantius is extant among the acts of the Council of Milan in vol. II of the Venetian edition of the Councils. In it he writes that he had also received letters from his brothers and fellow bishops—namely Lucifer and the other legates of Liberius—as well as from the bishops of the Arian party, in the name of the whole Council.]

To the most honorable Lord Eusebius, bishop: Lucifer, bishop; Pancratius, presbyter; and Hilary.

[Col. 0765A]

With the devil’s head trodden underfoot and his wicked suggestions defeated, holy lord, we ask you not to neglect the grace granted you by our Lord, but deign to hasten, so that the doctrine of the Arians may be quickly put to flight as it attacks. [Note: [Col. 0766A] Perhaps: “as it attacks.”] For the Lord and his Christ know that, just as at the coming of the most blessed Apostles the name of God is glorified in the downfall of Simon, [Note: [Col. 0766A] This alludes to the arrival of the Apostle Peter in the city of Rome and the downfall of Simon Magus through the Apostle’s prayers.] so, when Valens has been expelled at your arrival, the scheme of the blaspheming [Col. 0766A] Arians may be broken up and destroyed. [Note: [Col. 0766B] He compares Valens with Simon Magus. Valens, as it were the head of the Arian faction, managed everything in the Council at his own discretion against Athanasius and the Catholic bishops. He was Valens, the Arian bishop of Mursa in Pannonia.]

From the first day on which we came to Vercelli, [Note: [Col. 0766B] Lucifer had come to Vercelli in 354, when Liberius sent him to Constantius in order to negotiate with the emperor for convening an ecumenical council in Italy. The emperor was then living at Arles in Gaul.] most holy lord, we have desired your piety until the present day, and we pray the Lord that in this [Note: [Col. 0766B] That is, the Church of Milan.] Church all the saints may praise the perpetual restoration [Note: [Col. 0766B] Namely, of Catholic doctrine against the Arians.] and duly celebrate your spiritual power. [Note: [Col. 0766B] Another reading: “special.”] We believe this will come to pass because we trust that the passion of the Savior cannot be overcome. May Christ the Lord preserve you in glory, most holy and most blessed one.

[Col. 0765]

# LETTER OF POPE LIBERIUS TO LUCIFER IN EXILE (C)

[Note: [Col. 0765C] We have inserted this letter here from Coustantius’ edition of the Letters of the Supreme Pontiffs, where it bears the title “To Eusebius, Dionysius, and Lucifer, established in exile.” It contributes greatly to elucidating Lucifer’s actions; its beginning is connected with what Lucifer himself writes in several places concerning the peace offered by Constantius to the Catholics at the Council of Milan.]

[Note: [Col. 0765C] I retain these words from the other editions. Whether Lucifer had then reached the first place of his exile when he received Liberius’ letter, see what was said in the Preface. In it Liberius congratulates him on the glory of his confession, commends himself to Lucifer’s prayers, and asks him to inform him more fully of everything done at Milan.]

Liberius, [Note: [Col. 0766C] The copy of a similar letter written to Eusebius of Vercelli bears the same title, as is to be noted a little further below [Col. 0767B]. I here append Coustant’s note. This letter appears in Hilary, Fragment VI, from the Remigian and Pithoean manuscripts, as well as in Baronius under the year 355, no. 32, and transcribed by Stephen Ferrerius from the records of the Church of Vercelli and a Vatican codex. It was written not long after the Synod of Milan, held in the year 355 and, as scholars think, at its beginning; before Liberius himself was summoned to Milan, indeed before he had learned with certainty and precision what had been done in the aforesaid synod; accordingly, about the middle of 355. Baronius, under the year 355, no. 34, testifies that in the Vatican codex it is read as addressed both to Eusebius and to the other exiled bishops, Dionysius and all the rest. It would have been desirable for him to have transcribed the actual words of the copy. For I fear that this codex presents nothing other than what is found in Hilary. Before he went into exile, Liberius wrote this identical letter to the Confessors—that is, to Eusebius, Dionysius, and Lucifer, who were in exile. If we adhere to the wording of this inscription, it was not a circular letter addressed to all the Confessors exiled in different places, as Baronius writes, but an identical letter addressed separately to Eusebius, Dionysius, and Lucifer—or copies in the same form for three persons—which was later called *a pari*. At one time I had considered it probable that the same letter had also been sent to the presbyter Pancratius and the deacon Hilary. But since in the letter he addresses those whom he calls at the beginning “most welcome priests in the Lord,” then “holy priests,” and at the end “lords, brethren”; and since it by no means befits a bishop, and above all the bishop of Rome, to address his own clerics by these honorific titles, it seems more likely that Liberius wrote a separate letter to Pancratius and Hilary as to sons. In the records of the Church of Vercelli the particular inscription to Eusebius has been preserved in this form: “Liberius the bishop, to Eusebius, most beloved brother”; but nothing in the course of the letter has been altered. Coustant, with whom we agree; but regarding the time when it was written, see the Preface.] Bishop, to Lucifer, his most beloved brother.

[Col. 0765C]

Although, under the appearance of peace, the enemy of the human race seems to have raged more violently against the members of the Church, yet you, most welcome priests in the Lord [Note: [Col. 0768B] Thus Baronius. But the Pithoean manuscript has “most welcome priests.” [Col. 0768C] Ferrerius has “priests most welcome to God.” Coustant.], have been shown by your outstanding and singular faith both to be approved by God here and already marked out as martyrs for future glory.

With what proclamation of praise, then, with what exultant utterance, shall I set forth the merits of your courage? Placed as I am between grief at your absence and joy at your glory, I am wholly unable to find the words—except that I know I offer you more convincing consolation if you believe that I too have been driven into exile with you. Indeed, as I still hang in this very expectation, I am deeply grieved that, meanwhile, harsh necessity separates me from fellowship with you. For I had wished, most devoted brethren, to be spent before all of you, so that through me your love might more fully attain an example of glory. But let this be the palm of your merits: that you have come before me, through perseverance in faith, to the splendid glory of confession [Col. 0767B].

Therefore I beg your love to believe that I am present with you; and do not feel me absent in affection, but understand that I am greatly grieved because I am meanwhile separated from your fellowship. Finally, you may know all the more fully how great a glory you have attained, because those who have been crowned in persecution could experience only the bloody swords of the persecutor [Note: [Col. 0768C] Ferrerius reads: “because those who have been crowned in persecution [experienced] the sword, the reward of the persecutor alone.” In these last three words the Pithoean manuscript likewise agrees. Baronius, however, gives: “because those who … the blood-stained swords of persecution alone.” “Of the persecutor” should be retained, since it is contrasted with “false brethren,” from whom, Liberius says, it is both more grievous to suffer persecution and more glorious to triumph over them. Coustant.]; but you, devoted soldiers of God in every respect, having encountered even false brethren as enemies [Note: [Col. 0768C] That is, Arian bishops, especially Valens and Ursacius, of whom he often speaks elsewhere.], have gained victory over treachery. And in proportion as their violence could increase in the world, so rewards of praise are found to be bestowed upon holy priests.

Be secure, therefore, concerning the heavenly promise; and because you have been made nearer to God, lift me—your fellow priest, a servant of God—up to the Lord by your prayers, so that we may be able patiently to bear the assaults which, as they are reported day by day, inflict graver wounds: that, with faith unviolated and the condition of the Catholic Church preserved, the Lord may deem me worthy to be made equal to you.

And because I desire to know more faithfully what was done in that very conference [Note: [Col. 0768C] Baronius has “assembly,” rejecting in the margin “conference,” which the other books prefer—and more elegantly. Coustant.], I entreat your Holiness to deign to report everything faithfully in writing, so that either my mind itself, tormented by conflicting reports, or the strength of my body, now exhausted, may receive greater renewal from your encouragement.

And in another hand: [Note: [Col. 0768C] In place of this closing Ferrerius reads: “May God keep you safe, dearest lord brother; likewise, may you deign to remember me and mine.” There the letter is presented as addressed to Eusebius alone. Coustant. This closing was perhaps also appended to the copy of the letter sent to Lucifer [Col. 0768D].] May God keep you safe, lords and brethren.

[Col. 0767]

ONE BOOK OF SAINT LUCIFER, BISHOP OF CAGLIARI, ON NOT ASSOCIATING WITH HERETICS, ADDRESSED TO THE EMPEROR CONSTANTIUS. (C)

[Col. 0767D] When you saw that all your destructive attempts had been countered, and found that every device of yours against the Church of God had been revealed to all God’s people, you said that we had been, and were, enemies of peace, foes of unity, and even opponents of brotherly charity. If there ought to be no separation between the worshippers of God and the enemies of His religion, why, when Moses saw that carnal Jewish people—whose wisdom you possess—had incurred the guilt of idolatry, did he, after causing certain persons to be struck down with the sword, also wish his own station to be set apart? That this was so, receive the written testimony:

And the Lord said to Moses: “Say to the children of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people; beware lest, by bringing another plague upon you, I destroy you. Now therefore put off the robes of your glory and your ornament, and I shall show what I will do to you.” And the children of Israel removed their adornment and robes from Mount Horeb. And Moses, taking the tabernacle, pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and it was called the tabernacle of testimony. [Col. 0769B] And it came to pass that everyone who sought the Lord went out to the tabernacle of testimony, outside the camp. But whenever Moses went out from the tabernacle, all the people stood watching, each at the entrance of his own tent. They watched Moses as he went until he entered the tabernacle. Then, when Moses had entered the tabernacle, the pillar of cloud descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle and spoke with Moses; and all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tabernacle, and the whole people, standing, worshipped, each at the entrance of his own tent. And the Lord spoke with Moses openly, face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. But the minister Jesus, son of Nave, a young man, did not depart from the tabernacle (Exod. XXXIII, 5).

> [Note: Col. 0769D] “Watching,” as in the Greek, σκοπεύοντες (*watching, observing*). Sabbatier reads *watching* in the singular from the edition of the *Bibliotheca Patrum*.

> [Note: Col. 0769D] Thus the Greek, προσεκύνησαν (*they worshipped*); whereas Sabbatier reads *he worshipped* from the cited edition; and a little below, “face to face,” where this text has “openly, face to face.”

By this event it was shown that you, who sin against God, are to be avoided [Col. 0769C] and that one must withdraw from you. But, you say: “Behold, Moses, although he kept the tabernacle in another place, nevertheless did not desert the people, but urged them, with God made favourable, to correct the paths of their errors.” Nor do those who refused to associate with your sacrilege fail in these duties: for you know that you are told that, unless you correct your ways, you will perish eternally.

How, then, can we bring the point we have begun to make to complete proof? Whenever the people murmured against God and rose up against Moses, you have read that God said to Moses and Aaron: “Withdraw from the midst of this undisciplined and stubborn people, and I will destroy them” (Num. XVI, 21).

> [Note: Col. 0769D] Old Version: “Withdraw from the midst of this assembly, and I will consume them together.”

What, therefore, does He wish us to do except flee you as undisciplined and stubborn, lest we perish together with you, as those [Col. 0769D] who had assembled with Korah, Dathan, and Abiram perished? Or will you deny that you are undisciplined and stubborn? Look at your deeds against the Church of the Lord, and you will find how undisciplined and stubborn you are.

In Deuteronomy Moses says:

> [Note: Col. 0769D] Old Version: “You shall not make a covenant with them, nor have mercy upon them … nor join yourselves with them in marriage. You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor take his daughter for your son; for he will cause … [Col. 0770D] [him] to depart … [after] strange [gods] … indignation.”

[Col. 0770A] “You shall not make a covenant with them, nor have mercy on them; nor shall you give your daughters to them in marriage, nor give his daughter to your son. For he will lead your son away from Me, and he will serve strange gods; and the Lord’s anger will be wrathful against you and will quickly destroy you” (Deut. VII, 2).

> [Note: Col. 0770D] Closer to the Greek, ἐλεήσητε (*you should have mercy*). The remaining singular readings are characteristic of this version of Lucifer.

When He commands these things to be done, how can we meet with you or have peace with you, deniers of the only Son of God? How could we have fulfilled this wish of yours, when you see that God said through Moses concerning Moabites and Ammonites: “You shall not greet them peacefully all the days of your life, for ever” (ibid. XXIII, 6)? How could Arians and Christians have been together, when you hear Moses say: “There shall not be an adulteress among the daughters of Israel” (ibid. 17), and everywhere warn that every adulterer is to be put to death, brought to the gate, by stones: “And you shall remove,” he says, “the wicked one from among yourselves” (ibid. XXIV, 7)?

> [Note: Col. 0770D] Old Version: “prostitute.”

If God is said so to abhor carnal adultery that He commanded all adulterers to be punished, how much more must the Lord abhor your spiritual adultery, [Col. 0770B] on account of which you were and are to be fled from. We Christians could not meet with apostates, when we find the Holy Spirit saying through Moses:

“God will open for you His excellent heavenly treasury, to give rain to your land; in due season He will bless every work of your hands. You shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall make war on many nations, but they shall not overcome you. The Lord your God shall make you the head and not the tail; and you shall be above and not beneath, if you obey the commands of the Lord your God, whatever I command [Col. 0770C] you today to keep and do, and do not depart from any word which I command you today, to the right or to the left” (ibid. XXVIII, 12).

> [Note: Col. 0770D] Sabbatier reads *that He may give*; Greek, δοῦναι (*to give*).

> [Note: Col. 0770D] Old Version: “you shall not turn aside from all the words which …”

How could we associate with the Arian pseudo-bishops of your sect, when you see that we could not be blessed except because we did not go after your idolatry; except because we abhorred your Arian heresy, as we abhor the heresy of all heretics; except because we judged and regard you as such as the pagans—namely, worshippers of every demon; except because we abominated you as we do the Jews, who are found to be without God since they denied the only Son of God?

In Jesus son of Nave: “And when the people heard the sound of the trumpets, all the people shouted with a great shout; and all [Col. 0770D] the walls of the city round about fell. And all the people went up into the city, each man straight before his adversaries, and they took the city and devoted it to destruction, and whatever was in the city, from man to woman, from young man to old man, even to calf and [Col. 0771A] draught-animal, they killed with the edge of the sword. And Jesus said to the two young men who had explored: ‘Enter the woman’s house and bring her out, and all that is hers.’ And the two young men who had explored the city entered the woman’s house and brought out Rahab the prostitute, and her father and mother and brothers, and all that belonged to her, and all her kindred; and they led her outside the camp of Israel. And the city was burned with fire, with all that was in it” (Josh. VI, 20).

And below: “Jesus preserved alive Rahab the prostitute and [her father’s whole household], and she lived in Israel to this present day” (ibid. 25).

> [Note: Col. 0771D] Old Version: “and her father’s house”; Lucifer, with the Greek, καὶ πάντα τὸν οἶκον (*and all the household*).

When, therefore, you see that all the inhabitants of the city of Jericho were punished by the edge of the sword and that the whole city was burned, how did you suppose that we could associate with you, a heretic, [Col. 0771B] when we recognized that you and yours deserved an anathema greater than theirs?

> [Note: Col. 0771D] “For an anathema.” Tilius.

How could we associate with the Arian pseudo-bishops of your sect, when you see that no one was preserved alive in the city inhabited by idolaters except Rahab alone, because she believed that our Lord was almighty, while she recognized that the idolatry in which the people dwelling in Jericho trusted had been devised by human error?

How could we associate with you when, in the third book of Kingdoms, it is written that your houses are not to be entered, food is not to be taken with you, and water is not to be received from you?

> [Note: Col. 0771D] That is, Kings, as we shall also note in Book I *For St Athanasius*.

Holy Scripture makes this plain. It says concerning that fellow-apostate of yours: “And the word of the man of God came” (III Kings XIII, 4).

> [Note: Col. 0771D] In the book *On the Apostate King* it reads, “when he heard the words.”

[Col. 0771C] And below: “He stretched out his hand toward the altar, saying: ‘Seize him!’ And the king’s hand, which he had stretched out against him, became withered, and he could not draw it back to himself. And the sanctuary was split open, and its fat was poured out from the sanctuary, according to what the man of God had said by the word of the Lord. And the king answered and said to the man of God: ‘Entreat before the face of the Lord your God, that my hand may return to me.’ And the man of God entreated before the face of the Lord, and the king’s hand returned to him and became as it was at first. And the king spoke to the man of God and said: ‘Come with me into the house and dine, and I will give you gifts.’ But the man of God said to the king: ‘Not even if you gave me half [Col. 0772D] your house would I enter with you; nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place. For the Lord commanded me thus by His word, saying: “You shall not eat [Col. 0771D] bread, nor drink water, nor return by the road on which you went”’” (ibid.).

> [Note: Col. 0772D] There it reads “sacrifice.”

> [Note: Col. 0772D] “Face”; Latin, as in the book *On the Apostate King*; Greek, δεήθητι τοῦ προσώπου (*entreat the face/presence*).

> [Note: Col. 0772D] The Latin has *you gave*; the Old Version agrees with Lucifer.

How could we associate with you in worshipping God, when this man of God, sent by God to rebuke King Jeroboam, was deceived by the one called a prophet and such severe punishment was inflicted upon him? For Scripture then says of that man of God:

“And after this he went by another road and did not return by the road by which he had come to Bethel. [Col. 0772A] Now another prophet lived in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds which the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king; and they turned the face of their father. Their father said to them: ‘By what road did he go?’ And his sons showed him the road by which the man of God who had come from Judah had gone. And he said to his sons: ‘Saddle the ass for me.’ They saddled it for him, and he mounted it and went after the man of God. He found him sitting beneath a holm-oak and said to him: ‘Are you the man of God who came from Judah?’ He said: ‘I am.’ And he said to him: ‘Come with me and eat bread.’ But he said: ‘I cannot return with you, nor eat bread or drink water in this place, for the Lord commanded me thus by His word, saying: “You shall not eat bread there, nor drink water there, [Col. 0772B] nor return from there by the road by which you went.”’ And he said to him: ‘I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying: “Bring him back with you to your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.”’ But he lied to him. He brought him back, and he ate bread in his house and drank water. And while they sat at table, the word of the Lord came to the false prophet who had brought him back; and he said to the man of God who had come from Judah: ‘Thus says the Lord: Because you have provoked the word of the Lord and have not kept the command which the Lord your God commanded you, but returned and ate bread and drank water in the place concerning which He spoke to you, saying, “You shall not eat bread nor drink water,” therefore your body shall not enter the tomb of your fathers.’ And it came to pass, [Col. 0772C] after he had eaten bread and drunk water, that they saddled the ass for him. He returned and went on his way, and a lion found him on the road and killed him. His body lay cast upon the road; the ass stood beside it, and the lion stood beside his body. Men of that city came and spoke in the city where the old prophet lived. When the man who had brought him back from the road heard it, he said: ‘This is the man of God who provoked the word of the Lord.’ He went and found his body cast upon the road; the ass and the lion stood over his body, and the lion had not eaten his body nor attacked the ass” (ibid. 10).

If this befell him because he had eaten bread and drunk water in a profane place among foreigners, [Col. 0772D] what would have befallen us if we had joined in friendship with you, whom we know to be a heretic and a denier of the only Son of God, as you desired? If we had poured out prayer with you Arians? If, finally, we had allowed ourselves, as priests of the Lord, to celebrate with your Arian pseudo-bishops everything that we celebrate?

> [Note: Col. 0772D] For *because*, as often elsewhere.

Meanwhile, by reviewing your deeds, you ought to recognize that you were sent to deceive us just as that false prophet was sent to the man of God. For as he, though a false prophet, called himself a prophet in order to deceive the innocent man, so you, though not a Christian but an Arian, pretended to be a Christian in order to ensnare us. [Col. 0773A]

Then, although the Church of the Lord has always possessed peace and has cast you and the heretics of every sect outside, you said: “I want peace to be established in my empire,” wishing to violate the Lord’s peace among us, desiring to divide God’s people, and working to secure passage for all of us into your heresy. Thus you lied that you were a man of God when you said that you were making this peace for the sake of our salvation—just as that false prophet lied when he said: “Return with me, for I too am a prophet of the Lord, and an angel spoke to me” (III Kings XIII, 18).

> [Note: Col. 0773D] See what we have noted in Book I *For St Athanasius*, and what follows below in this book.

Thus, I say, you lied when you said that you had undertaken this in order to please God, [Col. 0773B] since you laboured to join each Catholic bishop to the communion of the Arians.

> [Note: Col. 0773D] At the Council of Milan, on which matter there will be a somewhat fuller discussion below.

How could Christians associate with you and your fellow Arians, when you see that the Lord said these things to King Jehoshaphat because he had received the idolater Ahab into friendship and gone to war with the enemy of the Lord? For after that sacrilegious Ahab of yours had been struck by a mortal wound in battle according to God’s word, and Jehoshaphat, because he had cried out to God with all his heart, had been restored to his household, Holy Scripture says that Jehu son of Hanani, the seer, went out before him and spoke thus:

“If you help that sinner and are a friend of those who hate the Lord, for this the wrath of the Lord is upon you. Yet good words have been found in you, because you removed the groves from the land and prepared your heart to seek the Lord” (II Chron. XIX, 2).

If these things were said to him, what would be said to us if we had preferred to be friends with you, a heretic and enemy of God?

> [Note: Col. 0773D] “With you, a heretic.” That is the sense intended.

Or will you dare say, “I am not an enemy of God as Ahab king of Israel was”? How are you not an enemy, when you do the same things Ahab did? For you attack the religion of God as he attacked it; you persecute His house as he persecuted it.

How could we associate with you and yours, when that king devoted to God was rebuked by God through a prophet because he had joined King Ahaziah of Israel in friendship? “Jehoshaphat king of Judah,” it says, “made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel; he began to act wickedly. [Col. 0773D] He allied himself with him to build ships with which to go to Tarshish; and he built ships at Ezion-geber. Then Eliezer son of Ozia from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying: ‘Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the Lord has shattered your work; your ships have been broken and will not be able to go to Tarshish’” (ibid. XX, 35).

> [Note: Col. 0773D] *Gaber*, Vatican codex, with the Greek in certain manuscripts cited by Sabbatier.

> [Note: Col. 0774D] “Were able”: so the source, as in the Complutensian Greek, ἐδυνήθησαν (*they were able*). Sabbatier reads “to go to Tarshish.”

If the Lord said those things to him because he had taken the king of the way of destruction as his partner in shipbuilding, what might be said to us if we, priests of God, regarded you—the destroyer of His house and persecutor of the Catholic faith—as a friend of God? If He shattered that man’s work because he had joined himself to a wicked man, surely we ourselves would already have been scattered by lightning because we had joined ourselves to you, a blasphemer.

How could we, servants of God, and you, servants of the devil, meet together, when God has willed there to be as great a separation between us and you as between light and darkness, life and death, sweetness and bitterness; as between the holy angels of God, who continually magnify His mercy, and those apostates whom you will see tormented with you for eternity, unless you rescue yourself from them? How, I say, could we servants of God be with you, servants of Antichrist?

For in the second book of *The Things Left Over* [Chronicles], God said to King Amaziah:

> [Note: Col. 0774D] That is, Chronicles; this is the interpretation of the title.

[Col. 0774B] “The army of Israel shall not go with you, because God is not with Israel, with all the sons of Ephraim. For if you think that you will prevail through them, the Lord will put you to flight before your enemies, because power is from the Lord” (ibid. XXV, 7).

How could we resist the devil if, in your great wickedness, we ran with you—with the enemies of God, with men found without knowledge of God, with men who do not possess God, in whom we know there is a troop of demons? For you cannot be deniers of the only Son of God without demons; you would not blaspheme unless those who blinded your hearts caused you to do so, so that the truth might not be understood by us.

> [Note: Col. 0774D] Vatican reads “by you,” more correctly.

Could we possibly dwell on your side and consent to your most shameful designs, when the Holy Spirit says through glorious David that only those are blessed who have withdrawn from you, deniers of the only Son of God; that only those who have not mixed themselves with your serpent-like thoughts will remain blessed?

“Blessed is he who has not gone in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the seat of pestilence” (Ps. I, 1).

How could there be one assembly for you and us, when you likewise hear David say in the sixth Psalm: “Depart from me, you who work iniquity” (Ps. VI, 9)? If you Arians do not work iniquity, judge for yourself, you leader in the sacrilege of the Arians, who persecute us with dreadful rage although we say that we are Christians. Know, therefore, that we acted rightly in withdrawing from you who are hateful to God. For how was it fitting that we should remain in your assembly, infected with every crime, [Col. 0774D] and not flee you as plagues and pestilences, when he says in the person of our people in the twenty-fifth Psalm:

“Because Your mercy is before my eyes, and I have been pleasing in Your truth. I have not sat in the council of vanity, nor will I enter with those who act wickedly. I have hated the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the ungodly” (Ps. XXV, 3).

> [Note: Col. 0774D–0775D] This also concerns the Council of Milan, in which the Arians proposed that, under the appearance of condemning Athanasius, the Nicene faith should be overthrown—as Sozomen, Book IV, chapter 9, expressly testifies: the Emperor and the Arians contrived Athanasius’ condemnation for no other purpose than to overthrow the Nicene faith.

If your council is not a council of vanity, prove it to me. It is not a vain council [Col. 0775A] in which the entire design is nothing but that the Son of God should be denied; that God the Father should be maintained not to be a true Father; that the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, should be asserted not to be the true Spirit of God; that apostolic and evangelical tradition should be destroyed and the tradition of Arius established? A council in which nothing else is confirmed except what may provide great rejoicing for all heretics, pagans, and Jews? All who abhor the religion of God rejoice because they see you, the emperor, accomplishing what they wished, because they see that you have become a denier of the only Son of God and a persecutor of His servants.

This is the council which you have been accustomed to assemble with all the powers of your empire, precisely in order that every authority of the sacred Scriptures might be dissolved by the authority of your empire, [Col. 0775B] that all truth might be buried, and that the lies of your detestable fabrication might appear true. These are the designs of your deliberation in that notable council, assembled by your power. Therefore you hate us; because we abhor your council of evildoers. Therefore we are in exile; therefore we are killed in prison; therefore the sight of us alone is forbidden; therefore, shut up in darkness, we are kept under heavy guard.

> [Note: Col. 0775D] Again concerning the same Council; it should have been discussed more fully in the Preface, where we also state our opinion concerning the number of bishops present, relying especially on this testimony of Lucifer.

> [Note: Col. 0775D] From this passage of Lucifer we infer that he wrote this book while he was in exile at Germanicia. See the Preface.

For this reason no person is permitted to visit us: because we would not have any fellowship in your crimes with you impious sacrilegious men. From our person this prayer is addressed to God: that, dwelling with you, we might not perish together, but might be separated from your wicked council and your unjust conspiracy. For he says in the twenty-seventh Psalm:

[Col. 0775C] “Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication when I pray to You, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy temple. Do not drag away my soul with sinners, nor destroy me with workers of iniquity—with those who speak peace with their neighbour while evil is in their hearts. Give them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their pursuits; render to them according to the work of their hands; repay them their recompense” (Ps. XXVII, 2).

> [Note: Col. 0775D] As in the Greek, τὴν ψυχήν μου (*my soul*). Old Version: “Do not drag me away,” etc.

Therefore you hate us, Constantius, because we would not have these things said of us which are said through the Prophet’s mouth of you and yours because of your wicked conduct, and which are said of the Jews, whose imitator you have become. If you are not, Constantius Augustus, one who [Col. 0775D] pretended to make peace so that evil purposes might be accomplished—namely, that the Son of God might be denied, [Col. 0776A] that the apostolic and evangelical faith might be destroyed and your Arian heresy established, and that all who did not comply with you might be deported, proscribed, tortured in various ways, and finally killed—then the Holy Spirit, marking and striking you and yours alike, says in the person of our people: “Do not destroy me with workers of iniquity, with those who speak peace with their neighbour while evil is in their heart” (ibid. 3).

> [Note: Col. 0775D–0776D] He speaks of the pacificatory edict issued by Constantius on behalf of the Arians, which he mentions later in this treatise. See below concerning what it was and why it was proposed to Catholics. Lucifer’s whole purpose is to reproach Constantius for his crafty and unjust scheme: under a guise of peace, he endeavoured with all his strength at the Council of Milan to force Catholics to condemn Athanasius and to commune with Arians. Hence his repeated references to “peace”; compare what is said in the Preface. To this belongs what Hilary writes in his one book *Against Constantius*: “He promotes unity in order that there may be no peace.”

You said to us: “I want peace to be made”; yet in your heart, remaining an enemy of our religion, you planned to make us idolaters through yourself. Therefore you will indeed receive according to your work, according to the wickedness of your designs, unless you take heed for yourself.

We avoided and are avoiding your counsel, which was and is formed against God. Foreseeing its designs, the Holy Spirit had already said through David in the thirty-second Psalm: “The Lord has scattered the counsels of the nations; He rejects the thoughts of the peoples and rejects the counsels of princes” (Ps. XXXII, 10). God rejects your counsels uttered against His Church. For He cannot hate His people and His inheritance while loving you, children of pestilence and persecutors of His servants.

You said: “Make peace with the bishops of my Arian sect, and be one.” But the Spirit of God says through Solomon in Proverbs: “Do not pursue the ways of the ungodly, and do not imitate the path of the wicked. Wherever they set their camp, do not go there; rather turn away from it and avoid it. For they do not sleep unless they have done evil; sleep is taken away from them, and they do not sleep. For [Col. 0776C] they feed on foods of impiety and are intoxicated with wicked wine. But the ways of the righteous will shine like light; they advance and give light until the day is made perfect. The ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble” (Prov. IV, 14).

> [Note: Col. 0776D] Sabbatier reads “Do not follow.”

How could we have fellowship with you Arians, spiritual adulterers, when we retain the written saying: “Do not attend to a deceitful woman; for honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, who for a time fattens your throat, but in the end you will find her more bitter than gall and sharper than a sword sharpened on both edges. The feet of fools who use her lead down with death to Hades” (ibid. V, 2).

> [Note: Col. 0776D] Sabbatier reads: “Do not give yourself,” etc.

> [Note: Col. 0776D] *Foolishness*. Latinius. The Greek has ἀφροσύνης (*of folly*).

But perhaps you say that these things are spoken of adulteries of the flesh. If you maintain that they are said concerning fleshly adulteries, how much more must you, spiritual adulterers, be avoided, lest through your Arian heresy, that spiritual prostitute, the things here spoken should come upon us? [Col. 0777A] For it seems sweet to some to join you, the king, in friendship by accepting your heresy; but they will find it more bitter than gall when they begin to experience being tortured with you eternally in everlasting Gehenna—those who chose to be with you. Then they will say: “Woe to us, who placed the Emperor Constantius before God.”

How could we and you possibly meet together, when Solomon further says: “Cast the pestilent man out of the council, and contention will depart with him” (Prov. XXII, 10); and: “Do not imitate evil men, nor desire to be with them; for their heart devises falsehood, and their lips speak pains” (ibid. XXIV, 1). Then: “Do not bring the ungodly near the pastures of the righteous, nor be deceived by fullness of belly. For the righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the ungodly will be weakened in evils” (ibid. 15).

> [Note: Col. 0777D] “Pestilence,” Vatican manuscript, as in the Greek, λοιμόν (*pestilence*).

How can we be with the proud and transgressors, with those who would rather be found with Judas Iscariot [Col. 0777B] than with the most blessed prophets, apostles, and martyrs, when I hear in the hundredth Psalm:

“I walked in the innocence of my heart in the midst of Your house. I did not set before my eyes a wicked thing; I hated transgressions. A perverse heart did not cleave to me; I did not acknowledge evil men who turned away from me. Him who secretly slandered his neighbour, I persecuted; with one of lofty eye and insatiable heart, I did not eat” (Ps. C, 2).

> [Note: Col. 0777D] Sabbatier has: “in the midst of your house.”

> [Note: Col. 0777D] The Old Version punctuates differently: “I did not set before my eyes an evil thing. Those who commit …”

And in the hundred and eighteenth Psalm: “I hated the wicked, and I loved Your law” (Ps. CXVIII, 13). Since you are wicked, as deniers of the only Son of God; since we must hate you because, abandoning the way of truth, you have embraced [Col. 0777C] every error; because, abandoning the light, you have chosen to go into outer darkness—how could we be most dear to you, a wicked head, destroyer of God’s house, patron of all workers of iniquity? How could we be intimate friends, as are Valens, Ursacius, Epictetus, Saturninus, and the rest?

> [Note: Col. 0777D] Valens and Ursacius, also mentioned in Book I *For St Athanasius*, took the lead at the Council of Milan against Athanasius and the Nicene faith, and exercised the greatest influence with Constantius.

> [Note: Col. 0777D–0778D] Epictetus was bishop of Centumcellae and a most violent Arian. He subscribed against Athanasius at the Council of Milan. Athanasius himself says of him in the *Letter to the Solitaries*, while dealing with bishops ordained by Constantius through the Arians: “Constantius keeps Epictetus, a novice, a man fierce in youth and bold in his passions, because he sees him ready and eager for every crime; through his agency he lays snares for whatever bishops he wishes. For there is nothing that man hesitates to do, provided he pleases the Emperor.”

> [Note: Col. 0778D] Saturninus, bishop of Arles, communicated with the Arians at the Council of Arles in 353; at Milan he joined Valens and Ursacius in a compact for Athanasius’ ruin, and through their efforts the Arian plague spread widely through the West. Moreover, he was responsible for the exile of Hilary, bishop of Poitiers, after Hilary had withdrawn from his fellowship following the Synod of Milan; this occurred under Constantius in 356, as Hilary himself testifies in his one book *Against Constantius*.

Though men of their number may see into what pit they have fallen, they nevertheless choose to perish with you, provided that they may enjoy with you the empty splendour of your reign.

> [Note: Col. 0778D] For “empty splendour.” Tilius. Perhaps the expression is to be construed: “provided that they may enjoy with you the empty splendour of your reign,” not “with an empty splendour.” La Cerda, rightly.

How could we be with you, when we regarded as hateful the very things which those men chose to enjoy with you—men who strive after the things that remain forever? In this matter, you and we do not agree: namely, because we refused to accept your heresy; namely, because we Christians refused to become Arians. [Col. 0777D]

Who indeed, unless he is out of his mind like you Arians, would abandon the house of God and make it a monument of the devil? [Col. 0778A] For this reason we suffer hatred from you: because we feared, and still fear, lest those things should be said of us which were said of those deserters, namely the Jews, whom Jeremiah accuses:

“Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord: What stubbornness did your fathers find in Me, that they withdrew far from Me, went after vanities, and became vain? They did not say: ‘Where is God, who delivered us from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness in an uncultivated and unknown land, in a land without water and without fruit, in a land through which no man passed and in which no son of man dwelt?’ And He brought you into Carmel [Col. 0778B] that you might eat its fruit and its good things; but you entered and defiled My land, and made My inheritance an abomination. The priests did not say: ‘Where is the Lord?’ The elders of My law did not know Me; the shepherds acted wickedly against Me; the prophets prophesied by Baal and went after useless things” (Jer. XI, 4).

We did not wish to hear these reproaches, and therefore we declared that you and yours must be fled from.

> [Note: Col. 0778D] The Latin reads *we judged*.

For those of God’s household could not associate with you foreigners, when we see God saying to that unfaithful carnal people of yours: “Turn your foot away from a rough road, and your throat from thirst” (ibid. 25). But where it says: “I shall be strengthened, because she loved foreigners and went after them,” we not only refused to go after you foreigners, after you *allophylai*—people of another tribe—but also pronounced anathema upon you, children of pestilence and [Col. 0778C] darkness. We did so lest, if we departed from the apostolic and evangelical faith and abandoned the way held by the most blessed Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Abel, Enoch, Noah, and all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs, these things also should be said by God of us which were said of your fellow-blasphemers, the Jews:

“As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, so shall the children of Israel themselves be ashamed, with their kings, their rulers, their priests, and their prophets” (ibid. 26).

We did not wish to be among you, lest that rebuke of the divine voice should also accuse us together with the Jews and you heretics: “Why do you speak to Me? You have all acted wickedly and have all transgressed against Me, says the Lord” (ibid. 29).

How could we associate with you, when you read what is written in the first book of Maccabees:

> [Note: Col. 0778D] It agrees with the Old Version from the manuscript of St Germain cited by Sabbatier, except for the words “assembly of Jews.”

**Version. [Col. 0779C] Ancient Version, which also has Vulgate: “A synagogue of the Assideans was gathered to them,” etc.]** Then there gathered to them an assembly [Col. 0779A] strong in might from Israel, every volunteer for the law; and all who fled from evils joined them and became to them [**Note: [Col. 0779C]** “a support.” Latin with the Greek, *eis stērigma* (εἰς στήριγμα), as also the Sangermanensis Version. Ancient Version: “for a support.”] a support. And they established [**Note: [Col. 0779C]** Ancient Version: “they gathered an army … in their wrath … so that they might escape.” The Greek agrees with the version of Lucifer and the Sangermanensis.] force, and struck sinners in their anger and wicked men in their indignation; and the rest fled to the nations to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went about and destroyed the altars; and they circumcised the uncircumcised boys, all whom they found within the borders of Israel, with strength; and they persecuted the sons of pride. And the work prospered [**Note: [Col. 0779C]** With the Sangermanensis Version. The Ancient Version has: “the work prospered … in their hands,” etc.] in their hands; and they recovered the law from the hands of the nations and kings, and did not give heart [**Note: [Col. 0779D]** Sabbatier reads *horn*. So does the Greek. The Vatican Latin manuscript, the Sangermanensis, and the Ancient Version have *heart*.] to the sinner (1 Macc. 2:42).

Could we have been with you, when you see what those men did who were found to have feared God with their whole heart? You say to a limb already cut from the body of the blessed [Col. 0779B] Church, when you became an Arian from a Christian, “Be with us.” Yet the Lord says in the Gospel: “If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it away from you. For it is expedient for you that one part of your members should perish, rather than that your whole body should be cast [**Note: [Col. 0779D]** With the Sangermanensis and Corbie manuscripts. Ancient Version: “go.”] into Gehenna. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut [**Note: [Col. 0779D]** Ancient Version: “cut it off, and let one [member] perish,” etc.] it off and cast it away from you; for it is expedient for you that one part of your members should perish rather than that your whole body should go into Gehenna” (Matt. 5:29).

The Church condemns Arius for having cut himself off and cast himself away according to the Lord’s command; and you say, “Receive your fellow-pestilences and plagues [**Note: [Col. 0779D]** He speaks in Latin, that is, of persons full of plague; so the Comic poet said: “that crime which destroyed me.” La Cerda.]”; you say, “Allow yourselves to perish by the same disease by which I have perished.” Thus Sabellius was cut off from the body of the Church, as was also this your utterly detestable Arius; and his discourse, like a cancer, has [Col. 0779C] so powerfully spread through you that you are now seen to be wholly cancer. Nor will you be able to say that you have not been made cancerous by Arius’s discourse [**Note: [Col. 0779D]** That is: you will not be able to say that Arius’s words have not made you cancerous—that they have not consumed you and made you foul, as the disease cancer gnaws and makes bodies decay. For the stench of your cancerousness, that is, of your Arian dogma, which like cancer spreads everywhere and corrupts all, has now invaded almost all Italy. Tilius. Apuleius used the same word in *On the Virtues of Herbs*, in the sense “to pass into the nature of cancer,” as Cangius notes in the *Glossary*. As cancer gnaws the body and causes it to decay, so you likewise are putrid. La Cerda.], since the stench of your cancerousness has reached every place in your kingdom, and we have all resolved to avoid you, lest we too should be made cancerous by your Arian pestilence.

Thus, I say, your master Arius was cut off and cast away, just as Sabellius was cut off and rejected, [Col. 0780A] because he dared to maintain that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one person; because he dared to say that he himself was both Father and Son and Holy Spirit. He was cut off because he did not hesitate to say that the Father himself was incarnate in the Virgin’s womb and suffered. Thus Marcion [**Note: [Col. 0780C]** Around A.D. 134 Marcion disseminated his heresy, by which he denied that the Son of God had assumed a true human body; and in A.D. 146, and again in 167, he was expelled and condemned by the Roman Church.] was cut off and cast away [**Note: [Col. 0780D]** A nominative is lacking here—perhaps “God,” or “the Church cast [him] away,” etc.], because he refused to confess that the Son of God assumed human nature from the Virgin’s womb and thereby became man. Thus Paul of Samosata, Photinus’s master, was cut off and rejected from the body of the Church, [**Note: [Col. 0780D]** He impiously taught that Jesus Christ was a mere man. He was first condemned in the Synod of Antioch in A.D. 265. Photinus, bishop of Sirmium, later drew the same poison of impiety from Paul; he was deposed from his see and condemned at the Council of Sirmium in A.D. 351, in Petavius’s judgment.] because he deigned to call the Son of God merely man.

Thus also the heretics of every sect are cut off, as Arius was cut off, and as you will deserve to be cut off, because you say of the Son of God [**Note: [Col. 0780D]** We correct this from the Latin and Vatican manuscript, where what was previously printed was “by God’s counsel.” The Vatican adds “only.”]: “He was made from nothing; he is not a true Son; there was when he was not.” [Col. 0780B] Therefore all you blasphemers have been cut off and cast out, by the power of God, from the Church of his mercy, because you did not remain in the faith in which the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs remained.

O man cut off from the body of the holy Church with all your fellow-blasphemers, lying in the devil’s cesspool, do you dare to say to her: “Be such as I am, so that you may be consumed by the disease by which I too have been consumed”? Did you think that we [**Note: [Col. 0780D]** Thus with the Vatican manuscript. The printed edition has “we could not.”] could be united with you, as though we did not retain what blessed Paul said: “We command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition which they received from us” (2 Thess. 3:6)?

What reasoning could have brought us, after abandoning the path that leads to the kingdoms of heaven, to take up yours, which hurls men headlong into Gehenna? You supposed that you could ensnare us by the subtlety by which the serpent ensnared Adam and Eve, composing an edict [**Note: [Col. 0780D]** Sulpicius Severus relates in Book II of his *Ecclesiastical History* that Valens and Ursacius, and the other Arians at the Council of Milan, fearing the people, who preserved the Catholic faith with extraordinary zeal, did not dare openly to profess their impieties, but assembled within the palace. “From there,” he says, “they issue a letter in the Emperor’s name, filled with every perversity, with the design, certainly, that if the people received it favorably, they might put forward the desired doctrines under public authority; but if it were received otherwise, all odium should fall upon the king and he himself should be pardoned, since as yet a catechumen he might reasonably seem not to have known the sacrament of the faith.” When the letter was read in church, the people rejected it. Lucifer refers in this place to this deed, and calls Constantius’s letter an “edict,” as in Book I *For St. Athanasius* and in *That One Must Die for the Son of God*, where he openly testifies that he opposed it in the palace. See what we have noted there. Just as Sulpicius affirms that this edict, or letter, was filled with every perversity, so Lucifer writes that it contained all the poisons of the Arian heresy. In notes appended to Sulpicius’s history, Jerome a Prato contends against Tillemont that Hilary also referred to this when he wrote in *On Synods*, no. 78: “Perverse men had gone so far that, though they themselves did not dare publicly to preach this—that is, the Arian doctrine—in the Church at Milan, they nevertheless deceived the Emperor into daring it. They deceived the ignorant king, occupied with wars, so that he might set forth the faith of such perfidy and impose a form of belief upon a Church which he had not yet entered through regeneration. They forced the opposing bishops into exile.” Earlier, the Maurist monks held the same view as Prato in the note attached to this testimony of Hilary.] in which all the poisons of your heresy are contained. But how could you have accomplished this [Col. 0781A] when blessed Paul had armed us against your poisons and those of your father, saying: “I say this, therefore, that no one may deceive you by loftiness of speech” (Col. 2:4)?

And again: “See that no one deceives [**Note: [Col. 0782C]** Ancient Version: “persuades.”] you through philosophy and empty seduction, according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ; for in him all the fullness of divinity dwells bodily” (ibid. 8). How could we be seduced, even by lofty words, by those sacrilegious Arian thoughts of yours, when we had recognized that your philosophy was empty? How could your words be sweet to us when we saw that you held the tradition of Arius rather than that of the blessed Apostles? To those Apostles he whom you deny to be the true Son of God said: “Go, baptize [**Note: [Col. 0782C]** Ancient Version: “Go therefore, teach all nations, baptizing them,” etc.] believers in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy [Col. 0781B] Spirit” (Matt. 28:19).

How could we Christians assent to you, a disciple of Arius, abandoning the apostolic tradition, when we find you saying that the Father is not a true father but is merely called father; that he does not have a true Son, but that the Son was made from nothing; and that the Holy Paraclete Spirit likewise consists of nothing? Whereas [**Note: [Col. 0782C]** “And whereas.” Latin.] we see that the Apostles believed in one God, the almighty Father, a true Father—true Father because he truly, not merely nominally, has a Son—and in his only Son Jesus Christ, that is, in the true Son of God, and in the Holy Paraclete Spirit, the true Spirit of God.

How could anyone holding such beliefs be supplanted by the devil through you, the founder of Arius’s blasphemy, when the apostolic faith [Col. 0781C] both confesses a perfect Trinity and acknowledges the one divinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, while the blasphemy of Arius—that is, yours—holds nothing except what pleases your dear devil? The difference between the faith of the blessed Church and your heresy is as great as that between light and darkness. Rightly, therefore, I said that you are separated from us as darkness is separated from light, because you are sons of darkness; and so you have vomited darkness from your viperish hearts.

You hoped to turn us aside from the path of truth, as though we did not know that the Holy Spirit had forewarned us through blessed Paul, saying: “Let no one defraud you, delighting [**Note: [Col. 0782C]** “in humility and the worship of angels, entering into what he has seen.” Ancient Version.] in humility of mind and in worship of angels, who appears to walk without cause, puffed up by the mind of his flesh and not holding the head [**Note: [Col. 0782C]** Ancient Version: “the head, Christ, from whom the whole body, joined together and supplied through its connections, grows and advances [Col. 0782D] into the increase of God.” This agrees more suitably with Lucifer’s version: *Ex hou pan to sōma dia tōn haphōn kai syndesmōn*, etc. (Ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων, etc.).] from whom the whole body, produced through connection and joining, grows into an increase of faith” (Col. 2:18). How could we follow you, walking without cause, nourished from the serpent’s mouth, swollen in the mind of your flesh by Arius, and made an apostate [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** Perhaps “apostate.”], when the apostolic command required that you be avoided?

You said that, desiring union for peace’s sake, you wished to join to us the pseudo-bishops of your sect. But how could we do this, so as to heed you, God’s enemy, rather than God himself? [Col. 0782B] We are not, like you, senseless enough to deny the Son of God, as do the Jews, participants in your blindness and leaders of your unbelief. Blessed Paul, showing the example of their rejection, says to the Hebrews (Heb. 3:5): “Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, speaking as a testimony to the things to be spoken [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** Ancient Version: “of things to be spoken.” Sabbatier so reads in Lucifer: “as a testimony to those things which were to be spoken.”], but Christ as a son over his house; whose house we are, if indeed we hold firm generosity [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** With Sabbatier one should read “liberty.” Ancient Version: “liberty and the rejoicing of hope firm unto the end,” etc.] and the rejoicing of hope. Therefore [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** “As he says.” The Ancient Version lacks, however, “as,” as does the Syriac Version.] the Holy Spirit says: ‘Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested me in trial and saw my works forty years. Therefore that generation was hateful to me, and I said, They always err in heart. But they did not know my ways; as I swore in [Col. 0782C] my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest. See, brethren, lest perhaps there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** With the Greek, *apistias en tō apostēnai apo theou zōntos* (ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος). Ancient Version: “of wickedness, to depart from the living God.”], but exhort yourselves daily while it is called [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** From the Greek, *kaleitai* (καλεῖται). Ancient Version: “called.”] today, lest any of you be hardened by the deceit of sin. For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold firm unto the end the beginning of our substance. While it is said, Today, if you hear my [**Note: [Col. 0782D]** “His.” Ancient Version.] voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation.’ For some, having heard, did not believe [**Note: [Col. 0783C]** “Having heard, they provoked [him].” The same version.], though not all who came out of Egypt through Moses. And with whom was he displeased forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses lay in the wilderness? [**Note: [Col. 0783C]** “With whom, moreover, was he displeased forty years? … whose bones fell,” etc. The same version. The Greek of Valesius in Sabbatier has *ptōmata* (πτώματα), “corpses,” as does Lucifer.] And to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, except the disobedient? [**Note: [Col. 0783C]** Greek: *ei mē tois apeithēsasin* (εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἀπειθήσασι), with Lucifer: “except the disobedient.” Ancient Version: “except the stubborn.”] And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief. Let us therefore fear lest perhaps [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** Greek: *mē pote* (μὴ ποτε). “Perhaps” is omitted in the Ancient Version.] any of you, having neglected the command to enter [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** Ancient Version: “may seem to have neglected to enter into his rest.”], may seem unable to enter into his rest. For the good news was announced to us as it was to them; but the word heard did not benefit them, not [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** With the Greek, *ho logos mē synkekramenos*, “the word not mixed.” In Latin, however, one should read with Sabbatier from the Ancient Version, “mixed,” referring to the word. Most manuscripts cited by him have *mē synkekramenous*, “not mixed.” Moreover, the Ancient Version has *faith* for *of faith*, which Lucifer has with the Greek, *tē pistei* (τῇ πίστει).] mixed with the faith of those who heard. For we shall enter [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** Ancient Version: “For we who believe enter into rest.”] into his rest who have believed, as he said: “As I swore in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.” And though the works were made from the foundation of the world, he nevertheless said somewhere concerning the seventh day: “Thus [Col. 0783B] God rested on the seventh day from all his works.” And again in this [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** The same version: “And again in this: And,” etc.; but the Greek agrees with Lucifer: *kai en toutō palin; ei* (καὶ ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν· εἰ), “and again in this: If.”]: “They shall not enter into my rest.” Therefore, since it remains [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** The same version: “It remains for the rest … it was foretold.” Lucifer from the Greek: *kai hoi proteron euangelisthentes* (καὶ οἱ πρότερον εὐαγγελισθέντες), “and those formerly evangelized.”] for the rest to enter into it, and those to whom it was first preached did not enter because of disobedience, he again appoints another day, saying in David, after so long a time, as was said before: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.” For if Joshua had given them [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** *Autous* (Αὐτούς) in the Greek. Ancient Version: “them.”] rest, he would not afterward have spoken of [**Note: [Col. 0783D]** Sabbatier reads “another [day].” Greek: *peri allēs* (περὶ ἄλλης), as in our edition. Ancient Version: “of another,” which, joined after the words “a later day,” has a meaning different from Lucifer’s.] another day. Therefore a rest remains for the people of God. For he who entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his” (Heb. 4:1).

Who is so foolish that, after reading and receiving these things from the blessed Apostle, he would abandon the apostolic faith and attempt to embrace heresy? Who would dare deny him whom he sees able to grant eternal rest to [Col. 0783C] those who believe in him [**Note: [Col. 0784C]** “In him.” Latin.], and wish to believe in one with whom he would begin to be punished eternally? Who is such a one unless you are, Emperor Constantius, who have abandoned the Lord’s camp and crossed over to the devil’s house?

We did not choose to burn, as you chose to burn with your lover the devil; rather, we hasten to enter eternal rest. How could we, through your cunning, be caught and turned aside from the way of truth [**Note: [Col. 0784C]** Tilius: “which with your …”; Latin: “how.” Yet from either reading an interrogative sense can be formed: “How could [we], with your cunning,” etc.], when the Apostle still urges us to seize eternal rest, saying: “Let us therefore hasten to enter into that rest, lest any fall by the same [Col. 0784A] example of disobedience [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** Sabbatier reads “in the same example.” Our edition agrees with Greek, *en tō autō paradeigmati* (ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ παραδείγματι), and with the Ancient Version, which has “lest anyone … fall away from the truth.”]. For the word of God is living and powerful, sharper than every [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** Greek: *hyper pasan machairan distomon* (ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον). Ancient Version: “sharper than every sword, and a searcher of soul and of the thoughts of the heart.”] sharpest sword, and penetrating even to the division of soul and spirit, joints and marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart. No creature is hidden before him, but all things are naked and laid open to his eyes, to whom we must give account [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** As in the Greek, *pros hon hēmin ho logos* (πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος). Ancient Version: “before whom is our prayer.” Sabbatier reads “prayer” also in Lucifer.]” (ibid. 2).

Since these things are so, how could any of us pass over to you who remain in the perfidy of the Jews? What order of things could join us Christians to you Arians, when we saw that you were imitators [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** “Imitators.” Latin and Tilius.] of the perfidy of that nation? How could those fleeing to the house of God emerge from it? [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** Perhaps: “when, in,” etc.] For in the Acts of the Apostles the most blessed Peter spoke thus: “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus [Col. 0784B] Christ for the remission of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For this promise is for you [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** With Cyprian, Epistle 73. Ancient Version: “for the promise is for you.” Greek: *hē epangelia* (ἡ ἐπαγγελία).] and your children, and for all who are far off, as many as the Lord your God [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** “Our.” Latin, with the Ancient Version and Vulgate.] calls.” With many other words he testified [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** Greek: *diemartyreto kai parekalei* (διεμαρτύρετο καὶ παρεκάλει). Many manuscripts cited by Sabbatier add *autous*. Ancient Version: “he testified and exhorted, saying, Save yourselves,” etc.] and exhorted them, saying: “Save yourselves from this crooked generation” (Acts 2:38).

Nor can you say that you Arians are not a crooked generation, as the Jews were and are, when you see that the scribes, Pharisees, and rulers of the Jews were called a crooked generation precisely because they denied the Son of God and persecuted all who believed in his divine majesty. You cannot, I say, maintain that you and all Arians are not a crooked and perverse generation, when you do what they did. If they denied the only Son of God, [Col. 0784C] so do you; if they persecuted the servants of his eternal mercy, you too persecute them.

What, then, ought we to have done but withdraw from you sacrilegious persons in accordance with the command of blessed Peter? For how could we agree with you, when the Lord said in the Gospel: “Take heed [**Note: [Col. 0784D]** Greek: *prosechete* (προσέχετε). Ancient Version: “beware … which is hypocrisy.” Lucifer agrees with Tertullian, Book IV *Against Marcion*.] of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy” (Luke 12:1)? How could we be one body, when blessed Paul, writing to the Corinthians, said: “It is altogether reported among you that there is fornication, and such fornication as is not even among the Gentiles: that one should have his father’s [Col. 0785A] wife. And you are puffed up and did not rather mourn, so that he who did this deed might be removed from among you” (1 Cor. 5:1)?

If, therefore, the Apostle commanded that one doing such a deed be removed from among them, lest the whole Church plainly be corrupted through fellowship with him, how much more fitting was it that we should flee you blasphemers? If he says that that man was delivered to Satan, how much more ought you to know that you have already been delivered over when you began to deny the Son of God? “For I indeed, though absent in body, yet present [**Note: [Col. 0785D]** With the Greek, *parōn de tō pneumati* (παρὼν δὲ τῷ πνεύματι). Ancient Version: “spirit.”] in spirit, have already judged, as though present, him who has so acted: in the name of the Lord Jesus, when you and my spirit are assembled with the power of our Lord Jesus, to deliver such a man [**Note: [Col. 0785D]** With Tertullian in *On Modesty*. The word “man” is absent from the Ancient Version, which also reads “on the day of the Lord Jesus.” Lucifer agrees with the Greek in many manuscripts cited by Sabbatier: *en tē hēmera tou kyriou hēmōn* (ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν).] to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. Your boasting is good [**Note: [Col. 0785D]** Ancient Version: “is not good.” Augustine, Book III *Against the Letter of Parmenianus*: it is spoken by way of reproach. “Your boasting is good” is the reading of some manuscripts, especially Latin ones.]. [Col. 0785B] Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump? Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new dough, as you are unleavened” (ibid. 3).

Since this is the Apostle’s rebuke, could Christians be joined to the servants of Antichrist? For how could one not have been corrupted by the poisons of your enormous blasphemy, since whoever communicates with you, whether hypocritically or sincerely, is in great danger? Since we were separated from you because of your heresy, how could we again have adhered to you? For the Apostle says: “I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with fornicators—not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, for then you would have had to leave the world. But now I have written to you not to associate, if anyone called a brother [**Note: [Col. 0785D]** With Greek, *ean tis onomazomenos* (ἐάν τις ὀνομαζόμενος). Ancient Version: “is called.”] is a fornicator [**Note: [Col. 0786D]** “Or a fornicator.” Latin from Greek, *ē* (ἤ).], or covetous, or an idol [Col. 0785C] worshiper, or reviler, or drunkard, or extortioner; with such a one do not even eat” (ibid. 9).

If we are commanded not even to eat with you, did you think Catholics could meet with heretics to celebrate all solemn rites? Could worshipers of God be with you wanderers, with you whom the devil’s poison has led into every drunkenness? How could it happen that we living should stand among the dead? Rather, it was fitting that you, sons of our adversary, should be seen gathered in one body, and we, Christ’s soldiers, gathered in another; so that you might without any doubt be called by all who love God the limbs and body of the harlot. We too could be called by that name if we gave ourselves up to you: “Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them [Col. 0785D] members of a harlot? Far be it. Or do you not know that he who joins himself to a harlot is one body with her? For, he says, ‘the two shall become one flesh.’ But he who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit. Flee fornication” (ibid. 6:15).

What sort of fornication do you wish us to flee? Whoever seeks another woman besides his wife is called a fornicator. Likewise, whoever serves idols is called a fornicator, because he abandons God and worships idols. Similarly, the heretic is called a fornicator. Consider which of these is the graver crime: to become a heretic, to serve idols, or to commit adultery according to the flesh. Since, therefore, either the Gentiles or you heretics are called idolaters [**Note: [Col. 0786D]** For “idolaters”; the populace thus corrupts foreign nouns. Tilius and Latin.], both parties necessarily practise idolatry; and yet you will understand, beyond all expression, [**Note: [Col. 0786D]** Perhaps *a* should be removed. The Latin is correct.] how much more vast those two crimes are than carnal fornication. [**Note: [Col. 0786D]** “You will understand that those two crimes are more vast, behold,” etc. The sense is clearer if “you will understand” is retained thus: “Yet, compared with carnal fornication … you will understand how much greater those two crimes are; behold,” etc.] See the evils by which you have slain yourself.

The most holy Apostle still cries out: “Every sin that a man commits is outside the body, but he who fornicates sins against [Col. 0786B] his own body” (ibid. 18). And: “You are not your own; for you were bought with a price. Glorify and [**Note: [Col. 0786D]** With the Greek in certain manuscripts: *kai bastasate ton Theon* (καὶ βαστάσατε τὸν Θεόν), “and bear God.” Ancient Version: “glorify God in your body.”] bear the Lord in your body” (ibid. 19). How can you bear God in your body, Constantius, when by rejecting the apostolic faith and accepting heresy you declare that you are not his, though our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs, declared themselves his?

Further, if the fornicator sins against his own body, how much more do you, who accomplish that work of the serpent not only through the flesh but through the soul itself? “Do you not know that he who joins himself to a harlot is one body, but he who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit?” (ibid. 16). Lest we too, becoming members of the harlot’s body with sacrilegious persons, should fail to deserve to be servants of the Lord but become, like you, [Col. 0786C] slaves of the devil, we judged that we must withdraw from you. Woe to you, who refused to be joined to the Lord and chose to be joined to the devil.

And when he says, “Do not be deceived: evil conversations corrupt good morals” (ibid. 15:33), what does he command me to do except flee your assembly, stained with sacrilege, lest by clinging to you I too perish with you? How could we have remained in your malign council, when we find that the blessed Apostle said to Timothy: “Lay hands hastily on no one, and do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure” (1 Tim. 5:22)? But how could we be pure if, by adhering to you, we were, like you, torn away from the purity of faith by those your dearest friends—the unclean spirits? How would we not share in others’ sins? If we had judged that we must remain with you, [Col. 0786D] we would become what you are: members of the harlot.

How could we Christians have existed with you heretics, when we knew that the Apostle had likewise written to Timothy, commanding us to withdraw ourselves [Col. 0787A] from you heretics: “Teach and exhort these things. If anyone teaches otherwise and does not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the doctrine which accords with godliness, he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but sick concerning disputes and strifes of words, from which arise envy, contention, blasphemies, evil suspicions [**Note: [Col. 0787D]** Ancient Version: “evil suspicions, wranglings,” etc.], evil wranglings of people corrupted in mind and deprived of the truth” (1 Tim. 6:2).

Therefore we chose to live separated from you, who do not believe as the people of God believe; from you, who do not teach as the Apostles of Christ, the only Son of God, taught; from you, who do not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ; from you, the assailant of the doctrine that accords with godliness; from you, puffed up against us through our enemy; from you, knowing nothing true [Col. 0787B] but sick concerning disputes; from you, through whose wicked efforts verbal quarrels, deadly contentions, and malign wranglings are found especially to have arisen in our own days; from you, that is, a man corrupted in mind and a falsifier of truth. We judged that we must withdraw from you and your viperish companions according to the Apostle’s command.
