“And the rest of the deeds of Manasseh, and all that he did, and how he caused Israel to sin—are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And he shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem mouth upon mouth [Note: [Col. 0811D] “Mouth upon mouth,” Latin, and correctly.], besides the sin by which [Note: [Col. 0811D] Sabat. has *that* for *which*, and below “twenty-two” for “twenty-two years.”] he caused Judah to sin, in doing what was evil before the Lord God. And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and his son Amos reigned in his place when he was twenty-two years old” (ibid. XXI.1).

What do you say to these things, Constantius? I think you will now cease to say: “Unless I acted well, I would not reign for so long,” when you see another Manasseh—yourself—doing such things and reigning fifty-seven years. And since we have said that you are another Manasseh, see that you possess all his qualities. He established idolatry in God’s house; you did the same in the temple and dwelling-place of the Lord. He made idols be worshipped and usurped for himself what was called the Lord’s, so that he might henceforth be called a worshipper of idols. You too have done all this, because you introduced the Arian heresy into the Church and ordered that your blasphemy be accepted as though it were the catholic faith, while the faith written at Nicaea—which we know to be apostolic and evangelical—be rejected.

Just as you have now desired these things to be done, so Manasseh commanded service to all idols and departure from God. Therefore it will not be surprising if you have claimed for yourself the buildings in which [Note: [Col. 0811D] For “in which,” or “among which,” Til. “into which,” Latin.] we are accustomed to assemble God’s people, and have called yourself, an idolater, “catholic,” when you see that Manasseh did what you now have done. Thus the Lord will spare you, who follow Manasseh’s way, as he spared Manasseh; and he will spare you for as long as he spared him, so that it may be written that Manasseh slept with his fathers, was buried in Jerusalem, and that his son received the kingdom in his place.

Do you read that he perished in war, or that he was overcome by some illness? [Note: [Col. 0812D] Or, “by any illness,” Til.] By no means. Yet, I think, in your vaunted wisdom you say that all things happened to King Manasseh without punishment. Such are you, to think thus concerning Manasseh: because he reigned fifty-seven years, handed the kingdom down to his son, and himself died in peace, you suppose that such great crimes could have passed without punishment for him.

Do not pity yourself in such a way that you fail to turn yourself to God; do not correct your wicked deeds, and you will find yourself tormented with Manasseh, whom you see that you surpass in this: he shed the blood of the righteous only within the bounds of Jerusalem, whereas you have shed and are shedding it throughout the Roman Empire. “But,” you say, “he burned or consecrated his sons before the images of his gods.” If you had sons, you would undoubtedly have made them receive the same Arian blasphemy.

Do you not know that, just as in those days those who burned their sons pleased the devil—since they had one mind, to abandon the Creator and serve the creature—so now the devil asks nothing of you except that you deny the only Son of God? This is the sacrifice most acceptable to him: that you believe as Arius believed. In our times it is more to him that you deny God’s Son than if you wished to burn yourself in fires in honor of all demons. For he sees that the worship of idols has been despised by all, because it has proved a vain invention; now he desires through you, his heretical servants, to deceive us servants of God.

“How,” you ask, “to deceive?” As he has already deceived you, so he wishes us also to be deceived. Though you are an Arian, you pretend to be a Christian, until by the poison of your heresy you can wound the worms [Note: [Col. 0812D] The sense is obscure; perhaps: “until you can wound even the worms”; or “you worms,” for “the worm,” wound Christians, so that they cannot remain true Christians.] so that they may thereafter not be Christians as we are, but Arians as you are. This is the fattening offering of your services which is made through you to demons.

For who but the devil and his sons can say of the only Son of God: “He is Son, yet he is not the true Son; he is God, yet he is not the true God”? Therefore, when you say, “I am a Christian, but I do not believe that the true God has a true Son; I do not believe that the Father and the Son have one power”; when you call the Son a creature, made from nothing; when you say that he existed when he did not exist—you sacrifice to the devil better than Manasseh then did when he either consecrated his sons to all demons through fire or burned them.

I grieve for you, Emperor, because you possess such great folly and, though you commit such great evils, nevertheless deign to say: “Unless I acted well, I would not still be in the kingdom; God would already have extinguished me.” Do you not see that Manasseh, comparable to you in sacrilege and unbelief, held the kingdom in Judaea for fifty-seven years, as I have often said? He caused the people of the Lord to forsake [Note: [Col. 0812D] “To forsake God,” Vatican manuscript.] God and serve idols; he placed images in the temple of the Lord and in God’s dwelling-places; he made God’s house, the sanctuary of his majesty, a sanctuary of idols.

God likewise endures and bears with you until he proves his household, crowns the worthy, and—unless you correct yourself—punishes you with the unworthy in eternal punishment. But believe that he could extinguish both Manasseh then and you now in one atom [Note: [Col. 0812D] That is, in the twinkling of an eye, Til. and La Cerda.] of the eyes. Yet he spares you, not because he lacks the power, but because it is fitting that his worshippers, remaining unmoved against your cruelty, should be crowned, and that you, enemies of his mercy, if you decide to persist as you are, should be condemned to everlasting punishment.

Those who do not merely refuse to correct you when you err, but drive you on to perish, make you say: “Unless I acted well, I would never still rule.” No wonder: for it is written that both you and they will be such: “The sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and he who works iniquity shall be blessed. The sinner has provoked the Lord according to the multitude of his wrath; he shall not [Note: [Col. 0813C] Thus the Hebrew, Septuagint, and Vulgate. The ancient version omits *not*.] inquire: God is not before his eyes; his ways are defiled at every time; let his judgments be removed [Note: [Col. 0813C] Lucifer alone reads “let them be removed”; everywhere else, “they are removed.”] from before him” (Ps. IX.3; after 21).

Therefore, when you say: “We do well to remove those bishops who confess that they hold the faith written at Nicaea, and to appoint those who confess as Arius confessed,” then they [Note: [Col. 0813C] That is, the Catholic bishops.] rightly say: “You are indeed that sinner who is unjustly praised for the desires of your soul; you are the lawless man who, though abandoned by God because of your blasphemies, nevertheless, among your flatterers, is not reproved for whatever sin you commit, but is instead told that you act well.”

When you say: “I did well to send soldiers to Alexandria to remove Athanasius” [Note: [Col. 0813C] See the notes above.], they say with the fullest justice: “To whom can you be compared except to the man whom the Holy Spirit marks through the psalmist—one who, though he does wicked things and is most evil and abominable, nevertheless desires to be praised?”

You say: “Unless I acted well, God would not still have spared me” (Wisdom XIX.2); and I find it said to God: “Therefore you correct little by little those who have gone astray [Note: [Col. 0813C] *Exerrarint* is read in some parts, and Latinius corrects it likewise, following the Greek: Διὸ τοὺς παραπίπτοντας κατ᾽ ὀλίγον ἐλέγχεις, ‘Therefore you reprove little by little those who fall away.’ Where Nobilius found *partibus* in Lucifer, it is impossible to guess, since it appears neither in the Paris nor Lyons editions of the *Bibliotheca Patrum*.], and admonish those who sin by speaking to them, that, abandoning wickedness, they may believe in you, O Lord. You hated also those ancient inhabitants of your land because they performed works hateful to you through unlawful sorceries and rites [Note: [Col. 0813D] Septuagint: τελετάς, ‘rites.’], and, being merciless murderers of children, you wished to destroy them by the hands of our fathers, so that the land most dear to you of all might receive a worthy settlement by the children of God. Yet you spared even them as men, and sent wasps before the army, that they might destroy them little by little [Note: [Col. 0813D] Sabat. reads “in parts.”].

“Were you unable to attack and subject the ungodly to the righteous, or to destroy them all at once by savage beasts or by a harsh word? [Note: [Col. 0813D] Sabat., using the Lyons edition, reads ‘not because,’ as also in the Greek, omitting *because*; but the first Paris edition has ‘were you unable?’ and we retain this.] But, judging them little by little, you gave them room for repentance, although you knew that their nation was wicked and their malice natural, and that their thought could not be changed forever: for their seed was cursed from the beginning. Yet, fearing no one, you granted pardon for their sins. [Note: [Col. 0813D] We retain *some* with Sabat., although it appears to be a printer’s error and the Greek has τινά, ‘anyone.’ Nevertheless, under either word the sense remains.] For who shall say to you, ‘What have you done?’ Or who shall stand against your judgment?” [Col. 0814A] Likewise you too are spared, Constantius, so that you may repent, or perish by the example of those who, when known … [Note: The supplied source breaks off here, within an unfinished note.]

[Col. 0813D] That is, those whom God had known would by no means perform repentance for their sins. Til.]

…had been known by God not to be going to repent, not to be going to turn themselves to God; and for that reason their seed had been evil from the beginning; yet he spared them and did not punish them immediately when they sinned.

[Note: [Col. 0813D] “That the seed was.” Latin. Perhaps: “because they had been wicked from the beginning.” Til. and La Cerda. Lucifer is referring to the words copied a little above from the Book of Wisdom.]

Therefore do not say: “If I were not acting rightly, surely God would never have spared me,” when you see that your fellow-criminals have long been granted an opportunity for repentance, so that at last they might perceive the causes of their evil actions and make sufficient satisfaction to God for their sin.

You too, therefore, if you do not turn to God, will be one of that accursed race concerning which it is said to God:

[Note: [Col. 0814C] See this same testimony a little above, where there are some variant readings.]

“Not being ignorant that their nation is wicked, that their malice is innate, and that their purpose could not be changed for ever; for their seed was accursed from the beginning” (ibid. 10).

[Col. 0814B] How glorious, then, will you consider yourself when you have begun to be among such people, when you see yourself judged among such people, when, found among such people, you are sent into unquenchable flames? You will be first of all and greater even there in those punishments; for no one can be found your equal in wickedness except the devil alone, so that someone might be seen better than you amid those punishments.

Do you dare to say: “If I were not living rightly, if my deeds were not upright, if my faith—that is, the Arian faith—were not Catholic, if I had not rightly acted in removing those bishops who preach the faith set forth by more than three hundred at Nicaea, I would never have reigned for so long, nor would I have shone so greatly in my reign,

[Note: [Col. 0814C] For the Fathers of the Council of Nicaea numbered three hundred and eighteen.]

[Col. 0814C] that, though only for a short time, I ruled alone within the bounds of the Roman world.”

[Note: [Col. 0814C] Namely from the year 350, after the death of Constans.]

If it is as you say, why does Job, the most righteous worshipper of God, say to those who assailed his righteousness with false allegations: “Hear me,

[Note: [Col. 0814C–D] Ancient Version: “Hear my words . . . and my flesh is seized by pains: Why . . . are their houses abundant, [Col. 0814D] and fear nowhere . . . their cows conceive and do not miscarry, and their offspring is preserved and gives birth . . . like their ancient sheep; and their little children provoke one another to play. They hold psaltery and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the instrument; and they end their life in prosperity . . . Yet they say to the Lord: ‘Depart from us; we do not wish to know your ways’ . . . Indeed . . . pains shall hold them in wrath. And they shall be like chaff in the wind, and like dust carried away by a whirlwind . . . Let his eyes see his own destruction.”]

for the pains of my wound compel me to speak”—

[Note: [Col. 0814D] A Greek scholiast in Nobilius in some manner indicates the unusual sense of this passage in Lucifer’s version: “I shall speak with earnestness, and shall briefly call to mind the things that are about to be said”—“why do the wicked live,” etc. For Nobilius’s following interpretation does not seem relevant to the matter. Sabatier reads *cogunt loqui*, “compel [me] to speak,” omitting *me* and *quid*, “me” and “why.”]

“Why do the wicked live, and why are their houses not destroyed, and why is fear far from them? Their cow

[Note: [Col. 0814D] Greek: βόῦς, “ox/cow.” The Septuagint.]

never

[Col. 0815A] miscarries;

[Note: [Col. 0815C–D] Thus Symmachus: οὐκ ἐξέτρωσε, “did not miscarry,” for “has not suffered an abortion.” Til.]

she always carries her offspring to term. But they themselves remain like sheep for ever,

[Note: [Col. 0815D] With the Septuagint: Μένουσι δὲ ὡς πρόβατα αἰώνια, “but they remain as everlasting sheep.”]

and their children, taking up an instrument,

[Note: [Col. 0815D] Septuagint: Ἀναλαβόντες ψαλτήριον, “taking up a psaltery.” Aquila, with an asterisk prefixed in the Hexapla: ὀργάνου, “of an instrument.” Everything else is wholly peculiar to Lucifer.]

play in delight, spending their lives in prosperity, though the Lord says: ‘Depart from me, you wicked; I do not wish to know their ways.’ For the lamp of the wicked shall be extinguished, and they shall grieve with groaning in their life; they shall be like chaff carried away by the wind, or like dust whirled about by a storm; but let their eyes see death” (Job XXI, 6).

[Note: [Col. 0815D] For “they shall see.” Til., as in the Vulgate.]

Since I know that the Lord said these things of them, “Know

[Note: [Col. 0815D] Here Lucifer explains Job’s meaning in these words: “Hear me, for the pains of my wound compel me to speak.”]

that none of you can restrain me into silence.” Why does the most glorious Job say this, unless because he knew that very many indeed act wickedly, yet are not immediately given over to certain [punishments?],

[Note: [Col. 0815D] The passage is mutilated. Perhaps: “to certain punishments.” Latinius. But if *certis* is understood as “for certain [persons],” the sense will be complete.]

but are preserved for this purpose: either that they may correct themselves, or certainly that after death they may suffer the penalties of their sins; that they may learn what it was not to have sought

[Col. 0815B] the Lord, not to have served him while opportunity remained—believing in him alone and serving him, so as to win his favor.

Now, convicted by the testimony of so great a man, believe; cease to say that you acted justly when you removed the priests of the Lord, appointed men of the Arian faith, and commanded the preaching of the creed of Arian doctrine; when you proscribed and deported, inflicted tortures, and killed those who believed in the only Son of God. Cease, I say, to maintain that you live and flourish so greatly in your reign because you did and continue to do these things. For you hear the righteous man Job—whom God declared to have served him without complaint, whom he described as his true worshipper—say that, although very many act impiously, they nevertheless live most pleasantly in this life.

Deign also to receive what he says below

[Col. 0815C] concerning you wicked people, and understand how, although you act wickedly, you are for the present spared; and present yourself to God through repentance. “I did not know” (ibid. XXIII, 17) “that such darkness would come before my face.”

[Note: [Col. 0815D] Ancient Version: “Darkness would come upon me, and mist would cover my face.”]

“Why, then, O Lord, could I not remain hidden for one hour? But the wicked cross into the boundaries of others, seize flocks of sheep together with their shepherds, oppress the cattle of orphans, take a widow’s ox as a pledge, reap a field not their own before its time, compel people to work in their vineyards without payment, strip many people, take bread away from the hungry, and besiege many in narrow passes, and do not understand

[Col. 0816A] the way of righteousness. Let their portion upon the earth be accursed” (ibid. 18).

[Note: [Col. 0815D–0816D] Ancient Version: “The hours were not hidden from the Lord; but did the wicked not know his days? They transgressed the boundary; they carried off a flock with its shepherd and fed it. They drove away the orphan’s beast of burden . . . they reaped; the weak cultivated the vineyards of the wicked without wage and food. They made many naked . . . and [against] the hungry . . . in straits [Col. 0816D] they laid wicked snares; but they did not know the way of righteousness.”]

“What hope indeed is there for wicked people, or what access can they have with the Lord? But” (ibid. XXVII, 8), “even if they grow strong, they shall come to want; and those left of them shall die an evil death, and no one shall pity their widows; and if they gather gold or silver like mud, all these things the righteous shall possess” (ibid. 14).

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Ancient Version: “For what hope has the wicked man, because he waits and trusts in the Lord, if perhaps he is saved?”]

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Ancient Version: “And if they have become young men . . . those around him shall die by death . . . and if he has gathered silver like earth and prepared gold like mud . . . others shall obtain them.”]

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Sabatier reads “if they strengthen themselves,” and below “if they gather” in place of “if they have gathered.”]

Therefore, emperor, do not now deign wrongly to flatter yourself because, being such a man as we have affirmed you to be, you suppose that you—a murderer and sacrilegious man—continue very long in this life because your works are acceptable to God. Your works are like those of the persons against whom the Holy Spirit inveighs through the mouth of Isaiah, saying:

“Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel who delivered you: I am God; I showed you the way in which

[Col. 0816B] you should walk. And if you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have become like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea; your seed and the offspring of your womb would have become like the sand of the sea” (Isa. XLVIII, 17).

“But,” you say, “these things were said to the Jews.” Certainly—to those whose imitator you have made yourself. And now, as has often been said, change your evil ways; believe as the holy Church believes, and God will be gracious to you in all things. For he himself says: “Return to me with all your heart, together with fasting, weeping, and mourning; and tear your hearts, not your garments” (Joel II, 12).

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Ancient Version: “Turn . . . with fasting, in sackcloth . . . and rend,” etc. Sabatier also reads “rend” in Lucifer.]

Return to God with all your heart; submit to these health-giving remedies so that you may behold and recognize your crime. Open the eyes of your heart; groan with your whole heart as you realize how grievously you have sinned. Then he who says, “When you turn and groan, then

[Col. 0816C] you shall be saved, and you shall know where you had been,” will have mercy on you.

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Perhaps he repeats this from the sense of Joel’s words, since it has not been possible to find this text anywhere.]

Remember that the prophet consecrated to God said: “I do not will the death of one dying,

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Ancient Version: “of the sinner.” Cyprian alone, in *On the Lapsed*, agrees with Lucifer.]

says the Lord, so much as that he should return and live” (Ezek. XXXIII, 11).

[Note: [Col. 0816D] Latinius restores the sense here by inserting the word “hear.” With the Vatican manuscript, we retain the word “remember,” which was lacking in the edition.]

Do not now think, because your works are evil, that you act well merely because you have not immediately received punishment for your deeds. Rather, consider what is written: the Lord is patient so that you may repent. Do not say, “I have sinned; and what grievous thing has happened to me?” For the Most High is a patient requiter (Ecclus. V, 4).

Hear also the blessed Paul inviting you to God, revealing to you how he may be appeased toward you: namely, that he is patient for this reason, and that the deserts of your deeds are not immediately brought before you,

[Col. 0817A] because he wishes you at last to emerge from evil through repentance, through true satisfaction. “Do you despise

[Note: [Col. 0817B] Ancient Version: “Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, patience, and long-suffering, not knowing that his goodness . . . according to works?”]

the forbearance of his goodness and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? But through your hardness and unrepentant heart you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who will render to each according to his work” (Rom. II, 4).

Return, Constantius, to God. Take up the weapons of repentance against the brigandage of your inward enemy. Flee the ruinous praise of flatterers, who have not deigned to tell you what they ought. Remember that the Lord said through the mouth of Isaiah: “Those who call you happy lead you into error and disturb the path of your feet” (Isa. III, 12).

[Note: [Col. 0817B] Ancient Version: “Those who call you blessed deceive you and throw the ways of your feet into confusion.”]

Believe in the only Son of God; receive pardon for your crimes. Repeat the saying of the psalmist:

[Col. 0817B] “Who will confess you among the dead?” (Ps. VI, 6).

[Note: [Col. 0817B] Ancient Version and Vulgate: “In hell.”]

And again: “Will dust make *exomologesis*—confession—to you?” (Ps. XXIX, 10).

[Note: [Col. 0817B] As in the Greek, μὴ ἐξομολογήσεταί σοι χοῦς, “Will dust not confess to you?” So too Cyprian, *Testimonies*, Book III. Ancient Version and Vulgate: “Will [dust] confess?”]

[Col. 0818A] Return to God; groan for your crimes. Hear, through Jeremiah, the voice of the Lord saying: “Will not one who falls rise again? Or will not one who turns away return?” (Jer. VIII, 4).

You fell on the day when you denied the Son of God; you will rise at the hour when you confess him. Since the wound of the enemy has settled upon you, give yourself over to be cured by medicine; apply the remedy to yourself. You wounded yourself by saying, “He is not the true Son of God.” You will in turn heal yourself if you say, as we say and believe, that he is the true Son of God.

“Return,” says Joel, “to the Lord your God, because he is merciful, compassionate, patient, abundant in mercy, and one who relents from the sentence of evil inflicted” (Joel II, 13).

[Note: [Col. 0818B] Ancient Version: “Turn . . . because he is merciful and compassionate, patient . . . repenting of evils.” Cyprian, Epistle 52, and Victor of Tunnuna agree with Lucifer.]

If you judge that this promised pardon for your *funera*—the disastrous deeds that brought such slaughter upon Christ’s Church—

[Note: [Col. 0818B] That is, the crimes that brought so great a slaughter upon Christ’s Church; Lucifer uses this word in the same sense above also, p. 41, line 24.]

is to be rejected by you, you will desire to obtain it there,

[Col. 0818B] where you will receive nothing except the torments of punishments.

[Column 0817]

**The Two Books of Our Holy Father Lucifer, Bishop of Cagliari, in Defence of Saint Athanasius, Addressed to the Emperor Constantius.** (C)

**Book One.**
[Col. 0817C] You compel us, Constantius, to condemn in his absence our fellow-bishop, the devout Athanasius; but the divine law forbids us to do this. By the wider authority of royal power you press the priests of the Lord to shed blood, unaware that you are attempting to remove from our minds the laws of justice divinely handed down to us. Can you maintain that it is divinely permitted for a man to be condemned when absent, unheard, and—what is greatest of all—innocent? For how do you suppose it divinely permitted that men should be punished unheard, when you see that Adam and Eve, the first parents of our race, were struck by God’s sentence only after being heard? And God called Adam and said to him: “Adam, where are you?” And he said: “I heard your voice, Lord, in paradise, and I was afraid because I am naked, and I hid myself.” [Col. 0817D] And God said to him: “Who told you that you are naked, unless you have eaten from the tree concerning which I commanded you not to eat from this tree alone?” [Col. 0818C] And Adam said: “The woman whom you gave me—she gave me from the tree, and I ate.” And God said to the woman: “What is this that you have done?” And the woman said: “The serpent persuaded me, and I ate” (Gen. 3:9).

[Note: Col. 0817D. Ancient Version: “And the Lord God called … and said to him: Where are you? And he said to him: I heard your voice walking … and I was afraid because … And he said to him: Who told … unless you ate from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat? … which you gave with me, she … and I ate. And the Lord God said … the serpent deceived me,” etc.]

Since, therefore, you observe that God has given such a model for judging, since from the sacred springs of the Scriptures you have gathered that God pronounced sentence only after those summoned from hiding had confessed, with what shamelessness have you prescribed for judging God’s servants [Note: “servants,” Vatican manuscript.] a procedure which could not have come from the law of the Lord? Nor did you fear that we might have said to God concerning you what was said [Col. 0818D] concerning that apostate angel: “The serpent persuaded me; [Col. 0819A] the Emperor Constantius deceived us; we believed him, thinking that he was a man.”

Could you not [Note: “Not,” Idacius.] see that you might be struck by such a sentence of the angered God as that by which the serpent too seems to have been struck? To it He says: “Because [Note: Col. 0819C. Ancient Version: “Because you have done this … cursed above all cattle and above all beasts … upon your breast … you shall walk … all your days. And I shall put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; she shall watch your head, and you shall watch her heel.”] you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and above all beasts of the earth which are upon the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall crawl, and you shall eat earth all the days of your life. And I shall put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed: he [Note: “The sense concerns Christ.” Tillemont.] shall watch your head, and you shall watch his heel” (ibid. 14).

Should you not have remembered, from this single sentence of the Lord, that you too could incur God’s wrath as that angel incurred it? Especially since you knew that your own deed was serpent-like. Or, because that serpent had been made from among angels, did you suppose that you, from among [Col. 0819B] men, could not become a serpent? Certainly not. But tell me, I ask, what difference there is between your deed and that of this apostate, fugitive angel. If he deceived inexperienced people by a lie, so did you—and indeed people not inexperienced; if, for the sake of advantage, he enticed their minds to eat the fruit of the tree, so have you, under the pretext of peace [Note: Col. 0819C. “On account of the edict of peace issued by the Arian Constantius under the pretext of peace with his younger brother Constans, who was Catholic, as will be seen later.” Tillemont. “But this is not the sense of the passage. Lucifer wrote these books after the Council of Milan of 355, at which, because he had refused to subscribe to the condemnation of Athanasius in his absence, he was driven into exile with other Catholic bishops, perhaps to Cappadocia, the first place of exile. In the year 349, however, Athanasius had already been restored to the Alexandrian Church by Constantius, who had allowed himself to be brought to this by fear of Constans. Thus, when Lucifer says that Constantius contrived that Athanasius should be condemned by Catholic bishops for the sake of peace, he means that the Emperor proposed Athanasius’s condemnation as a pretext for pacifying the Church.”] allied yourself with them. And since you have said that you undertook this deed for the good of all Christians, then, once your deeds have been examined [Note: Col. 0819D. This is an absolute ablative in Greek fashion, which he uses for a plural: “when your deeds have been examined”; he uses it frequently, both in nominative and accusative cases. Tillemont.], it is understood that you have imitated that serpent: desiring men to become transgressors of God’s commands, you gave orders that an absent man be condemned unheard, and that a hearing be denied to one who proclaims that he can clear himself of the charge laid against him [Note: Col. 0820C. “To one proclaiming.” Vatican manuscript. “What we call one appealing. This participle occurs elsewhere in the author in the active voice: ‘If it is a just judgment for one proclaiming himself to be heard,’ that is, one appealing from the unjust sentence of the judge which Constantius had perversely issued against Athanasius.” Tillemont.].

Abel the righteous is murdered, and Cain, when questioned, receives [Note: Col. 0820C. “He says ‘receives sentence’ for ‘is condemned.’ Thus he receives sentence, that is, is condemned by the Lord, who gives us a model for judging only after we have heard and carefully questioned. As He said to the serpent: ‘Because you have done this, cursed above all cattle of the earth,’ etc.” Tillemont and La Cerda.] sentence; and do you wish the Lord’s priest to be punished unheard? [Col. 0819C] “Abel,” he says, “became a shepherd of sheep, but Cain was a worker [Note: Col. 0820D. Ancient Version: “He worked.”] of the earth. And after some days Cain offered to the Lord a sacrifice from the fruit of the earth, and Abel too offered from the firstborn of his sheep. And God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts; but upon Cain and his sacrifices He did not look. And Cain was greatly grieved, [Col. 0820A] and his countenance fell. And the Lord God said to Cain: ‘Why have you become sad, and why has your countenance fallen? Why [Note: Col. 0820D. “This rendering of this verse is wholly peculiar to Lucifer alone. No trace of it could be found in Greek or Latin Bibles, nor among the Fathers or interpreters. Ancient Version: ‘If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned? Be still,’ etc.”] did you not offer rightly? You sinned; be still.’ And below: ‘Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go into the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him. And God said to Cain: Where is your brother? And he said: I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper? And God said: What is this that you have done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the earth’” (ibid. 8).

Could God not have punished Cain before summoning and questioning him? But He did not wish to do so, giving a model for the manner in which we should begin judging those committed to our charge—those of whom, I say, through the prophet Jeremiah, He says to peoples consecrated to His majesty: “And [Col. 0820B] I shall give you shepherds according to my heart, and they shall feed you, feeding you with discipline.” “Condemn,” you say [Note: Col. 0820D. “You say,” Vatican manuscript.], “one whom you do not know to have sinned” (Jer. 3:15). Why? Clearly so that we might no longer deserve to be called bishops, but madmen and executioners. Do you not fear, I ask, while giving such orders, the voice of the Lord speaking to most holy Noah? “Like the green herbs [Note: Col. 0820D. Ancient Version: “of fodder.”] I gave you all things, except [Note: Col. 0820D. “But flesh in the blood of its life.” The same. The Greek lacks “its,” as does Lucifer.] flesh and the blood of life you shall not eat. For I shall require your blood, the blood of your lives, from the hands of every beast; [Note: Col. 0820D. Ancient Version: “And from the hand of a man’s brother I shall require it,” etc.] I shall require the life of a man. Whoever sheds the blood of a man, for the blood of that man his blood shall be shed [Note: Col. 0820D. Ancient Version: “His life shall be shed.” “His life” is absent from the Greek, as from Lucifer.], because I made man in the image of God” (Gen. 9:3).

Do you not fear, I ask, who see yourself to have become the killer of so many servants of God, that you still slaughter innocent persons and compel us to become partners [Col. 0820C] in your murders? When Moses’ father-in-law Jethro said to him that he kept the whole people waiting throughout the day, he replied: “The people come to me seeking [Note: Col. 0820D. Ancient Version: “to inquire.”] judgment from God” (Exod. 18:15). Therefore, if the judgment of bishops ought so fittingly to be just because it is said to be decided by God’s judgment, how could you command us to condemn an unheard man [Col. 0821A] when you find Moses saying: “The people come to me seeking judgment from the Lord” [Note: Col. 0821C. Above: “from God.”] (ibid.)? If the people gather to us for this reason, that they may be judged according to God’s law, why do you say, “Condemn the innocent man”? Therefore, since this command which you have issued does not come from the law of God but is plainly established by the will of the devil, at last understand who you are.

Lot’s wife was turned into salt because she could not fulfil what had been commanded. But, I suppose, through your intervention—because, forsooth, you are emperor of the Roman Empire—no evil would happen to us if we condemned one burdened with false charges. In Exodus, sacred Scripture says: “Moses went up to the mountain of God, and God called him from the mountain, saying: ‘Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob and announce to the children of Israel: You yourselves have seen how great were the things [Col. 0821B] I did to the Egyptians, and I took you up as upon eagles’ wings and brought you to myself. And now, if in hearing you hear my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be to me a people surpassing all nations. The whole earth is mine. But you shall be to me a most sacred kingdom [Note: Col. 0821C. Greek: ἱεράτευμα, “priesthood.” Ancient Version: “most holy.”], and a holy nation’” (Exod. 19:3).

How shall we be a holy nation if we become killers of innocent people? How a kingdom most sacred to God, if we pass over His commands? Again God says: “You shall not commit adultery; you shall not kill; you shall not bear false witness against your neighbour” (Exod. 20:13). You say the contrary: “Believe me when I utter falsehoods, and slaughter the innocent man.” In Exodus God warns: “You shall not believe an idle report; you shall not join with the wicked to become an unjust witness. You shall not be with the many [Note: Col. 0821C. Sabatier reads “with the greater number,” as in the Ancient Version.] in evil. You shall not [Col. 0821C] join [Note: Col. 0821C. Ancient Version: “You shall not join the multitude in turning aside with the many … and you shall not spare the poor man,” etc.] with the many in turning aside with the crowd, so that you turn aside [Note: Col. 0821D. Thus the Ancient Version; the Septuagint has ὥστε ἐκκλῖσαι, “so as to turn aside.” But Cotelerius, vol. 1 of *Monuments of the Greek Church*, notes, p. 5, that Lucifer’s version agrees with the Complutensian Greek: ὥστε ἐκκλίναι.] judgment, and you shall not pity the poor in his judgment” (Exod. 23:1). And below: “You shall not overthrow the judgment of the poor in his case; you shall depart from every unjust word; you shall not kill the innocent and righteous; you shall not justify the ungodly for gifts, for gifts blind the eyes of those who see and corrupt [Note: Col. 0821D. Septuagint: λυμαίνεται, “ruins.” Lucifer seems to have read λοιμαίνεται, from λοιμός, “pestilence.” Cotelerius, ibid.] righteous words” (ibid. 6).

To exclude these commands, you compel God’s servants to overthrow his judgment, even attempting to corrupt by gifts our just conscience consecrated [Col. 0822A] to God. God says: “If in hearing you hear my voice and do all that I tell you, I shall be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those opposed to you” (ibid. 22). It is now for you to prove that God commanded innocent persons to be struck down, apostolic faith to be abandoned, and your own unbelief to be embraced [Note: Col. 0821D. “Some believe that when Lucifer calls Constantius’s unbelief, blasphemy, and idolatry, he means the letter, full of perversity and falsehood, which he proposed for subscription to the Catholic bishops gathered in the Church of Milan for the council held in 355. This is more probable; concerning this—or rather the edict proposed to them by Constantius, as Lucifer himself calls it below—see the notes on the book *On Not Associating with Heretics*. In a simpler sense, however, understand the Arian heresy, which he almost everywhere designates by these names. Jerome a Prato, in the *Diatribe on the Deeds of Liberius*, §10, prefixed to the Works of St Damasus, thinks that the word ‘idolatry’ alludes to the Ariminian formula of faith; others, to the Arian Sirmian formula. But since Lucifer chiefly has in view the proceedings of the Council of Milan, I think he indicates neither in these books; for both were published after that council, although Lucifer wrote the books for Athanasius after the councils of Rimini and Sirmium.”].

Why did you think that these things, which oppose the Lord’s commands, ought to be commanded? You remember that in Leviticus the Lord said to Moses: “Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: I am the Lord your God. You shall not act according to the practices of the land of Egypt, in which you lived; nor shall you act according to the practices of the land of the Canaanites, into which I shall bring you; nor shall you walk in their statutes. You shall perform my judgments and keep my commandments, and walk in them. I am the Lord your God. [Col. 0822B] Keep all my commandments and all my judgments, and do them. The man who does them shall live by them. I am the Lord your God” (Lev. 18:2).

If you can show it written in the Lord’s commands [Note: Col. 0822D. “That it is just for the righteous to be punished at the instigation of the unrighteous,” Vatican manuscript.] that righteous persons are to be punished at the prompting of the unrighteous, you may rightly consider that you have acted, and are acting, rightly in all things. Show it written in God’s commands that His worshippers, assailed by calumnies, ought to be put to death by us bishops at the command of you, the persecutor of His household. Why have you been led by your Coarians to carry out this wickedness? What reason compelled you, an emperor, to assail God’s man with false accusations? Had you not read that God said in Leviticus: “Do not [Note: Col. 0822D. “These words seem drawn from two verses, at least, of the same chapter; but the earlier words could nowhere be found, even by Sabatier, who consequently placed both under verse 11. The earlier differ from the Ancient Version, which he gives here from Augustine; the latter nearly agree.”] assail by falsehood, nor shall any one of you slander his neighbour” (Lev. 19:11)? And below: “You shall not lie nor bring calumny against your neighbour, and you shall not profane the name [Col. 0822C] of the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God. You shall not harm your neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God [Note: Col. 0822D. Sabatier omits “your.”]. I am the Lord your God. You shall not commit [Note: Col. 0822D. Sabatier reads “you shall commit,” from the Lyons edition in the *Library of the Holy Fathers*; Greek: ποιήσετε, “you shall do,” as in the Paris edition.] injustice in judgment. You shall not show favour to the person of the poor, nor be awed by the person of the powerful; in justice you shall judge your neighbour. You shall not walk deceitfully among your people. You shall not consent to the blood of your neighbour. I am the Lord your God. You shall not hate [Note: Col. 0822D. “Instead of ‘you shall not pursue or hold your brother in hatred.’” Tillemont and La Cerda.] your brother in your mind [Note: Col. 0822D. Ancient Version: “You shall not hold … in hatred in your soul; rebuking, you shall rebuke.”]; you shall surely rebuke your neighbour, and you shall love your neighbour as yourself. I am the Lord [Col. 0823A] your God. Keep my law” (ibid. 12).

Though you remember these things written, do you think we shall be acceptors of your person? You asked for the death of an innocent man, and when you saw yourself despised, you stretched yourself toward the infliction of every kind of punishment. God says: “Do not fear the face [Note: Col. 0823D. Ancient Version: “You shall rise before the face of an elder and honour the person,” etc. Greek πρόσωπον, “face/person,” as in Lucifer. Yet I suspect that the preceding words, ‘Do not fear the face of a rich man,’ have been repeated from verse 15 of the same chapter, ‘nor be awed by the person of the powerful,’ because they belong to the sense.] of the rich man; and you shall honour the face of the elder and fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God” (ibid. 32). And did you suppose that you could be feared, and Athanasius dishonoured, when God commanded that he be honoured?

Had you not read God’s saying: “You shall not act unjustly in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in balances; you shall weigh with a just balance” (ibid. 35), yet you determined that an absent man should be killed by us? If it is a just judgment for one proclaiming himself to be heard [Note: Col. 0823D. “Not ‘to be heard.’ Latin text, rightly.”] to be punished while absent, then yours will be just accusations before God against us, who have rejected the commands of your rashness. In Deuteronomy the glorious Moses is found saying to the judges whom he had given to the people: “Hear matters between your brothers, and judge justly between a man and his brother and his proselyte. You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall judge the lesser as well as the greater. You shall not accept [Note: Col. 0823D. Sabatier omits “accept.”] the person of a man, for judgment belongs to God” (Deut. 1:16).

And you wish, Constantius, I suppose, because you dwell in royal exaltation, that your person should be accepted. You are very eager for us, priests of the Lord, to slaughter the man whose blood you thirst for. For this reason, then, we are detestable in your eyes: because we pronounce judgment according to God’s will. For this reason you thought your executioner’s hand should be stretched out [Col. 0823C] to the sword, as though you could conquer by the sword those whom you saw neither hesitate, for the Son of God, to lose their present life nor dread death.

Most holy Moses recounts to the children of Israel at God’s command: “See, the Lord your God has delivered the land before your face. Go up and possess it, as the Lord God [Note: Col. 0823D. “God” is omitted by Sabatier but is read in Greek.] of our fathers said to us. Do not fear or be dismayed” (ibid. 21). If they, who bore an image of our calling, were commanded to fear no one but God, how much more fitting is it that we fear no one but God, who seek to gain not the lands of Canaanites, Jebusites, Gergesites, and Amorites, but heavenly kingdoms and God’s everlasting love? How could the empty force of your [Col. 0823D] rank bend, or be able to bend, us away from this purpose, since we have determined to fear no one but God?

We are not Christians of those who said: [Col. 0824A] “Because the Lord hated us, he brought us out from the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites and destroy us” (ibid. 27). Rather, we are among those who said, and say, to God: “For your sake [Note: Col. 0824D. Ancient Version: “we are put to death.”] we are killed all day long; we are reckoned as sheep for slaughter. But in all these things we overcome through him who loved us” (Rom. 8:36).

We did not fear, and do not fear, your threats, we who know that nothing can resist God, lest we perish like those who hear Moses say: “Your brothers turned away your heart, saying: ‘The nation is great and [Note: Col. 0824D. “Instead of ‘very hard and rough,’ after his and the Greeks’ custom, who very frequently use adjectives of this kind adverbially; or a comma should be placed before *multa*, so that it reads: ‘a nation great and hard, very [great] and stronger.’ Tillemont and La Cerda, rightly; for the Greek has ἔθνος μέγα, καὶ πολύ, etc.] very strong, stronger than you; its cities are great and walled up to heaven, and we saw there also sons of giants’” (Deut. 1:28).

We Christians do not fear your sword, for we confidently expect, once you enemies of God’s religion have been overthrown, to come to the banquet of patriarchs, [Col. 0824B] prophets, apostles, and martyrs. We soldiers of God do not fear the strength of your perishing kingdom. We are not among those children of unbelief who judged their enemies able to do more than God, so as to fear your fragile power. For if the Jews had not believed that the Canaanites, Jebusites, Amorites, and other enemies could do more than God, Moses would certainly never have added [Note: Col. 0824D. “That is, Moses would never have added these words to them, nor continued his discourse to them.” Tillemont.] these words: “Do not speak, nor be dismayed by them. The Lord your God, who goes before your face, will himself fight them together with you, according to all the things that he did for you in the land of Egypt and in this wilderness which you see: how the Lord your God cherished you, as a man might cherish his son, throughout all the way that you travelled [Note: Col. 0824D. Sabatier reads “travelled,” and below “that you might travel in it.”] until [Col. 0824C] you came to this place, leading you by fire at night, showing you the way in which you might walk, and by cloud in the day” (ibid. 29).

If after these saving warnings the children of Israel had not believed those against whom they were waging war to be more powerful than God, they would certainly never have come to utter destruction. Therefore we know that God is able to deliver us from your hands as we press on toward the heavenly kingdom promised us. We cannot fear your cruelty, especially since we have chosen to be punished by you rather than by God.

You said: “Condemn Athanasius.” Whom, Constantius, were we to condemn? Him whom we see confessing the Son of God, as patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs confessed him? Or you, who deny him, as your master Arius denied him, as Judas Iscariot [Col. 0824D] and all the Jews denied him? God says to Moses: “You shall have no other gods besides me. You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any [Note: Col. 0824D. Sabatier reads “of all”; the Greek is παντός, “of every.”] likeness of those things which are in [Col. 0825A] heaven above, and of those which are on earth below, and of whatever things are in the waters beneath the earth. You shall not worship them nor serve them, for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of fathers upon children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy to thousands who love me and keep my commandments” (Deut. 5:7).

And you say that these divine commands must be trampled under foot: “Embrace my idolatry; abandon God; kill Athanasius, my enemy, not God’s, so that you may be found among those who hate God, to whom He promised that He would repay unto the third and fourth generation. Take pains not to be loved by God with those of whom He says: ‘Showing mercy to [Note: Col. 0825D. A little earlier he said “to thousands”; here, according to the Greek, εἰς χιλιάδας, “unto thousands.”] thousands who love me and keep my commandments’” (ibid. 10).

You see, most prudent emperor, that what seems good to you is evil, and what is evil, good. Or will you deny that good is good, or deny that you understand evils to be good? If you deny that evils are good, answer: Is it good or evil to condemn the innocent? Is it good or evil to abandon God and follow idolatry? If you say it is evil, we shall say to you: Why do you do these things?

Again Moses cries out in Deuteronomy: “Keep [Note: Col. 0825D. For “keep”; infinitive used as an imperative. Tillemont. Sabatier reads “keep”; Greek has φυλάξῃ, though I think this is an error in our Paris edition.] the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies and ordinances, whatever he commanded you; and do what is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, that it may go well with you, and that you may enter and inherit the good land which the Lord swore to your fathers” (Deut. 6:17). And you chose these things as good and pleasing to God: that idolatry should be established through the force of your kingdom, in insult to His majesty, [Col. 0825C] and that those who have confessed themselves His worshippers should be slaughtered.

“Behold,” Moses says, “I have set before you today blessing and curse: blessing, if you hear the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you today” (Deut. 11:26). Therefore, since those are blessed who do not punish the innocent, and those keep the Lord’s commands who refuse to condemn a man unheard, how do you think yourself blessed when by your deed you prove yourself to stand among the cursed? Or, if you are not among the cursed, why do you despise Moses saying: “If there is found in one of your cities, which the Lord your God gives you, a man or woman who has done evil before the Lord your God, transgressing [Note: Col. 0825D. “Transgressing the covenant.” Latin, closer to the Greek: παρελθεῖν τὴν διαθήκην.] his covenant, and they have gone [Col. 0825D] and served foreign gods and worshipped them, either the sun or the moon or everything that is in the heaven of the world” (Deut. 17:2)? And below: “You shall bring out that man or woman, and stone them with stones, and they shall die. On the testimony of two witnesses or three he shall die; one who is to die shall not die on the testimony of one witness. The hands of the witnesses shall first be upon him to kill him, and afterward the hands of all [Col. 0826A] the people; and you shall remove the evil from among yourselves” (ibid. 5).

If you are not, Constantius, running with the cursed, why did you not obey the commands of God’s servant Moses? Why, when he says that even an idolater must perish upon two or three witnesses, did you not wish a hearing to be granted even to a man consecrated to God? Why did you cause a hearing to be denied to him to whom you have been delivered by God—to him, I say, whom, if you resist while he defends what is just, you are commanded by the mouth of Moses to die the death?

For, in order that the judgments of the priest may remain inviolate, he says thus: “Rising up, you shall go up to whatever place [Note: Col. 0825D. Sabatier: “wherever.”] the Lord your God chooses for his name to be invoked there; and you shall speak [Note: Col. 0826D. “You shall come.” Latin from Greek ἐλεύσῃ.] to the priests, Levites, or to the judge who shall be in those days. And after inquiring, they shall tell you the judgment; and you shall do according to every command which they tell you, [Col. 0826B] who are in that place where the Lord your God chose for his name to be invoked. Take great care: you shall do according to all that they have determined [Note: Col. 0826D. Sabatier has “shall determine.”] for you. According to the law and according to the judgment which they declare, you shall do. You shall not turn aside from the word which they tell you; you shall do whatever they indicate to you, turning aside neither right nor left. And whatever man acts presumptuously, refusing to hear the priests who stand ministering in the name of the Lord God, or the judge who shall be in those days, that man shall die; and you shall remove evil from Israel. And all the people, hearing, shall fear and shall no longer act impiously” (ibid. 8).

But you say: “In this passage Moses, wholly devoted to God, makes mention of priests just as he does of a judge.” Prove that you were made judge over us; prove that you were appointed emperor for this purpose: to bring us by your weapons to fulfil every will of your friend the devil. Since you cannot prove that it was commanded to you—not only not to lord it over bishops, but also to obey their decrees so fully that, if you attempt to overthrow their decisions and are caught in presumption, you are commanded to die—how can you say that you are able to judge bishops, when, if you do not obey them, you have already, so far as God is concerned, incurred the penalty of death?

Since this is so, why, you who are profane, do you assume this authority over the priest of God among God’s household? God even allowed the Jewish judges themselves, when they remained in God’s law, to be drawn from their own people. For Moses says: “If you say, ‘I shall set over myself a ruler [Note: Col. 0826D. Ancient Version: “rulers,” with the Greek Alexandrian manuscript. Lucifer agrees with the Oxford manuscript and Aldine and Complutensian editions: ἄρχοντα, ‘a ruler.’ Besides, certain other readings vary in this text.], like all the other nations around [Col. 0826D] me,’ you shall surely appoint over yourself the ruler whom the Lord your God chooses; you shall appoint him from among your brothers. You shall not be able to appoint over yourself a foreigner, because he is not your brother” (ibid. 14).

And it follows why He did not wish a foreigner to become ruler: namely, lest he draw others to his own sect. Therefore He says: “Lest [Note: Col. 0826D. Sabatier omits this testimony; it is nevertheless in the Greek Septuagint, differing little from Lucifer’s version: μὴ ἀποστρέψῃ τὸν λαὸν εἰς Αἴγυπτον, “lest he turn the people back to Egypt.”] he bring us back to Egypt” [Col. 0827A] (ibid. 16), that is, to the worship of idols. As though He said: “Who are you, I ask, who have usurped this authority which God did not hand over to you? And even if He had handed it over and allowed it to be in [Note: Col. 0827D. That is, in your possession, power, and discretion; at your disposal. It is a harsh and exceedingly uncouth expression, which he uses very often. Tillemont. “In you,” Latin.] your hands, first you would have had to be a Christian, because it would be a crime for a foreigner to judge God’s servants, for an enemy of religion to judge God’s household.”

Then, if you had been a Christian and God had judged you worthy to share with priests in governing [Note: Col. 0827D. “Ruling,” Latin. That is, governing and directing His people; here he uses *gerere*, “to carry on,” for “to govern and direct.” Or perhaps *regendum*, “to rule,” should be restored, having been altered through a scribe’s error. Tillemont and La Cerda.] His people, hear what kind of person He commanded you to be in Deuteronomy: “And when he sits in his rule, let him write [Note: Col. 0827D. Sabatier: “He shall write … and shall read it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God … above his brothers,” almost entirely as in Greek.] this in a book before the priests and Levites; and it shall be with him, and you shall read it all the days of his life, that they may learn to fear the Lord your God, to keep all these commandments and perform these ordinances, so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers and he may not transgress [Col. 0827B] the commandments to the right or left, in order that he and his sons with him may endure long in his rule among the children of Israel” (ibid. 18).

What do you possess of this kind, except everything contrary to it, except everything that attacks God’s household? First, you are a heretic; then, a persecutor of God’s household. You have attempted, and are attempting, to slaughter Athanasius—as though you did not remember that it is written: “If a man hates his neighbour and lies in wait for him [Note: Col. 0827D. “For him.” Tillemont and La Cerda.], and rises against him and strikes him deliberately, and he dies, and the killer flees to one of these cities, the elders of that city shall send and take him from there and deliver him into the hands of those seeking blood, and he shall die. Your eye shall not spare him, and you shall cleanse innocent blood from among them, and it shall be well with you” (Deut. 19:11).

And again: “One witness [Note: Col. 0828D. “Witness” is absent in Sabatier, but Greek has μάρτυς εἷς, ‘one witness.’] shall not stand [Col. 0827C] in testimony against a man concerning any iniquity or any sin that he has committed. Every word shall stand on the mouth of two or three witnesses. But if an unjust witness stands against a man, accusing him of iniquity, the two men between whom the dispute is shall stand before the Lord and before the priest and in the presence of whatever judge shall be in those days. The judges shall inquire carefully; and behold, if the unjust witness has given false testimony, bringing an accusation against his brother, you shall do to him as he wickedly intended to do to his brother, and you shall remove [Note: Col. 0828D. Sabatier reads “you shall remove,” plural. Greek is ἐξαρεῖς, “you shall remove,” as in our edition.] evil from among yourselves. And the rest, hearing, shall fear and no longer add to doing this evil thing among you. Your eyes shall not spare him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot” (ibid. [Col. 0827D] 15).

When you see these things done, say that God has determined them concerning you, murderer. I ask: what else is it to say, “Condemn him whom you know to be innocent; act against God’s commands,” except: “Tear out your hearts; take away your own [Col. 0828A] reason; slaughter your own souls of your own accord. Though you see that it is a pit, pretend to be blind; hurl yourselves headlong into the eternal abyss; plunge yourselves into that pit from which you see that you cannot be rescued; take life away from yourselves; receive everlasting death”? What else is it to say, “Do what God forbade to be done,” except: “Be enemies of God; acquire the devil as your friend; take care that you do not attain paradise, or indeed the kingdom of heaven which God promised you if you keep His commands. Love the underworld; cherish the burning lake; desire to be with all those who are forever paying punishments; desire…”
—to be called men of the devil. Such are the rewards which your distinguished counsels procure: these are those excellent things which bring forth everlasting death, things which plunge a man already near heaven down to hell. [Note: [Col. 0828D] “May plunge.” Vatican manuscript.] Did you not yet know that it was written, that you should urge us to commit these evils?

“There shall not be in your bag one weight and another weight, a greater and a smaller; there shall not be in your house one measure and another measure, a greater and a smaller. You shall have a true and just weight, and a true and just measure, that you may live many days and that it may go well with you upon the land which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance; for everyone who does these things, everyone who acts unjustly, is an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deut. 25:13). [Note: [Col. 0828D] “As an inheritance,” in Sabatier.]

Since the sacred writings declare that one who does not keep sound weights and just measures is abominable, I suppose you thought that we should then be most acceptable if we pronounced an unjust judgment against him. Moses says: “Cursed is he who removes the boundaries of his neighbour.” We are forbidden to tear up and transfer a neighbour’s boundaries from one place to another; [Col. 0828C] yet you say: “Depart, priests of God, from the boundaries of justice” (Deut. 27:17).

The Holy Spirit says through the mouth of Moses: “Cursed is everyone who perverts the judgment due to the stranger, the orphan, and the widow”; while you, making sport with our blood, said: “Punish the man whom you do not know to have sinned” (ibid., 19). We did not wish, Constantius, to be cursed with you; rather, we desire that you may be found blessed with us in the holy Church. We do not heed your voice, which urges us to incur God’s displeasure; but we heed the voice of Moses, the servant of the Lord, saying:

“And it shall be, if you do not hear the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all his commandments which I command you today, that all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you. Cursed shall you be in the city, cursed in the field; cursed your storehouses and what remains to you; cursed the children of your womb, the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep; cursed shall you be in your going out. The Lord shall send upon you weariness and *thlipsen* [affliction], and distress in everything to which you put your hand, whatever you do, until he swiftly destroys you because of the wickedness of your undertakings” (Deut. 28:15).

[Note: [Col. 0828D] “You hear … your God,” in Sabatier, and “that you may keep and do.” The Greek in the Alexandrian and Oxford manuscripts is φυλάσσειν καὶ ποιεῖν, “to keep and do.”]

[Note: [Col. 0828D] *Thlipsen*, “affliction,” from the Greek θλῖψις. From this it is readily understood that they commonly spoke in this way and often used Greek; for on the island where Lucifer resided [Col. 0829D], the Greek idiom was in use. La Cerda.]

If falsely bringing accusations, persecuting worshippers of God, introducing idolatry into God’s Church, and slaughtering by military force believers in God’s only Son are not wicked undertakings, then perhaps these curses will not come upon and overtake you and those who run with you.

You summoned us to slaughter God’s priest, to kill the man through whom God had decreed that you should hear his commands.

“Moses wrote the words of this law in a book and gave it to the priests and Levites, who carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to the elders of Israel. And Moses commanded them on that day, saying: After seven years, at the time of the year of release, on the feast day of Tabernacles, when all Israel assembles to appear before the Lord your God [Col. 0829B] in the place which he shall choose, you shall read this law before Israel in their hearing, assembling in the church the men and women, children, and the proselyte who is in your cities, that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, and hear in order to do all the words of this law; and their children who do not know shall hear and learn the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land” (Deut. 31:9).

[Note: [Col. 0829D] “To the elders.” Vatican manuscript and Sabatier.]

[Note: [Col. 0829D] Thus the Greek; Sabatier has “proselytes.”]

You persecute the man through whom the Lord commanded you to hear; while he is still active in human affairs, you send your fellow-heretic George as his successor. [Note: [Col. 0829D] “And fellow-apostate”; and in similar expressions observe a compound formed from Greek and Latin, showing that this little book was written in the common manner of speaking. Tillemont.]

[Note: [Col. 0829D] George the Cappadocian was forced by Emperor Constantius upon the Church of Alexandria in A.D. 356, after Athanasius had been expelled, during Lent, as Athanasius testifies in his *Apology for His Flight*. Nazianzen calls him “the monstrous Cappadocian” in his oration in praise of Athanasius, where he describes his wicked life.]

Although Athanasius had already been delivered from the body, you had no right to appoint one; rather, the man whom God had deigned to establish as bishop for his people was and is in God’s hand—namely, through his servants, that is, the Catholic bishops.

[Note: [Col. 0829D] “And from the body” is omitted by Latinus. Yet these words seem to be retained, so that the reading should be *e corpore*, “from the body,” and the sense is: “although Athanasius, released from the body, had already obtained,” etc.]

For the power of the Holy Spirit for governing God’s people could not be fulfilled except in him whom God had chosen and upon whom hands had been laid by Catholic bishops, just as, after Moses’ death, we find his successor Joshua son of Nun filled with the Holy Spirit. Holy Scripture says:

“Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of understanding, for Moses had laid his hand upon him. And the children of Israel heard him and did as the Lord commanded Moses” (Deut. 34:9).

[Note: [Col. 0829D] He says *allegisset* for *elegisset*, “had chosen,” or “had called,” or “had been attracted by him.” Here is recognized the form of the institution of true bishops: a ruler has no right to appoint bishops, and there is the laying on of hands. Tillemont.]

You see that you have opposed God’s ordination and, by acting against God’s will, have slaughtered yourself with the point of your own sword. For no one could lawfully be ordained unless Athanasius were dead; and after Athanasius’ death, [Col. 0830A] a Catholic bishop ought to have been ordained by Catholic bishops.

Holy Scripture says that God spoke to Joshua son of Nun:

“Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, cross the Jordan—you and all this people—to the land which I give them. Every place upon which you have set the sole of your foot I will give to you, as I said to Moses: from the wilderness and Lebanon as far as the river Euphrates, [Note: [Col. 0830D] “The great river Euphrates.” Vatican manuscript, with the Greek: ἕως τοῦ ποταμοῦ μεγάλου, etc.] and as far as the great sea toward the setting of the sun, shall be the boundaries of your territory. No man shall stand against you all the days of your life; and as I was with Moses, so I shall be with you, and I shall not forsake you or despise you” (Josh. 1:2).

[Note: [Col. 0830D] Sabatier reads “your feet.”]

Can God be with his enemy George? Can he be favourable to one whom he has not ordained, whom he has not chosen? George is such as Arius was, and such as Valens and Ursacius are, or as the Adoxius to whom you sent me among the people of Germanicia. [Note: [Col. 0830D] The most famous adherents of the Arian party: Valens, bishop of Mursa, and Ursacius, bishop of Singidunum.]

[Note: [Col. 0830D] This is Eudoxius, an Arian, bishop of Germanicia, where Lucifer lived in exile for some time by Constantius’ command. He calls him “Adoxius” by antiphrasis, that is, “inglorious.”]

For thorns can produce nothing but thorns. You may ascertain that this is so from the acts of George himself, by reading the remonstrances of the Alexandrians. [Note: [Col. 0830D] Namely, the letters of the citizens of Alexandria to Constantius, in which they complained bitterly of George’s crimes. See Baronius under the year 356.]

And although it pleases you that he should be a wicked blasphemer—for he could not otherwise be most dear to you except because he is wicked—yet I have set these matters forth so that you may behold your own remarkable work. [Note: [Col. 0830D] That is, your eminent and notable deeds and works. Tillemont.]

Since, then, you know that God is not with George, but is with Athanasius, whom he established as bishop for his people, you can finally recognize that you have attempted to destroy God’s ordination and that you have persecuted God in Athanasius. For you hear God saying to Moses’ successor: “As I was with Moses, so I shall be [Col. 0830C] with you, and I shall not forsake you or despise you” (ibid., 5).

See also another passage:

“Be strong and act manfully, keeping and doing as Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to right or left, that you may understand in all that you do. Let not this book of the law depart from your mouth; meditate upon it by day and night, that you may keep and do all that is written in it. Then I shall direct your ways, and then you shall understand. See, I have commanded you: be strong and act manfully. There is no need for you to be dismayed or afraid, for the Lord your God is with you in every place” (ibid., 7).

[Note: [Col. 0830D] For “keep and do,” an infinitive is used for an imperative, after the manner of the Greeks, whose expressions he follows entirely in such matters. Tillemont. Thus the Greek: φυλάσσεσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν, though Sabatier reads “keep and do.”]

It remains for you to prove whether what you or George are doing comes from God’s commands. You hear God promise [Col. 0831A] that he will be with Moses’ successor, as he was with Moses, provided that he keeps what is written in the book of the law. If, therefore, you do not find it written that you should do these things, fairness itself will at last require you to see that God is not with you Arians, but that the one who dwelt in Cain dwells in you.

What cause, Constantius, drove you to these actions, so that, carried to such arrogance by the power of your rule, you decreed to kill the man whom God had chosen for himself in priestly honour? Had you not found written in the first book of Kingdoms:

“Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the strong man glory in his strength, nor the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: to know and understand God, and to do judgment and justice in the midst of the earth” (Jer. 9:23).

[Note: [Col. 0831C] The ancients called these books “Kingdoms,” not “Kings,” as may be seen in Tertullian, Cyprian, Augustine, and other ancient writers. Tillemont and La Cerda.]

[Note: [Col. 0831C] This testimony is read in the Vulgate at Jeremiah 9:23, but it is also found at 1 Kingdoms 2:10 in the Septuagint; Lucifer therefore was not at all mistaken in memory, as Latinius claims. The Old Latin version from the manuscript codex of Saint-Germain differs somewhat from Lucifer’s wording: it has, “The wise man in his wisdom, and not … to understand and know the Lord.” But the Greek in Theodoret has ὁ σοφὸς ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ αὐτοῦ, “the wise man in his wisdom,” as Lucifer does, and he agrees with Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book 3. Sabatier adduces Lucifer’s version at Jeremiah 9:23, reading verse 23, “and let not the strong man glory in his strength,” etc., as Lucifer himself does within book 2 *For Saint Athanasius*; but at verse 24 the Old Latin version he gives from Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book 3, differs from Lucifer: “To understand and know that I am the Lord, who exercise mercy, judgment, and justice upon the earth.”]

Why, passing these words by—when you ought always to have rendered just judgment—did you compel us also to commit injustice with you? You had decreed that a Catholic should be deposed by us and a heretic confirmed. [Note: [Col. 0831D] After George had violently occupied the Alexandrian see, Constantius seems to have endeavoured to make the Catholic bishops approve his act. Lucifer, together with the others, resisted; therefore, we infer, he was punished with a harsher exile and handed over to Eudoxius, bishop of Germanicia and a most bitter enemy of Catholics. Thus he underwent a second exile in that city.]

But when could persons of sound mind have done such a thing? If Eli the priest, because he had appointed unworthy sons to priestly honour, heard and suffered what he did from the Lord, what would we deserve to hear and suffer if, condemning a Catholic bishop—and indeed one absent and unheard—we allowed the Arian George to become bishop of the Alexandrians?

“And a man of God came,” it says, “and said: ‘Thus says the Lord: I plainly revealed myself to the house of your father, from all the tribes of Israel, to be priests for me, to go up to my sacrifice, burn incense, and bear the ephod. And I gave to the house of your father all the grain-offerings of the children of Israel for food. Why then have you looked upon my incense and my sacrifice with an evil eye, and honoured your sons more than me, to bless them from the first in all the sacrifices of Israel before [Col. 0832A] me? Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: I said that your house and your father’s house should walk before me for ever; but now it shall not be so. Thus says the Lord: Far be it from me; it shall not be so from me. For those who honour me I will honour, and he who despises me shall be brought to nothing. Behold, days are coming, and I shall destroy your seed and the seed of your father’s house; and there shall not be an old man in my house all your days. I shall destroy a man from my sanctuary, that his eyes may fail and his soul waste away; and all the surviving multitude of your house shall fall by the sword of men. And this shall be the sign to you which shall come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: both shall die by the sword of men on one day’” (1 Kingdoms 2:27).

[Note: [Col. 0831D] Old Latin: “To Eli … I was openly revealed to the house of your father while they were servants in the land of Egypt, in Pharaoh’s house. And I chose the house of your father from all [Col. 0832C] tribes of Israel to serve me in the priesthood … at my altar … and to bear,” etc. But from Jerome’s letter to Marcella, Lucifer’s version must certainly be supplied so as to yield this sense: “And I chose the house of your father from all the tribes of Israel for my priesthood,” etc. “Tribes” is from the Greek in another translator of the Hexapla: ἐκ πασῶν τῶν φυλῶν.]

[Note: [Col. 0832C] Old Latin: “to the house … all the things which are fire-offerings of the children … And why … upon my sacrifice, insolently … and you glorified … above me, to bless the first-fruits of every sacrifice in Israel before me?” But the Hebrew has “you honoured,” as does Lucifer; and in Greek the preposition *in* is absent before “Israel,” which Lucifer also preserves.]

[Note: [Col. 0832C] Old Latin: “Lord God … they shall pass … and [Col. 0832D] now says the Lord: By no means; but those who glorify me I shall glorify, and he who despises me shall be despised.” In Greek, “by no means” is with Lucifer, as is διελεύσεται, “shall pass.”]

[Note: [Col. 0832D] “Shall walk before” for “shall walk,” as he says *deleam* for *delebo*. Tillemont and La Cerda.]

[Note: [Col. 0832D] Old Latin: “I shall exterminate … and the seed of your father’s house … old man … And I shall exterminate for you a man from my altar … and he may waste away … and everyone remaining of your house … in one day,” etc. Greek πρεσβύτης, “old man,” and ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ, “in one day,” as in Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0832D] “I shall destroy for you.” Vatican manuscript, as in Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0832D] *Gladio virorum*, “by the sword of men,” is omitted by Latinus; these words are also absent from the Greek and Latin Bibles.]

If he received this rebuke from God because of his sons, what would we deserve [Col. 0832B] to receive because of you, Constantius? I suppose it would have been said to us: “You have honoured Constantius more than me,” just as it was said to him that he had honoured his sons more than God. “In what respect?” you ask. Because, if we had done your commands, we would have been found to have despised the Lord’s; because George is, as Eli’s sons were, a son of pestilence, whom you judged that we should set in the place of Athanasius, the man of God.

Then, when God says, “He who honours me shall be honoured, and he who despises me shall be brought to nothing” (ibid., 30), would we have honoured God if we obeyed your sacrilegious voice, uttered against his own divine commands? Or rather if, judging you to be nothing, we endeavoured to obey only his sacred ordinances? Meanwhile rejoice, because you dishonour God. For you hear him himself say that all who despise him will come to nothing.

Will you deny that you dishonoured the Lord by removing from their congregations the priests whom he ordained? Will you deny that you dishonoured the Lord when, against his decrees, you compelled [Col. 0833A] his priests to condemn a man absent and unheard, who had indeed been attacked by you and your agents with false accusations? Did you not dishonour God when you set aside apostolic and evangelical tradition and established to be maintained by human worshippers of God the idolatry which the devil built in Arius’s heart? [Note: [Col. 0833D] Either: “which the devil built in Arius’s heart”; or, “the devil established in [Arius’s] heart”; or, “which Arius built in his heart, you devil,” etc. Latinus.]

Since this is so, it will now be for your prudence to judge what it is expedient for you to do: whether, correcting your errors here and obtaining pardon for such great crimes, you should determine to be found among God’s household; or whether, brought to nothing—as the Lord promises those who despise him—you should begin to pay for ever the penalties paid by those whose paths you have chosen to follow.

And so that you may clearly see what dangers await you because you dishonour the Godhead, hear also what is said to Samuel concerning Eli’s sons:

“The Lord said to Samuel: ‘Behold, I am doing my words in Israel; everyone who hears them, both his ears shall ring. On that day I shall raise up against Eli all that I spoke concerning his house, and I shall accomplish what I foretold to him; for I shall take vengeance upon his house for ever because of the iniquity of his sons, which I know: because his sons, despising the Lord, spoke evil things, and he neither warned nor chastised them. And now I have thus sworn to the house of Eli: the iniquity of Eli’s house shall never be propitiated by incense or sacrifice’” (1 Kingdoms 3:11).

If these things were promised to Eli because of his sons’ transgression, what is promised to you because of your sacrilege? If these were promised to him for eternity, what of you, who do such great things? If God said that Eli’s sons spoke evil of him, how much more [Col. 0833C] will he say this of you, who have embraced Arius’s blasphemy in order to attack the faith which the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and all the martyrs held?

We ask you, amid these actions, to repent of your deeds, considering at least what befell Eli’s sons for dishonouring God.
