Hilary also indicates this in these words from *On the Synods*: “Now, as heresy breaks forth under the profession of public authority, what it formerly muttered only here and there, it now gloried in victoriously, no longer in secret.” And Sulpicius Severus, *History*, book 2: “The Arians concealed their unbelief; not daring openly to proclaim the doctrine of their error, they behaved as Catholics.”] of prostitutes, who at first practise harlotry secretly, but afterwards become so shameless and lose the honour of chastity so completely that they wish to practise harlotry openly?

How have you loosed every bond of iniquity, when against blessed Athanasius you still retain, after so many years, the fury you once conceived, so that you desire his [Col. 0879A] blood to be shed? How have you released the crushed into rest, when you do not cease in various ways to torture [Note: [Col. 0879D] He employs the gerund *torquendo* (“by torturing”) in place of the infinitive *torquere* (“to torture”), as above *ferendo* in place of *ferre*. Tillemont and La Cerda.] the servants of God? And how have you released [Note: [Col. 0879D] Vatican manuscript: “you have brought down the crushed.”] the crushed into rest, when you see that prisons, [Note: [Col. 0879D] The Latin has “prisons, mines,” etc. See what we shall note on this matter in book 2.] mines, and exiles can scarcely now contain the number of Christians condemned by you? Even if you broke your bread for the hungry, how could the Lord find it acceptable, when you have devoted his servants to death by starvation, unto his eternity? If you brought the homeless needy into your house, how could God deign to look upon your work, when he sees the servants of his glory cast out of private homes and thereby made exiles because they would not accept your idolatry established through Arius? If you clothed the naked, how could you please God, when you have taken away his servants’ property and said: “If you condemn the apostolic faith [Col. 0879B] and accept the Arian faith, you shall receive back all that is yours”?

Certainly, among all these sacred commands of the Lord, you may find [Note: [Col. 0879D] “You may be found,” in the Vatican manuscript and Galandius.] one which you fulfil: namely, that you do not despise those of your own seed. You do not despise, indeed, your viper-brood Arians, born, that is, of your shameless [Note: [Col. 0879D] *Impuderatus*, “shameless,” is used for *impudens*, such as the Devil, father of all heretics. Tillemont and La Cerda. Poncius, among the editors of the Lyons *Bibliotheca Patrum*, printed *inviperato* (“made into a viper”), as Tillemont had interpreted it, and rendered it *impudente*; but this does not seem acceptable. Lucifer frequently uses unusual words. See Du Cange, *Glossarium*, s.v. *impuderatus*. Galandius.] father, the devil. You love your brothers [Note: [Col. 0879D] Lucifer recalls how greatly the Arians, especially their bishops, enjoyed Constantius’s favour and authority. They managed everything at their own discretion, enriched with Catholic property and possessing the more distinguished churches. Hilary perhaps refers to this in his sole book *Against Constantius*, reproaching the emperor in these words: “You bestow bishoprics on your own men.” Athanasius testifies, in his *Letter to the Solitaries*, that bishops of fifty sees were sent with a military escort to unwilling peoples.] because you see them nearer to you. You love these men with singular affection; to them you grant all the glory of your kingdom; you have them as associates and partners in destroying God’s inheritance within your realm. You have made them rich; you have exalted them above all who are set in high station—those, that is, who have thought fit to mingle themselves with your darkness.

Since you do these things which God hates, how do you think that you can be heard by God? Or, if you perform almsgiving, could it there be accepted, [Col. 0879C] when you hear him say: “Then your morning light shall arise, and your health shall quickly spring up; righteousness shall go before you, and the majesty of God shall surround you. Then you shall cry, and God shall hear you. While you are still [Note: [Col. 0880D] The same Lucifer has “and while you are still” a little below.] speaking, he will say to you: ‘Behold, I am here’” (ibid., v. 8)? Do you suppose that you can obtain any of these things, when no morning light has risen for you, but inextricable darkness has besieged your mind and the gloom of errors has enveloped you [Note: [Col. 0880D] The Latin reads *caligine*, “with gloom,” but Galandius rightly does not depart from the printed text.]? What health has arisen for you, when you are placed in every wound of death, when every day you bring increase to your wounds, when you labour to extinguish yourself utterly?

For us, indeed, health comes from no other source than, in the first place, believing as the patriarchs, [Col. 0880A] prophets, apostles, and martyrs believed. How can righteousness go before you, when you persist wholly in unrighteousness, when you are the cesspool of Arian doctrine, when you are a shedder of Christian blood? How can God’s majesty surround you, when you assault that very majesty which you have forsaken in judging it right to accept the idolatry of Arian doctrine? How then will you cry out and God hear you? While you are still speaking, will he say to you, “I am here,” when you deny God the Father, deny his only Son, deny the holy Paraclete Spirit? How can he either hear you or say to you, “Behold, I am here,” when, so far as lies in your power, you overturn his religion, remove his Catholic bishops, and appoint heretics? How will he hear you, whom you considered fit to be trampled upon in every way, [Col. 0880B] unless you repent of your evil deeds, unless, abandoning your wicked ways, you embrace the righteous path of the holy Church? Then indeed you will be able to obtain these promises of God.

For it is written concerning those who turn themselves wholly in heart to God: “Thus says the Most High, who dwells on high [Note: [Col. 0880D] The Ancient Version and Sabatier punctuate thus: “And dwelling on high for ever; Holy in the holy places is his name; exalted in the holy places,” etc. The Ancient Version continues: “Giving patience and life to those contrite in heart . . . . I shall take vengeance upon you, nor shall I always be angry with you.” Sabatier reads *animaequitatem* (“equanimity of soul”).] for ever, holy among the holy ones; his name is the Lord Most High, resting among the holy ones and giving equanimity to the soul, and giving vengeance to those afflicted in heart. I shall not be angry with you for ever, nor shall I always exact vengeance from you” (ibid. 57:15). But to whom does he say this? Plainly, to those who have turned back by satisfaction in order to blot out their sins.

Hence also: “This is not the fast I have chosen,” says the Lord, “but loose every bond of iniquity; loose the obligations of oppressive contracts; release the crushed into remission, [Col. 0880C] and tear up every unrighteous written bond. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring into your house the poor who have no roof. If you see one naked, clothe him, and you shall not despise those of your own seed. Then your morning light shall arise, and your health shall quickly spring up; righteousness shall go before you, and the majesty of God shall surround you. Then you shall cry, and God shall hear you; and while you are still speaking, he will say to you: ‘Behold, I am here’” (ibid. 58:6).

God will be with you if first you believe in him, and then turn yourself to these deeds which he also says below must be performed: “If you remove [Note: [Col. 0880D] The Ancient Version: “If you remove . . . . . the binding, and the command.”] from yourself the bond of iniquity and obligation, and the word of murmuring; and if from your heart you give your bread to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then light shall rise for you in darkness, and your darkness shall be as noonday. And God [Col. 0881A] shall be with you always; you shall be filled as your soul desires, and all your bones shall grow fat; and they shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring whose water has not failed” (ibid., v. 9). [Note: [Col. 0881B] From the Greek ἐξέλιπεν, “has failed.” The Ancient Version has *deficiet*, “will fail”; Sabatier, *deficit*, “fails.” Certain other minor readings in this text vary in the Ancient Version.]

As has already been said, you will be able to obtain these things if you turn to the Church, if you avoid your fellow Arians, if you deign to hate that assembly of evil men which is yours. Then God will always be with you; then light will rise for you in darkness; then your darkness will be as noonday; then your course will be directed in good things. But if you remain in this obstinacy, in this cruelty by which you torment his servants, God will not be with you, but he who is found even today in your Arian gathering: namely, the devil. For the things you deign to do are not God’s works but the devil’s.

If it is God’s work for you to proscribe [Col. 0882A] those who either have not condemned Athanasius, God’s bishop, though innocent, or have not communicated with your fellow heretic George [Note: [Col. 0881B] George the Cappadocian occupied the Alexandrian see until the year 361, when an enraged populace killed him.], or call themselves Christians because they refuse to become fellow apostates with you, then they may indeed judge [Note: [Col. 0881B] The Latin text and Galandius read “be judged.”] whether such works are pleasing to God. Likewise, if this is almsgiving which you give from [Note: [Col. 0881B] Constantius especially gloried in ecclesiastical expenditure and in a certain pious generosity toward the poor. But Lucifer reproaches him with this here and elsewhere, since he lavishly bestowed upon others—especially men of his own party—either spoils taken from Catholic churches, or the goods of bishops whom he had driven into exile, or of Catholics whom he had ordered either killed or deprived of their property. Hence Hilary, in his sole book *Against Constantius*: “You burden God’s holy things with the gold of the state, and thrust upon God things taken from temples, confiscated by edicts, or exacted by penalties.” And again: “He builds roofs for churches in order to destroy the faith.” Thus Lucifer himself said above: “You restore memorial shrines of martyrs, and shed the blood of God’s servants.”] others’ tears, from the goods of those who preferred to be deported, killed, and proscribed by you rather than either condemn an innocent man or deny the only Son of God—in believing in whom they knew that Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs, had been glorified—then he who has power to grant this to us is witness that my wishes concerning you are that you should become their companion and a participant with them all.

## Second Book in Defence of Saint Athanasius

[Col. 0881]

[Col. 0881C] Constantius, do you dare to stretch out your hands against persons consecrated to God, to harass those whose blessedness the Apostle declares when he says: “We know that all things work together for good to those who love the Lord [Note: [Col. 0881D] Old Latin: *God* … *for good* … *because those whom he foreknows* … *image*, etc.], to those who are called according to his purpose, whom he foreknew and predestined to be made conformable to the image of his Son” (Rom. 8:28). Your persecutions do indeed work for our good. But heed what God promises you persecutors through Jeremiah, saying: “Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his harvest; all who devour him shall incur guilt. I will bring evils upon them, says the Lord” (Jer. 2:3).

The evils which God promises you will come upon you, Constantius, unless you correct yourself, as they came upon that carnal people, your fellow-blasphemer, to whom it is said: “You have acted wickedly, [Col. 0881D] defiling your ways; and in your hands has been found the blood of innocent souls” (ibid., v. 33). You will be forever among God’s enemies unless, hearing, you heed his holy admonition: “If by correcting you correct [Note: [Col. 0881D] Sabatier reads *emendaveritis*, ‘you correct’.] your ways and your thoughts, and by doing you do justice between a man and his neighbour [Col. 0882C] and do not oppress the proselyte, the poor, and the widow [Note: [Col. 0881D] That is, you shall not exercise your power so as to shed his blood and put him to death; here *potentare* is used for exercising power and dominion. Tilius and La Cerda.], do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not go after foreign gods” (Jer. 7:5).

You will correct your ways if you now cease persecuting God’s servants; if you confess that you are a Christian and deny that you are an Arian; if you believe the Son of God to be the true Son of God; if you anathematize those who say, “There was [Note: [Col. 0881D] This Arian formula was expressly condemned by the Council of [Col. 0882D] Nicaea: “But those who say, ‘There was when he was not,’ and ‘Before he was begotten he was not,’ and ‘He came to be from things that did not exist,’ these the Catholic and Apostolic Church anathematizes.”] a time when he was not,” and “He was made from nothing.” You will change your ways if you repent of your murders and of [Note: [Col. 0882D] With the Latin witnesses we have correctly emended the printed reading *pro quo* (“for which”) to *proque* (“and for”).] your sacrilege. Otherwise you will be [Note: [Col. 0882D] “You will be one of those.” Tilius.]—as you now are—among those concerning whose reproach God says: “Is my house, in which my name has been invoked, a den of robbers?” (ibid., v. 11).

Whom do you say are God’s house—are you Arians, or are we Christians? For if your malignant assembly is God’s house, then the assembly of robbers [Col. 0882D] is God’s house. For in shedding the blood of God’s servants, as the Jews then shed it, you show yourselves to be robbers. By your fruits, Emperor Constantius, you are known not to be a Christian but plainly a contractor of robbers. For you order the innocent to be killed, dwelling, of course, not in the Lord’s church but in a den [Col. 0883A] of robbers. You do not cease murdering those whom you see ready to be killed for the glory of the only Son of God, for his eternal majesty.

We did not wish, in response to your false accusations, to pronounce sentence against a righteous man, lest that rebuke of the Lord should strike us too, with you and with the Jews: “He has bent his tongue like a bow for falsehood, and faithfulness has not prevailed in the land, because they have gone from evil to evil and have not known me” (Jer. 9:3). You, both fabricator and lover of false charges, you who do not know the Lord—unless [Note: [Col. 0883D] “Unless you correct yourself, you will be one of them.” So the same editor and Gallandius; but *as you are* may be retained in this sense: “Unless you correct yourself from what you now are.”] you correct yourself—will be, as you are, one of those of whom you have read it written: “They do not speak truth; their tongue has learned to speak falsehood. They refused to return, and did not abandon usury upon usury, deceit upon deceit. They refused to know me, says the Lord. Therefore,” [Col. 0883B] says the Lord, “behold, I will consume them and test them; for what else shall I do because of the wickedness of the daughter of my people? Their tongue is a wounding arrow; the words of their mouth are malignant. To his neighbour he speaks peaceably, while within himself he harbours enmity. Shall I not [Note: [Col. 0883D] “Shall I not visit?” Latin; in Greek, *mē ouk*, as in the Vulgate: “shall I not?”] punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall not my soul take vengeance upon such a nation?” (ibid., vv. 5–9).

Rescue yourself, Constantius, from the pit of Arian madness, lest you suffer eternal punishments with your fellow-sacrilegists. Do not glory in your perishable rank. Consider that you are mortal, since you cannot otherwise attain immortality unless you acknowledge God and do his will; as it is written: “Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom [Note: [Col. 0883D] Some manuscripts in Tilius read *patientia*, “patience.”], nor the strong man glory in his strength, nor the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: to seek [Note: [Col. 0883D] Old Latin: “to understand and know that I,” etc. See what we noted on this text above, p. 65, n. 7.] [Col. 0883C] me, to understand, and to know how to glory in God, because I am the Lord who exercises mercy, judgment, and righteousness upon the earth; for in these is my will, says the Lord” (ibid., vv. 23–24).

Therefore, when you see that the Lord’s will is in these things, how can you deign to hold in hatred what he says he loves? “Let him who glories,” he says, “glory in this: to seek me, to understand, and to know how to glory in God” (ibid., v. 24). How can you now say that you glory in God? How can you undertake to establish him when you provoke all worshippers of his majesty to abandon the apostles’ faith and embrace the blasphemy of your doctrine? “Let him who glories glory in this: to seek [Col. 0884A] me, to understand, and to know how to glory in God, because I am the Lord who exercises mercy, judgment, and righteousness upon the earth; for in these is my will, says the Lord” (ibid.).

Since, then, you desire that an unjust judgment be issued by God’s priests, and since you are a shedder of innocent blood, you are not the servant of him who deigned to speak these words through the prophet. You are plainly the servant of him who filled Cain’s heart so that he might kill the righteous boy, the first worshipper of the Lord. Thus it is that, though placed in so exalted a position, you are nevertheless found to be one of those concerning whom you have read the Lord speaking in the Gospel: “You [Note: [Col. 0883D] This agrees with Cyprian, *On the Lord’s Prayer*. Old Latin: “You are from your father the devil, and the desires … he was a murderer,” etc. The Cambridge manuscript in Sabatier, and Sabatier himself in Lucifer, read *concupiscentias*, “lusts,” as is also read in *On Not Sparing Those Who Sin against God*.] were born of the devil as father, and you desire to do your father’s lust; for he was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth” (John 8:44).

You are a liar and a murderer: a liar, because you have brought false [Col. 0884B] charges [Note: [Col. 0883D] For *obiecisti*, “you brought.” Tilius. How many and how grave were the calumnies which the heretics fabricated against Athanasius is entirely evident from his life.] against God’s servant Athanasius; a liar, because you call the heretical faith catholic and the catholic faith heretical; a murderer, because you pursue Athanasius’ blood and have already killed [Note: [Col. 0883D] He means Catholics, especially bishops, worn out by hardships, exiles, and prisons. Athanasius himself testifies to this in his *Letter to the Solitaries*: “Bishops were scourged and bound with harsh chains … how many monks were scourged, how many bishops mutilated!” This was especially so in the East, where Constantius was active. Among the bishops conspicuous in enduring Constantius’ cruelty he names Serapammon, Paulinus of Trier, Eusebius of Vercelli, Dionysius of Milan, Lucifer himself, bishops of the Church of Cagliari, and others mentioned by Ecclesiastical History, especially Hilary of Poitiers.] a definite number of God’s worshippers. Without doubt you have not stood in the truth while doing these things, but are wholly established in falsehood, since your father is a liar—the one who compels you to deny the only Son of God and drives you to shed the blood of his servants.

We were unwilling to condemn one who was absent; we were unwilling to pronounce sentence upon the innocent [Note: [Col. 0884D] For *de innocentibus*. It would have been clearer had he said, “We were unwilling to pronounce sentence upon innocent persons,” or “upon an innocent person”; perhaps *in innocentem*, “upon an innocent person,” should be read. Tilius and Latinus.] or accept your heresy, lest, made like you, we should deserve to hear what your fellow-wandering [Note: [Col. 0884D] That is, those who err along with you.] Jews hear, to whose reproach we gather from Jeremiah the saying: “All nations are uncircumcised [Note: [Col. 0884D] Old Latin: “uncircumcised in flesh; but the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”], and the whole [Note: [Col. 0884D] Sabatier reads *all*.] house of Israel is uncircumcised [Col. 0884C] in heart” (Jer. 9:26).

You are, and will be unless you surrender yourself to us, among those against whom the Holy Spirit cries, speaking in the person of our people to God: “I know, Lord, that a man’s way is not his own, nor will a man walk and direct his own thought. Correct us, Lord, but in judgment and not in anger, lest you make us few. Pour out your wrath upon the nations that do not know you and upon the kingdoms that have not invoked your name, because they have devoured Jacob, consumed him, and destroyed his pasturelands [Note: [Col. 0884D] Below Lucifer himself reads *desolaverunt*, ‘laid waste’.]” (Jer. 10:23–25).

You see that you are one of those against whom God’s Spirit speaks in the person of our people. You see that, unless you turn, the Lord’s wrath will come upon you—a foreigner [Col. 0885A] and a king—because not only have you not invoked the Lord’s name, but you have also persecuted. For when it says, “They have devoured Jacob, consumed him, and laid waste his pasturelands” (ibid., v. 25), who can be found among your fellow-tyrants as the chief destroyer of this pasture except you—who have neither ceased tearing [Note: [Col. 0885C] The expression is very harsh and uncouth; after the Greek manner two negatives are used for an affirmation. Likewise he says *laniando*, “by tearing,” for *laniare*, “to tear,” as he has often before used a gerund for an infinitive; then immediately he uses a participle for an infinitive, *seminans* for *seminare*. More Latinly expressed: “except you, who have neither ceased to tear God’s servants nor to sow your blasphemies throughout your whole realm.” Tilius and La Cerda; the latter adds that this man, by employing gerunds for infinitives, throws the sentence into confusion.] God’s servants to pieces nor [ceased] sowing your blasphemies throughout your realm?

For no one can doubt [Note: [Col. 0885D] For “no one can doubt,” that is, no one can be ignorant that you attempted to destroy the pasturelands—*pascua*—of God. Tilius.] that you have attempted to destroy the pastureland of God’s people, when you have removed its shepherds, of whom, as we have often said, God spoke through Jeremiah: “I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they shall feed you, feeding you with discipline” (Jer. 3:15); and when you have appointed heretics, while compelling other Catholics to accept such a condition that, if they wished [Note: [Col. 0885D] For “if they had it in their wishes,” that is, if they wished to remain safely in their own sees, they would not dare preach the apostolic faith. The cruelty and savagery of heretics against Catholics should be noted. The same editor and La Cerda.] to remain seated in their own [Col. 0885B] sees, they would not dare preach the apostolic faith or venture [Note: [Col. 0885D] For “undertake” or “dare to attempt.” The same editors.]—while you, the defender of the Arian heresy, remained in the body—to impart evangelical tradition to the peoples.

This is what proves that you attempted to destroy the pasturelands of God’s people. For the entire nourishment [Note: [Col. 0885D] That is, the faith of the patriarchs, etc., is rich nourishment for the soul.] of Christian souls is nothing other than believing as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs believed, and then practising every righteousness. But you, by contrast, sought both to remove faith from the hearts of God’s peoples and to implant your faithlessness; and you seek to have it done in God’s church as an act of righteousness [Note: [Col. 0885D] The sense may be: “When you wish it to occur in God’s Church as something just that …” Gallandius substitutes *injustitiam*, “injustice,” for *justitia*, “justice.”] that one absent and innocent should be condemned by the followers of justice, and that through priests their fellow-priest, a Catholic, should be punished at the prompting of you, a heretic [Note: [Col. 0886C] “Who are a heretic.”]. How can you seem not to be the destroyer of the pastureland of the Lord’s flock, [Col. 0885C] when our pastureland is nothing but heavenly teaching? “If you wish,” says the Lord, “to enter into life, keep the commandments” (Matt. 19:17); and again, “If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends” [Note: [Col. 0886C] Thus also the manuscript of the Greater Monastery in Sabatier. Old Latin: “I no longer call you servants, because … but I have called you [Col. 0886D] friends.” Lucifer himself shortly afterward has: “What I command you, I shall no longer call,” etc.; and again below: “What I command you,” etc.] (John 15:14).

Since this is so, you must produce, in your own defense, a commandment of the Lord requiring that an innocent Catholic bishop, accused meanwhile by you, the heretical emperor, be put to death by his fellow-priests. Perhaps you will try at this point to say that you did not attempt to destroy the pastureland of the Lord’s flock. If you cannot produce any commandment of the Lord of the sort you have put forward, it remains that [Col. 0886A] the eyes of your heart, blinded by the blasphemy of Arius, may be opened through God’s servants, so as to see this rebuke: that you have done all the things of which we accuse you.

You cannot deny that you show yourself toward us as Herod showed himself toward those little children whom we read in the Gospel were killed for God, the Son of God. In murderous rage, in sacrilege, and in royal dignity, you are found to be Herod’s companion. You have certainly found in the Evangelist Matthew the cruelty of Herod which you now deign to display: “Then Herod, when [Note: [Col. 0886D] Old Latin: “he saw that … exceedingly; and he sent and killed … the boys who were in … his territories.”] he saw that he had been deceived by the Magi, was violently enraged and sent to kill all the infants in Bethlehem and throughout all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had learned from the Magi” (Matt. 2:16).

Perhaps you still do not see that you have been moved unjustly against us worshippers of God just as Herod was moved against those children. Why do you deign to be hostile to us? Surely because we confess that we are Christians and have not condemned the righteous man oppressed by false charges from you. You may discern what sort of man you are from the answer of blessed John the Baptist, and reconcile yourself to God by repentance: “Brood of vipers, who showed [Note: [Col. 0886D] Several manuscripts in Sabatier read “showed”; Old Latin: “will show … the wrath to come.”] you how to flee from the wrath that is to come? Therefore bear fruit worthy of repentance, and do not put forward [Note: [Col. 0886D] Old Latin: *proferre*, “bring forth.” The manuscript of Saint-Germain in Sabatier agrees with Lucifer.] yourselves, saying, ‘We have Abraham as father.’ For I tell you that God is able [Note: [Col. 0886D] Old Latin: “Because God is able.”] from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. For already [Note: [Col. 0886D] Vatican manuscript: “indeed.”] the axe has been laid to the roots of the trees. Every [Note: [Col. 0886D] Old Latin: “Every therefore … shall be cut down … shall be thrown.” Greek with Lucifer: *ekkoptetai … balletai*, “is cut down … is thrown.”] tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire” (Matt. 3:7–10).

What do you think of this? Ought we to have condemned the innocent? Ought we to have passed sentence against one absent and unheard? And how, had we done this, could we have been found Christians? Blessed John urged those men—who did not yet comprehend the way of righteousness—to become Christians by bearing fruit worthy of repentance [Note: [Col. 0886D] For *facerent*, “they might bear.” Tilius and La Cerda.]. But we, who already hold that way, were and are pressed by you to take up that path of iniquity in which the Jews are known to stand. What, then, could have happened to us had we been fed upon your viperish counsels, except that from Christians we should have become a brood of vipers [Note: [Col. 0886D] Vatican manuscript: “viperish.”]?

Why did you order these things to be done, except because you desired to make us your fellow-serpents [Col. 0887A]—you who know that the Lord said in the Gospel: “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. Blessed are the merciful, because [Note: [Col. 0887D] With Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book 3. Old Latin: “because God will have mercy on them.”] they shall obtain mercy” (Matt. 5:6–7)—and yet have said that an innocent man must be killed?

For how can I be blessed if I condemn a righteous man? How, if I reject thirst for righteousness and conceive a burning desire for injustice? How shall I be satisfied by God because of the fruits of righteousness, when this unjust deed makes me a fratricidal Cain? Again, how shall I be able to attain the heavenly kingdom among the merciful, enriched with the fruits of mercy, when, if I kill God’s servant in accordance with your desires, I shall be found not merciful but cruel and criminal—indeed, a murderer? And when [Note: [Col. 0887D] “If when”; understand, “if ever.”] I have been unmerciful toward my brother, so likewise will that lover of mercy, that exactor of righteousness, be toward me—he who says: “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. Blessed are the merciful, because [Col. 0887B] they shall obtain mercy” (ibid.).

“Whoever,” says the Lord, “shall break one of these least commandments and teach people so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven” (ibid., v. 19). And do you say, Constantius, that whoever has not shed innocent blood cannot attain the kingdom of heaven? Tell me, most holy emperor, in what can the righteousness of Christians abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees if we kill the man whom you persecute because he calls himself a Christian and refuses to become an Arian? In what should we be superior to the scribes and Pharisees if, along with you, we became deniers of the only Son of God; if, as they [Col. 0887C] reject it, we rejected with you the evangelical faith and destroyed apostolic tradition?

Did you not remember that the Lord said: “You have heard that it was said to the ancients [Note: [Col. 0887D] Old Latin: “by the ancients … but whoever.”], ‘You shall not kill; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment’ [Note: [Col. 0887D] Old Latin: “liable to judgment” in both places. *In* is absent from the Greek, as it is in Lucifer.]. But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause shall be liable to judgment” (ibid., v. 21)—that you should order these things to be done? If I am angry without cause with my brother, if I say to him, “Fool,” the only Son of God says that I shall be liable to Gehenna; and [Note: [Col. 0887D] Perhaps: “and you, Emperor,” etc. Gallandius.] you, Emperor Constantius, say that if I shed innocent blood, I shall possess eternal rest. Nor, when you meditated on putting Athanasius to death, could you retain in mind on what condition the Lord commanded gifts to be offered: “Therefore, if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that [Note: [Col. 0887D] With Hilary of Poitiers, *Commentary on Matthew*. Old Latin: “If therefore you offer … because your brother has something against you, leave there … then, having come, you shall offer.”] your brother has [Col. 0887D] something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and [Col. 0888A] first go and be reconciled with your brother; then return and offer your gift” (ibid., vv. 23–24).

What evil had Athanasius done that you ordered him to be killed as a transgressor of these commands? Surely only this: that he said, or says, that he is a Christian. There is no other thing which you detest or desire to punish in Athanasius. Did you not remember that the Lord commanded even enemies to be loved, that you should so fiercely persecute one whom you knew to have sinned neither against you nor against God? “You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate [Note: [Col. 0887D] Old Latin: “you shall hate … bless those who curse you.”] your enemy.’ But I say to you: Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who [Note: [Col. 0888D] Old Latin: “those who hate you; pray for those who accuse you falsely and persecute you … he commands his sun to rise … For if you love … do they do this? And if you greet your brothers … what more will you do? Do not even the Gentiles do this? Be therefore,” etc. Cyprian, *On the Good of Patience*: “who persecute you.” Several manuscripts: *philous*, “friends.” Greek: *poieite*, “you do”; Tertullian, *Against Marcion*, book 1: “you shall be.” All these agree with Lucifer.] persecute you, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven, who causes the sun to rise on good and [Col. 0888B] evil and rains upon just and unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your friends, what more do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do likewise? Therefore you too shall be perfect, as your Father who is in heaven is perfect” (ibid., vv. 43–48).

The Lord commands even enemies to be loved, and you persecute us because we did not shed with you the blood of an innocent priest of the Lord. The divine voice cries: “With whatever judgment you judge, you shall be judged; and with whatever measure you have measured, it shall be measured back [Note: [Col. 0888D] Old Latin: *remetietur*, “shall be measured back”; Tilius and Latinus correct accordingly.] to you” (Matt. 7:2). Yet you say: “Slay the man whom you do not know to have sinned.” Though you know yourself to be the source of evils, you nevertheless dared say of one whom you knew was falsely accused by your party: “He is guilty of death.”

You are so senseless, Augustus Constantius, that when ordering these things to be done you could not even remember that saying of the Lord: “Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Allow me to remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, a beam [Note: [Col. 0888D] The Corbie and Saint-Germain manuscripts read *trabis*, ‘of a beam,’ in Sabatier and the Old Latin.] is in your own eye? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see to remove the speck from your brother’s eye” (ibid., vv. 3–5).

The Lord says that there is a beam in your eye, and yet you dare say to Athanasius, a most righteous man, “You have a speck in your eye.” For he has done none of the things you deign to charge against him. You, on the contrary, have done everything we have said whenever you said, “Condemn the innocent man.” What other path did you wish us to take except yours—the one which the Lord describes when he says: “How [Note: [Col. 0888D] Old Latin: “Because broad … is the way … to destruction.” Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book 3; Hilary on Matthew; Codex Claromontanus; Sabatier with Lucifer: “How broad.”] broad and spacious is the way that [Col. 0888D] leads to destruction, and many are they who enter through it” [Col. 0889A] (ibid., v. 13)?

Because [Note: [Col. 0889D] For *cum*, “when.” Tilius.] you stand in this broad and spacious way, you ordered the innocent man condemned, evidently desiring it to be revealed to all that your extensive destruction holds sway. When [Note: [Col. 0889D] This alludes to Constantius’ arrival in Italy from Gaul in 354, where he set in motion the acts wickedly carried out by the Arians at the Council of Milan in the following year.] you came into Italy, you disguised yourself as a sheep though you were a wolf, as though we would not discover you from your deeds, as though the Lord’s warning [Note: [Col. 0889D] For “admonition and exhortation.” Tilius. Du Cange also notes this word in his *Glossarium mediae et infimae Latinitatis*, citing Lucifer.] would escape us: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly [Note: [Col. 0889D] Old Latin: “from within.”] are ravening wolves; by their fruits you shall know them” (ibid., v. 15).

Did not your exceedingly bitter fruits, ripened at once by the devil’s poisons sown in you, appear when you tried to say that an unheard man ought to be condemned? Did not the snares of you, the ravening wolf, immediately become evident? For, since you had constructed a very great engine against God’s sheepfold, you were known by your fruits to be not a sheep but a wolf. And the sacred Gospels likewise prove what sort of tree you are—unless you take care for yourself—a tree appointed for fire. “Do men gather grapes [Note: [Col. 0889D] Old Latin: “grapes … Every therefore … Thus by their fruits … shall say.”] from thorns, or figs from thistles? So every good tree bears good fruits, but a bad tree bears bad fruits. A good tree cannot bear bad fruits, nor can a bad tree bear good fruits. Every tree which does not bear good fruit shall be cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore by their fruits you shall know them. Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father” (ibid., vv. 16–21).

If you do the will of the Father of the only Son of God, how is it that you deny his only-begotten Son, say that the Father himself is not a true Father, attempt to destroy the foundations [Col. 0889C] laid through the apostles, killed and still kill his worshippers, drive his bishops from the peoples entrusted to them, command that one absent and unheard be condemned, and introduce into the church your heresy, which blasphemes the one divinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit? If all these things, as we have said, please God the Father, you may enter the kingdom of heaven. For you hear his only Son say: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father” (ibid., v. 21).

You order the innocent condemned. Do you not recall God saying in Exodus: “If two men quarrel [Note: [Col. 0889D] Old Latin: “If two men litigate.”] and strike a woman with child, and she suffers a miscarriage [Note: [Col. 0889D] For “has suffered a miscarriage and gives birth to a child not malformed,” that is, whole and complete, not deficient or mutilated in limbs. This reading is closer to the Hebrew text than our common text. Tilius and La Cerda. Old Latin: “and her child comes forth not yet formed.” Gallandius reads “not yet formed” with Augustine, *Questions*, 80, and rejects Tilius’ interpretation, though it may be defended.] of one not malformed, he shall suffer a penalty: [Col. 0890A] whatever the woman’s husband assesses, he shall pay with [Note: [Col. 0890D] Thus the Greek, *meta axiōmatos*. Old Latin: “with a demand”; and “but if it shall be formed … burning for burning.” Sabatier reads, “but if it is malformed,” for “but if it is.”] due valuation. But if it is malformed, he shall give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise” (Exod. 21:22–25).

I believe [Note: [Col. 0890D] This is said ironically. See the note in *On Dying for the Son of God*.] that none of the sacred Scriptures escapes you; for you could not give us such excellent commands unless you were skilled in the law. You have certainly also read this: “Everyone who hears these words of mine [Note: [Col. 0890D] Old Latin: “these my words … is like.”] and does them, I shall compare him to a prudent [Note: [Col. 0890D] With the Greek, *phronimō*, ‘prudent’; Old Latin: ‘wise’.] man who built his house upon a rock. The rain descended, and [Note: [Col. 0890D] Old Latin: “the winds blew, the floods came, and struck … these my words and does not do them, is like a man … the winds blew, the floods came, and struck against that house.”] the floods came, the winds blew, and they beat [Note: [Col. 0890D] Calmet reads from Lucifer *impugerunt*, ‘struck against,’ among variant readings, vol. VII of his *Commentary on Holy Scripture*.] against that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon a rock. But everyone who hears my words and does not do them, I shall compare him [Col. 0890B] [Note: [Col. 0890D] Sabatier reads “him.”] to a foolish man who built his house upon sand. The rain descended, the floods came, the winds blew, they struck against that house, and it fell; and its fall was great” (Matt. 7:24–27).

Which of these do you say you are, Constantius: wise or foolish? If you say wise, why do your deeds show you foolish? Why is your house found placed upon sand? For you cannot say that you have built your house upon rock when every wise person sees the structure of your folly, when every servant of God beholds this great ruin of your salvation, foretold by the Lord. For in what is a Christian found to stand, except in obeying the Lord’s commands? Except in remaining immovable, though harassed by every persecution for the name of God’s Son? In what will a Christian be perfect, except if he is even killed for him whom you deign to deny is the true Son of God?

But you, since you are not in the church but among the Arian enemies of God; since you deny God’s only Son; since you do not fulfil his commands of mercy but rather attempt to destroy them; since you are a transgressor of the law, a deserter from the oath of heavenly military service, a persecutor of God’s religion, and show yourself an executioner toward his worshippers—how can you be found a wise man like the one whom the Lord said had built his house upon a rock?

But you answer this: “I am not foolish; I know myself to be wise.” If you are wise, why have you done and why are you doing what only fools can do? [Col. 0891A] If you are wise, why did you order one absent and unheard condemned? Why did you command the innocent to be killed? Why did you desire God’s priests to become God’s enemies? For they cannot become God’s friends by such an act, since you know the Lord said to the apostles: “If you do [Note: [Col. 0891D] See what we noted at p. 119 of this edition, col. 886, note h.] what I command you, I shall no longer call you servants, but friends” (John 15:14).

If you are wise, why ought I, a priest of God, to listen to Athanasius condemning you? You did not permit him at all to state the grounds of his defense. If you are wise, if you worship God, why do you persecute us because we confess that we are Christians? Why do you love intensely those who say not that they are Christians but confess themselves to be Arians? If you are wise, why have you repeatedly sent armed soldiers to God’s house? If you are prudent and know yourself to be God’s servant, [Col. 0891B] why have you persecuted and do you persecute his people with arms? Finally, why do you call the apostolic and evangelical faith heretical and pronounce the heretical faith catholic?

You call yourself wise, but we see, to the contrary, that no one who does these things can be wise. What sacrilegious man can be called prudent, except by persons more imprudent than himself? If you are wise, Constantius, I cannot find anyone more foolish than you. Do you still think yourself wise—you who imagined that prophets, apostles, and martyrs were killed for a creature? For you will not dare deny that all these were killed for the only Son of God. How can you be called wise when you not only did not try to withstand descending rains, flooding rivers, and blowing winds, lest they drag you down—you who are found to be a house [Col. 0891C]—but yourself turned into rains, rivers, and winds, in order that you, a diabolical whirlwind and storm, might drag us with you into outer darkness?

“But the works of the flesh,” says the Apostle, “are manifest: adulteries, fornications, uncleanness, shamelessness, licentiousness [Note: [Col. 0891D] *Luxuria*, ‘licentiousness,’ is absent from the Old Latin, which has “provocations” for “quarrels” and “shall possess” for “shall inherit.”], idolatry, sorceries, enmities, contentions, jealousies, angers, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, envies, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. I forewarn you, as I have forewarned you, that those who do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God” (Gal. 5:19–21). And is your mind, vigorous in devising an innocent man’s death, wisdom? The Apostle cries that murderers shall not possess the kingdom of heaven; yet you, most prudent Emperor Constantius, say: “Slay those absent, sacrifice those unheard, kill the innocent, [Col. 0891D] and God’s kingdom shall be yours.”

This shows how wise you are—whether, in short, [Col. 0892A] you are the man who built his house upon a rock. For you cannot deny having said: “I desire to condemn Athanasius because I wish to please God.” Thus you desired that we too should please God, just as you yourself have now pleased him, since you deigned to contemplate killing Athanasius, the Lord’s priest, in the conscience of all of us [Note: [Col. 0891D] Gallandius reads *sacerdotem*, singular, incorrectly; the sense is clear: “in the conscience of all of us, priests of the Lord.”]. Thus [Note: [Col. 0891D] Said ironically.] Cain, at the beginning, pleased God.

…was pleasing as soon as he had planned to kill his brother. Constantius, how clear it appears from what root, from what stock you descended. Can you then deny that you belong to that company which the Apostle describes to the Romans?

> “And since they did not see fit to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do what is unfitting, filled with every injustice, wickedness, impurity [Greek: *akatharsia*], greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits; whisperers, slanderers, hateful to God, insolent, proud, self-pleasing, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents, foolish, disorderly, without natural affection, without mercy; who, though they knew God’s righteousness, did not understand that those who do such things are deserving of death. And not only those who do them, but also those who approve those who do them.” (Rom. 1:28)

[Note: Col. 0891D. Ancient Version: “in knowledge,” as Lucifer himself has in *On the Son of God*, where he also has “may agree” for “agree.”]

[Note: Col. 0891D. Two Sabatier manuscripts: Greek *akatharsia* [“impurity”], with Lucifer. Ancient Version: “fornication, greed,” omitting “malice,” and “malignity” in place of “evil habits.”]

[Note: Col. 0892D. Ancient Version: “whisperers, slanderers … haughty,” omitting “self-pleasing, boastful.”]

[Note: Col. 0892D. Ancient Version: “obedient … without affection … knew.”]

[Note: Col. 0892D. Sabatier and the Ancient Version omit “them.”]

Behold what your excessive love, suddenly aroused toward us, would have brought us had we dared obey you: we should have swallowed everlasting death. Again he says below:

> “Repaying no one evil for evil; providing what is good not only before God but also before all people. If possible, so far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.” (Rom. 12:17)

[Note: Col. 0892D. So also Clement of Alexandria, with certain manuscripts: Greek, “not only before God, but also before human beings.” Ancient Version: “only before human beings.”]

Thirsting to trample these saving admonitions underfoot, you urged us to punish an innocent man. How could we have been found to provide what is good not only before God but also before people, if we had condemned an innocent man and furnished an example for shedding the blood of the righteous? How could I have been found to desire peace with all people if, through your false prompting, I had extinguished my fellow priest’s peace by the departure [*exitus*] of a heretic, had I condemned an innocent man?

[Note: Col. 0892D. “Departure” [*exitus*]. Latin and Galandius read *excitūs* (“incitement”); but it may also mean “peaceful end, departure, death,” which I would have taken away if I had condemned an innocent man; or “the prompting of the heretic’s departure,” namely, that which would have brought about the ruinous end of the true faith.]

Tell me, Constantius: did you bring a true charge against Athanasius before God’s Church, or a false one? If you are certain that you brought a true charge, prove it to me, who have now recognized you as the bearer of a false accusation. Do you suppose that you committed no evil in the sight of God? What reason compelled you to become a false witness? Why did you become a lying emperor? Why did you not fear that you might be struck down after the example of Ananias and Sapphira?

Scripture says in the Acts of the Apostles that blessed Peter said to Ananias:

> “Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to withhold part of the price of the estate? While it remained unsold, did it not remain yours? And after it was sold, was it not under your authority? Why did you set this matter in your heart? You have lied not to human beings, but to God.”  
>   
> When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and died; and great fear came upon all who heard. The young men rose, carried him out, and buried him. About three hours later his wife, not knowing what had happened, entered. Peter said to her, “Tell me, did you sell the estate for this amount?” She answered, “For this amount.” Peter said to her, “Why have you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” Immediately she fell at his feet and died. (Acts 5:3)

[Note: Col. 0893D. As Cyprian, *Testimonies*, book 3. Ancient Version: “Why did you fill … to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to appropriate from the price of the possession?” Lucifer himself shortly afterward has “that you had lied” for “to lie.”]

[Note: Col. 0893D. Ancient Version: “Why indeed did you put … this … And immediately, having heard … these words … all hearing these things … and at once … gathered her and, carrying her out … about … and his wife, not knowing what had happened, entered. Peter said to her … ‘Did you sell the field?’ She said, ‘Yes, for so much.’ Peter said to her, ‘Why indeed … you … your husband … stand at the door …’ And she fell immediately.”]

I believe that you read these things, and yet did not fear to devise a lie before the Lord’s sight. Why did you do this, unless because you are wise? What do you think awaits you, who are not only a liar but a murderer; not only a murderer but also a heretic? Do you believe that such things will pass without punishment for you? Do you believe that you can escape eternal punishments? It is said to Ananias: “Why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit?” (Acts 5:3). And will you, Emperor Constantius, say that Satan did not fill the hearts of you Arians, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit abiding in God’s Church?

For you approached the Church saying, “Athanasius has sinned against God”; and the Holy Spirit saw your lying souls, just as he saw Ananias and Sapphira. The Holy Spirit saw, I say, when you fabricated these things, that you had contrived such accusations against Athanasius in order to introduce your heresy into the Church and destroy apostolic tradition. Ananias and Sapphira, because in selling their field they deceived concerning its price, because they dared not speak wholly truthfully before God’s Apostle, deserved to be judged in this manner.

But you, who not only brought false charges against God’s servant, but persecuted the whole household of God; who shed the blood of his worshippers; who sent his priests to the mines and into exile; who appointed heretics in their places; who called the evangelical faith heretical and your blasphemy catholic; who introduced idolatry into the Church; who abandoned the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, and of all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs; and who followed the idolatry of Arius—do you suppose that, if you persist in this blasphemy and cruelty, the greatest vengeance will not come upon you?

[Note: Col. 0893D. We read “your blasphemy,” where the printed text had “blasphemous”; thus Lucifer himself writes shortly afterward, “in this blasphemy.” See the Preface.]

Moreover, if God deemed it fitting to inflict such vengeance on Susanna’s adversaries, do you think that a heavier judgment will not proceed against you? It will, believe me, unless you promptly turn back. For if they, because they attempted to violate Susanna’s chastity, deserved to suffer what I shall set forth, how much more you, who have undertaken to violate the chastity of the Church? They sought Susanna on a false charge; and you sought in like manner not Athanasius alone, but all who resisted you.

Can you name a single one of those who resisted whom no charge was laid against? Thus you were armed to violate the Church’s chastity, as they were armed against Susanna, who said:

> “The garden doors are shut; no one sees us; we desire you. Therefore consent to us and be with us; otherwise we shall give false testimony against you, saying that a young man was with you and that you therefore sent the maidservants away from you.” (Dan. 13:20)

Or will you attempt to deny that this was what was said? “We Arians desire that we and you Christians should become one body: abandon the faith set down at Nicaea which you maintain against us; submit to Arius’s doctrine. Otherwise, since we are very powerful and the imperial authority is ours, we shall afflict you by whatever means we wish and remove you all from your sees.” You cannot deny that matters stood thus, when your God-hating designs have been exposed by their actual execution.

Why were we compelled, even if we did not condemn Athanasius, nevertheless to mingle in communion with the Arians, unless because you, the procurer of the Arian heresy, desired by any means whatever to make us all fellow-sacrilegists with you? Yet I suppose you still try to deny that you persecute us because we refused, though Christians, to become Arians. How can you deny it, when you sent into exile the most holy Dionysius, bishop of Milan, who, believing your false allegation, had condemned Athanasius, because he refused to become an Arian? Or is not Auxentius, whom you rashly and pestilentially appointed in his place, an Arian?

[Note: Col. 0893D–0894D. Saint Dionysius, Bishop of Milan until 355, was deceived by the Arians at the Milanese Council of that year and condemned Athanasius. But by the shrewd and prudent counsel of Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, his subscription was erased. Eusebius turned to the Arian bishops and, pretending that he too agreed to Athanasius’s condemnation, requested that he be allowed to subscribe before Dionysius, since he was older. Moved by this argument, the Arians erased Dionysius’s name and granted precedence to Eusebius. Rebuking and mocking them, he said: “I neither pollute myself with your crimes nor permit my son Dionysius to share with you.” Dionysius was driven into exile, and the Arian Auxentius was appointed in his place. He at times pretended to be catholic and, by the favor of Emperor Valentinian, occupied the Church of Milan for twenty years; he died in 374.]

If Auxentius holds the holy faith set down at Nicaea, then you too may be no Arian; nor can you have done all that I allege, nor brought a false charge against Athanasius.

[Note: Col. 0894D. “Holds,” with Tilius, Latinus, and Galandius rightly; formerly, however, the text read otherwise.]

[Note: Col. 0894D–0895D. “Brought” for “sent in”; that is, if you have not done what I allege against you, you are no longer an Arian and did not falsely accuse Athanasius. Tilius, La Cerda, and Galandius.]

Perhaps you will say that we are not catholic because Susanna was heard, whereas we were not. So far as our conscience is concerned, we know that we were vindicated when you, serpent, were exposed; when all your poisons were uncovered; when your whole contrivance was laid bare. For this was the vengeance we desired against you enemies of God: that God should reveal to his people that you were heretics. Nearly the whole world now knows that Athanasius was falsely accused by you, and that you are the author of this wickedness; for you were seen to desire one thing and to have uttered another.

[Note: Col. 0895A. The whole machinery of the Milanese pseudo-council was directed toward procuring Athanasius’s condemnation by catholic bishops, especially Western ones, as though he were guilty of crimes repeatedly fabricated against him by heretics. Thus it might lend some appearance of legitimacy to Arian impiety, of which Constantius was patron. Athanasius himself says in his Letter to the Solitary: “The Emperor therefore pressed the bishops to subscribe against Athanasius; threateningly he drew the sword against them and ordered some to be dragged from his presence. But when he saw the constancy of the bishops Lucifer, Eusebius, and Dionysius … he immediately rose and said: ‘I am now Athanasius’s accuser; because of me believe what the Arians say.’ They replied: ‘How can you be accuser in the case of one absent? If the accuser is present but the accused absent, no trial can be conducted; and because of the distance of the journey he could not be present … If you allege matters from hearsay, it is fair that you should also believe what he himself says; but if you do not believe him while believing these men, then these men seem rather to say such things for your favor and to accuse Athanasius for that reason.’ When the Emperor heard these things said before him and regarded them as an insult to himself, he banished them.” Athanasius, ibid. This also concerns what Lucifer intimates here, and what he said a little above, from “What reason compelled you to become a false witness?” to this place.]

Susanna says with groaning to the elders:

> “Distress surrounds me on every side. If I do this, death will be mine; but if I do not do it, I shall not escape your hands. It is better for me, without having done it, to fall into your hands than to sin in the sight of the Lord.” (Dan. 13:22)

And we, as soon as we saw charges laid upon us by you, would have destroyed our brothers, since we would have been darkness as you are. What Christian would not say that it is better to be killed by you, forerunner of Antichrist, than to enter into the darkness of you Arians or of any other heretics? You caused charges to be laid not only against Athanasius but also against us, because we refused, though Christians, to become Arians. No individual charge that could be alleged against each person was lacking, so that none of us might appear to have been sent into exile for God’s sake, but seemingly on account of our own crimes.

[Note: Col. 0896D. Said ironically.]

Since, therefore, you were guilty of so many crimes because Athanasius was unwilling to have God angry with you, you declared him worthy of death. This is what those elders, your equals in this wickedness, also did. Scripture says:

> “On the next day the people assembled at the house of her husband Joachim; and two elders, full of wicked intent against Susanna, came in order to put her to death. They said before the people, ‘Send for Susanna, daughter of Chelkiah, wife of Joachim.’ They sent for her; and she came, with her parents and all her relatives. Susanna was exceedingly delicate and beautiful in appearance. The unjust men ordered her unveiled—for she was veiled—that they might satisfy themselves with her beauty. All her family and all who saw her wept. Then the two elders rose up among the people and laid their hands upon her head. She, weeping, looked toward heaven, because her heart trusted in the Lord.  
>   
> “The elders said, ‘As we were walking alone in the garden, this woman came in with maidservants, dismissed the maidservants, and shut the garden doors. Then a young man, who had been concealed, came to her and lay with her. We were in a corner of the garden; when we saw this wickedness, we ran toward them and saw them coming together. We could not seize the young man because he was stronger than we were and, opening the doors, leapt out. But we seized this woman and asked her who the young man was; she would not tell us. This is our testimony.’ And the whole assembly believed them, because they were elders of the people and judges; and they condemned her to die.” (Dan. 13:27)

[Note: Col. 0896D. That is, in order to deliver her to death; so earlier. Hence also the participle used below: “your poisons lie slain by God’s power,” that is, dead, vain, and empty. Tilius and La Cerda.]

[Note: Col. 0896D. Sabatier reads “their own.”]

[Note: Col. 0896D. Tilius, from the Greek and Vulgate, reads “lying together”; Galandius agrees.]

Consider thoroughly, Constantius, whether the accursed inventions of you Arians are not the very things which you did against Athanasius, just as those men did against Susanna. For who would not have believed you, the emperor, when you said, “Athanasius has committed sacrilege”? Yet because you proved more detestable than those utterly ruined false elders, we did not give you credit. For it was said to you that an absent man could not be condemned. Those elders uttered criminal allegations against a person present, and the whole assembly passed sentence upon one present. But when, at the accusation of heretics, you compelled a catholic to be condemned unheard and absent, the machinery of your drama had already begun to be seen.

But now hear what was granted to chaste Susanna by the defender of the innocent and avenger of the oppressed. Hear what the Book of Daniel relates concerning Susanna’s vindication:

> “Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said, ‘Eternal God, knower of hidden things, who know all things before they come to pass: you know that they have borne false testimony against me; and behold, I die, though I have done none of the things which these wicked men have fabricated against me.’ And God heard her voice. As she was being led away to perish, God stirred up the holy spirit of a young boy named Daniel. He cried out with a loud voice, ‘I am innocent of this woman’s blood!’ All the people turned toward him and said, ‘What is this word that you have spoken?’ Standing in their midst, he said, ‘Are you such fools, O Israel, that without examination and without learning the truth you have condemned a daughter of Israel? Return to the judgment, for they have borne false testimony against her.’” (Dan. 13:42)

So now too, while Athanasius cries out to God, God has caused all his servants to rise for the truth against you, his adversaries. He has granted his worshippers what he then granted his most devoted Daniel, so that we might understand you to be a false witness, one of the brood of vipers, and that you devised these falsehoods with your fellow-sacrilegists.

[Note: Col. 0897D. That is, fabricated and falsely brought forward; for poets invent many things which never existed. Tilius and La Cerda.]

All now return to a righteous judgment, turning against you the sentence of death which you meanwhile inflict—yes, even those whom the ruler of your soul, the devil, had by your cunning deceived without their knowing it.

[Note: Col. 0897D. “The passage is corrupt,” says Tilius; Latinus corrected it thus: “all now turn against you,” etc. But the sense, although obscure, is this: all the catholic bishops, including those whom you had deceived, return to a just judgment for Athanasius against you, while you inflict a sentence of death upon us.]

For except for your fellow-Arians, no one can fail to desire the vindication of Athanasius’s innocence; so greatly does everyone favor his innocence. Just as Susanna, once it was established that she was falsely accused—a chaste woman by unchaste men, a pure woman by adulterers, a handmaid of God by servants of the devil—so the standing of this innocent man, faithfully serving God, was assailed by you, the serpent-sons of Satan. But you have been overthrown: all your poisons lie dead through God’s power. Indeed every Christian soul prays to God that, as he rescued Susanna from a false accusation, he may rescue Athanasius from a false charge, from your executioner’s sword, from your murderer’s cruelty.

Meanwhile, again and again I press you to see what madness has seized you Arians, what insanity has possessed you, that you dared to devise these things for the death of an innocent man, when you knew that God knows all things before they happen. Yet it is no wonder that this plot against Athanasius was constructed by you and yours, since you did not hesitate to say of God the Father, “He is not a true Father, for he has no true Son.” For when you say that the Son of God is from nothing, what else do you say than that he is not a true Father?

It is not surprising, I say, if you rose thus against God’s servant Athanasius, when you did not hesitate to lay your deadly hands upon him whose servant Athanasius is. For a robber who has not spared the master of the house cannot spare the household that resists him.

But now let us return to what you commanded us to do. You said, “Condemn Athanasius.” What had occurred that we should not see him face to face? What had happened that I should not investigate every aspect of the matter? Why did you not allow him to be convicted by competent witnesses? Did the most holy Daniel—or rather, the Holy Spirit through Daniel—condemn even those men unheard? For we read that glorious Daniel said to the people:

> “Separate them from one another.”  
>   
> He called one of them and said to him, “Aged in evil days, now your sins which you formerly committed have come upon you: you gave unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty, though the Lord says, ‘You shall not kill the innocent and righteous.’ Now, if you saw this woman, tell me: under what tree did you see them embracing?” He replied, “Under a mastic tree.” Daniel said, “You have lied correctly against your own head; for already the angel of the Lord, having received a command from God, will cut you in two.”  
>   
> When he had removed him, he commanded the other to be brought forward and said, “Seed of Canaan and not of Judah: beauty deceived you, and lust perverted your heart. This is how you acted toward the daughters of Israel; and they, through fear, lay with you. But the daughter of Judah did not endure your injustice. Now tell me, under what tree did you seize them embracing one another?” He answered, “Under an oak.” Daniel said to him, “You too have lied correctly against your own head. For the angel of God stands ready, holding a sword to cut you in two and destroy you both.”  
>   
> Then the whole assembly cried out with a loud voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in him. They rose against the two elders, because Daniel had convicted them from their own mouths as false witnesses; and according to the Law of Moses they did to them what they had wickedly intended to do to their neighbor: they put them to death, and on that day innocent blood was saved.” (Dan. 13:51)

What can your folly answer to this, Constantius? Do you see persons guilty of such a crime condemned everywhere without every matter being most carefully examined? And yet against one whom you knew to be innocent you did not hesitate to command God’s priests to pronounce a sentence of death? What would we have heard, had we done so? Surely what those false-witness pseudo-elders, stumbling blocks of lust, hear: “Aged in evil days, now your sins which you formerly committed have come upon you: you gave unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty, though the Lord says, ‘You shall not kill the innocent and righteous’” (Dan. 13:52).

Would we not rightly and deservedly merit to hear this, if we had been either seduced or frightened by you, the cesspool of Arian doctrine, into condemning an innocent man? And for this reason all these evils have come upon you. You and yours will hear what those men heard through Daniel, whether because you are guilty of alleging a false charge, because you summoned the entire company of bishops to put an innocent man to death, or because you wished all God’s people to receive your heresy.

[Note: Col. 0898D. On the number of bishops present at the Council of Milan, see what has already been said in the Life of Saint Lucifer.]

Indeed, you will hear more grievous things, because your deeds are more grievous: you who proved to be the destroyer of God’s religion; who killed a vast multitude of those called Christians; who introduced your Arian heresy into the Church; who condemned the catholic faith; who denied that God the Father is a true Father; who said that his only Son is not a true Son; and who asserted that the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is not the true Spirit of God.

By contrast, the faith of the holy Church cries out against you and against all God’s enemies that it believes in God, the true unbegotten Father; and in his only Son, begotten from the unbegotten and true Father—that is, from the Father’s substance: God from God, light from light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, of one substance with the Father, which the Greeks call *homoousion* [ὁμοούσιον], through whom all things were made and without whom nothing was made; and in the Paraclete, the true Spirit of God.

[Note: Col. 0898D–0899A. These formulas of catholic faith, from “God from God” through “all things were made,” are taken from the Nicene Creed.]

[Note: Col. 0898D. That is, of the same substance as the Father, which is the proper meaning of the Greek word *homoousios* [ὁμοούσιος]. See Petavius, *On the Trinity*, book 4, chapter 5.]

Therefore, to you—a false witness, spiritual adulterer, sacrilegious murderer—more grievous words will deservedly be spoken, since by such great and such numerous crimes you are worse than those pseudo-elders, Susanna’s enemies. For if it is said to them as they lie, “You have lied correctly against your own head. For already the angel of the Lord, having received a command from God, will cut you in two” (Dan. 13:55), and, “You have lied correctly against your own head. The angel of God stands ready, holding a sword to cut you in two and destroy you both” (Dan. 13:59), how much more will such things be said to you, unless you take heed for yourself!

[Note: Col. 0899D. Above Lucifer likewise uses *enim* (“for”).]

[Note: Col. 0899D. “And you” is added above by Lucifer himself; there he also has “stands ready” for “stands.”]

Do you not know that it is written: “Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it” (Luke 11:28)?

[Note: Col. 0899D. The Ancient Version omits “it.”]

This had slipped from your heart, bound by the darkness of error, when you commanded an innocent man to be condemned. For, unless I am mistaken, the sacred Law everywhere declares that the innocent and righteous person must not be condemned. And because you commanded this thing contrary to God’s precept, we count you among those whom the Lord strikes in the Gospel:

> “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, because you are unmarked tombs, and people walk over them without knowing it.” (Luke 11:44)

[Note: Col. 0899D. Ancient Version: “Woe to you because … unmarked … walking over.”]

Those whom you drew into loving you, sacrilegious man, did not know—because through your efforts they had not perceived it—that you were a tomb full of every uncleanness; they thought you a human being. But we, immediately when you began to impose on the bishops the necessity of condemning an absent man, at once declared that you were a worshipper of injustice and a persecutor of justice.

Again, when we, the envoys of the blessed Church, pressed you to condemn Arius’s sect, you declared that sect rather to be catholic; and we foretold that you were the forerunner of Antichrist.

[Note: Col. 0899D. Lucifer presided over the Synod of Milan as Liberius’s legate, together with Pancratius and Hilary, clerics of the Roman Church.]

When you deign to persecute Christians and to kill them, Constantius, you make yourself like those to whom the Lord says:

> “Woe to you who build the tombs of the prophets, while your fathers killed them. Thus you bear witness—not consenting to the deeds of your fathers—that they indeed killed them, but you built their tombs. Therefore I send prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute, so that the blood of every prophet, shed from the foundation of the world until this generation, may be required—from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, it shall be required of this generation.” (Luke 11:47)

[Note: Col. 0899D. Ancient Version: “Surely you testify that you agree.”]

[Note: Col. 0899D. Latinus correctly reads “you” for “not,” and Galandius follows him.]

[Note: Col. 0899D. Ancient Version: “They themselves … build.” Sabatier likewise has “build.”]

[Note: Col. 0899D–0900D. Ancient Version: “For this reason the wisdom of God also said: ‘I shall send to you … and they will kill and persecute them, so that the blood of all … generation … righteous Abel … shall be required of this generation.’”]

You are understood to belong to them from this: although you restore the memorials of blessed martyrs, you nonetheless shed the blood of the servants of God’s only Son. Return, Constantius, to God’s house; be a Christian, lest, found outside the Church, you remain forever as you are today among those whom the Lord strikes, saying:

> “Strive to enter through the narrow door. For I tell you, many seek to enter and will not be able. When the master of the house rises and shuts the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’ He will answer, ‘I do not know where you are from.’ Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.’ But he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from; depart from me, all workers of iniquity.’ There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets entering the kingdom of God, but yourselves cast outside.” (Luke 13:24)

[Note: Col. 0900D. Latinus and Sabatier, from their edition, read “will seek.” Ancient Version: “Through the narrow gate … seek to enter and were not able.” Our edition agrees with the Corbie manuscript cited by Sabatier.]

[Note: Col. 0900D. For “has shut.” Tilius. The use of *cludo* for *claudo* occurs elsewhere. La Cerda. Ancient Version: “But when he has entered … and shut … his.” The Greek, with Lucifer, has *egerthē* [ἐγερθῇ], “has risen.” Sabatier reads “has shut” for “shut.”]

[Note: Col. 0900D. Ancient Version: “knock at the door … he will say to you: ‘I do not know from where,’ etc.”]

[Note: Col. 0900D. The Ancient Version adds “and in the synagogues,” but this is absent from the Greek.]

[Note: Col. 0900D. Ancient Version: “I do not know you … depart.”]

[Note: Col. 0900D. Vatican manuscript and Ancient Version read “when you see.”]

Do not think yourself so secure that you allow yourself to hear these words among them, especially since you see that you have been more wicked than one to whom it may deservedly be said, “Depart from me, worker of iniquity.” You will be, Constantius, if you choose to remain in this malevolence of yours, among that carnal people to whom it is said, “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you” (Luke 13:34). You will be among them, I say, because you persecute those who exhort you to win God’s favor, just as they persecuted the prophets and apostles.

Again, the defense of truth demands that the reason be sought from you why you commanded an absent man to be condemned. Tell me, please: do you order this to be done rightly or wrongly? If you say rightly, I suppose you will appeal to the deed of blessed Paul, because he wrote to the Corinthians that he had already punished the sinner whom he had discovered to have sinned grievously. Let us now see whether you, brute beast, possessing only a human body but a beastly mind, acted as the Apostle acted; whether you handled the matter in the same order as he who said:

> “It is actually reported among you that there is sexual immorality, and such immorality as is not even among the Gentiles: that someone has his father’s wife. And you are puffed up, rather than mourning, so that he who has done this deed might be removed from among you. For I, though absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged as though present the one who has so acted: when you are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, to deliver such a man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.” (1 Cor. 5:1)

[Note: Col. 0900D. Ancient Version: “Certainly … fornication, and such fornication … someone [with] his father’s … from the midst … For I indeed, as … spirit … in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ … such a one to Satan … on the day of the Lord Jesus Christ.”]

You say, I suppose: “And I for that reason commanded you to condemn an absent man, because the Apostle too had condemned one.” First of all, catholic men had reported the matter to the blessed Apostle—men whom he knew to be faithful, whom he had proved devoted to God, and whose entire holy Corinthian Church he knew to be a witness. You, by contrast, along with your fellow-sacrilegists, hateful-to-God heretics acting as accusers, deigned to press us to condemn a man in his absence.

[Note: Col. 0901D. Vatican manuscript: “You, darkness, along with your fellow-sacrilegists,” etc.]

Then, when you hear the Apostle say, “When you are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of the Lord Jesus, to deliver such a man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh” (1 Cor. 5:4), why did you refuse when we said to you: “We shall go at our own expense to the people over whom he was divinely appointed; we shall hear the man himself. Only provide catholic accusers in accordance with the command of the sacred Law”? Why did you refuse? Why, as though we were gladiators and not bishops, did you devote yourself merely to fulfilling your wishes, so that we might kill the man whose blood you had long thirsted for?

[Note: Col. 0901D. “Our Lord Jesus Christ.” Lucifer himself has this above.]

[Note: Col. 0901D. “Darkness,” singular, though not in ordinary usage, is used for the plural “darknesses,” as he uses “your work” for “your works.” Tilius and La Cerda. Lucifer likes this manner of speaking; likewise below: “If we had followed you, darkness.” Galandius.]

Meanwhile, you ought to know that you, wretched man, have been delivered to Satan for your murders and sacrilege, just as that man found guilty of that offence among the Corinthians.
