For your past and present deeds are no lesser deaths; so that if the Holy Spirit declares through the mouth of the blessed Apostle that he delivered that man to Satan for destruction, he surely did not fail to deliver you as soon as you committed such grave crimes.

For if it were otherwise, you would certainly remember that the Apostle said: “You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of human beings” (1 Cor. 7:23). You would never have dared to compel God’s priests to condemn a man unheard. For I, who was bought with a price and, liberated from the law of sin, became a servant of righteousness, ought not, while living under the law of righteousness, to have had a burden imposed upon me by you so that I might again become a servant of wickedness and injustice.

Therefore, a burden was imposed by you because you had been delivered to Satan for destruction on account of murders and sacrilege. If you had not been delivered to Satan, you would have kept in mind what the Apostle wrote to Timothy:

> “We know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, knowing this: that law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the unrighteous and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the wicked and profane, parricides and matricides, the sexually immoral, those who lie with males, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is opposed to sound doctrine, according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God which was entrusted to me.” (1 Tim. 1:8)

[Note: Col. 0901D. Ancient Version: “it … knowing … for sinners, wicked … parricides and matricides, those who lie with males, murderers, the sexually immoral.”]

If, since you denied the Son of God, you have not been delivered to Satan for destruction, how, passing over so many things that could have restrained you from so great a crime, to these …
have you deigned to omit the things that ought to be done, which can remove all these things known to belong to sound doctrine? You who do these things contrary to sound doctrine—who outlaw, torture, deport, send to prison, and kill—tell me, I beg you, whether you differ from that King Herod whose butchery Holy Scripture describes in these words:

“At that time King Herod laid hands upon some of the Church in order to harm them. He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword; and when he saw that this pleased the Jews, [Col. 0902B] he proceeded to seize Peter also. Now these were the days of Unleavened Bread. When he had seized him, he put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of soldiers, intending after Passover to bring him before the people. Peter, however, was being kept in prison. But prayer was being made most earnestly to the Lord by the Church for him. And when Herod was about to bring him out, that very night Peter was sleeping between soldiers, bound with two chains; and guards before the door were keeping the prison. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood there, and light shone from him in that place. Striking Peter’s side, he woke him, saying: ‘Rise quickly.’ And he rose, and the chains fell from his hands” (Acts 12:1).

[Note: [Col. 0901D] For “some.” Til[lius]. Old Latin: “But at that time Herod laid hands … to afflict some.” “To harm” for “to kill”; La Cerda.]

[Note: [Col. 0901D] Old Latin: “He killed … and, seeing that it was pleasing … he proceeded to seize … And having seized him … handing him over … to guard him.”]

[Note: [Col. 0901D] Greek: ἀναγαγεῖν, “bring up.” Old Latin: “bring forward.”]

[Note: [Col. 0902D] Old Latin: “Peter indeed was being kept … But prayer was made unceasingly … to God … And when he intended to bring [him out] … Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound … and guards before the door were keeping watch … and light shone in the dwelling: he struck,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0902D] “And he rose” is absent from the Old Latin.]

And below:

“And when he had passed the first and second guards, he came to the iron gate leading [Col. 0902C] into the city, which opened of itself for them. When they had gone out, they proceeded one street, and immediately the angel departed from him. Then Peter, coming to himself, said: ‘Now I know truly that the Lord has sent his angel and delivered me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the Jewish people’” (ibid., 10).

[Note: [Col. 0902D] Old Latin: “And having passed the first guard and the second, they came … which of its own accord … And going out they passed … having returned to himself, he said … hand.”]

[Note: [Col. 0902D] Greek: Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι, “Now I know truly that.” But Lucifer read the words transposed, ὅτι ἀληθῶς, “that truly”: “Now I know that truly, and not merely in a vision, the Lord has sent [his angel].” Chrysostom too is reported to have read it thus. Galandius. See Chrysostom, Homily 26 on Acts.]

“When day came, there was no little disturbance among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter. And when Herod had searched for him and not found him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away” (ibid., 18).

[Note: [Col. 0902D] Old Latin: “No small affliction.” Greek has only τάραχος, “disturbance,” as does Lucifer, and ἐγένετο, “came to be,” whereas the Old Latin has *factus est*, “there was.”]

[Note: [Col. 0902D] Old Latin: “Searching for him and not finding him, investigating.”]

We see that you are like him in every respect, both in cruelty and in sacrilege. For as he killed the blessed apostle James, so you have killed a vast multitude of believers, who believe as the apostle James believed. As he persecuted God’s only [Col. 0903A] Son in the apostle James, so do you both in those whom you have already killed and in us whom you persecute.

Again we instruct and exhort you: return to God’s Church, and cease now to persecute Athanasius, or us who act against your heresy, lest you begin to perish after the example of this Herod. Holy Scripture speaks of his destruction, saying:

“He went down from Judaea to Caesarea [and] stayed there. Now he was hostile to the Tyrians and Sidonians. But they came to him in a body; and after persuading Blastus, who was in charge of the king’s bedchamber, they asked for peace, because their regions were supplied from the royal territory. On an appointed day Herod, clothed in royal apparel, sat on the tribunal and addressed them. And the people cried out: ‘The voice of a god, and not of a man!’ Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give honour to God; and, crawling with worms, [Col. 0903B] he expired” (ibid., 19).

[Note: [Col. 0903D] Sabatier reads “into Caesarea.” Old Latin: “Going down from Judaea, he stayed in Caesarea … Herod was hostile in mind … to the Sidonians; but with one accord … the bedchamber … cities … clothed in royal apparel and seated … they cried aloud: ‘The voice of a god’ … because he had not given glory to God, and, consumed by worms …”]

Did you not know—you who wish to appear learned in the Law—that the apostle John said, when you said, “Condemn the innocent”:

“By this we know that we have known him: if we keep his commandments. But whoever says, ‘I have known him,’ and does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. But whoever has kept his word, truly in such a person the love of God has been perfected” (1 John 2:3).

[Note: [Col. 0903D] See the note in *One Must Die for the Son of God*.]

[Note: [Col. 0903D] “The blessed Apostle.” Vatican manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0903D] “When you said.” Same manuscript. The sense is: “Did you not know, when you said, ‘Condemn the innocent,’ that John had said,” etc. *Ut* (“when”) is superfluous.]

[Note: [Col. 0903D] Greek: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ἐγνώκαμεν αὐτόν, etc. Old Latin: “And by this we know him, if we have kept [his commandments]. He who says that he has known [him] … keeps … has kept … in this the love of God has been perfected.”]

You command what is contrary to God’s command; and the apostle, on the contrary, says that whoever does not keep his precepts has not even known him. For, he says, “If he says, ‘I have known him,’ and does not keep his commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him” (ibid., 4).

[Note: [Col. 0903D] Above Lucifer likewise has “in this.”]

You want us to be liars; you want us to be found murderers, doubtless so that we may not be found to be Christians. For neither liars nor murderers are Christians. The apostle says: “Whoever has kept his word, truly the love of God has been perfected in them” [Col. 0903C] (ibid., 5); while you, apostate and forerunner of antichrist, say: “Whoever does not keep his commandments shall live.”

Further: “Whoever says that he is in the light,” he says, “and hates his brother, is still in darkness. But whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no stumbling-block in him. But whoever hates his brother walks in [Note: [Col. 0903D] Old Latin: “For he who is in darkness walks in darkness; and they have blinded his eyes.”] darkness and does not know where he is going, because darkness has blinded his heart” (ibid., 9).

What can you, a man of darkness, say to this? Why, set in darkness rather than in the light, do you say: “Hate with me the one whom I unjustly hate; share in my madness; become murderers as I too am”?

Then, if he says that one who hates his brother walks in darkness [Col. 0904A] (ibid., 11) and does not know where he is going—plainly because the darkness of violence has blinded his eyes—what if someone kills his brother? What if he is a murderer? Yet you think nothing of being a murderer, though you are found to have shed the blood of so many servants of God.

[Note: [Col. 0904D] “Murderer.” Latin [version] and Galandius.]

You dare command God’s priests to do deeds pleasing only to your father the devil and to you Arians, his sons. The most holy apostle likewise exhorts us to hold to the path of righteousness, that we may deserve to be established in everlasting rest; but you, most wise man, compel us to come with you to eternal torments:

“Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever does righteousness is righteous [Note: [Col. 0904D] Old Latin: “Little children … deceive.”], but whoever commits sin is of the devil, because the devil sins from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested: that he might destroy the works of the devil” (ibid. 3:7).

[Note: [Col. 0904D] The Old Latin adds: “just as he is righteous,” though these words are lacking in certain manuscripts.]

[Note: [Col. 0904D] Old Latin: “Because from the beginning … For this purpose [he was] manifested … might destroy.” Lucifer himself below has *idcirco*, “for this purpose,” in place of *ad hoc*.]

Therefore, since the apostle says [Col. 0904B] that sin is from the devil, and you compel us to commit capital crimes, what else can I call you except the devil’s agent? I see you so loving his cause, so serving his interest, that you desire all of us to be found on his side. For why do you compel every worshipper of God to pass over to him, unless you have chosen to favour that same party?

You hear the blessed apostle say, “For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil” (ibid., 8); yet you urge God’s worshippers to complete the devil’s work. When you do these things, do you not see that you have made yourself an assailant of him who destroyed the devil’s works? But it is no wonder that you have chosen to have rebuilt through yourself, the devil’s attendant, those things which God’s only Son destroyed, since you did not hesitate to deny [Col. 0904C] the very one who destroyed the devil’s work.

This is why you count it nothing to shed innocent blood: denying the lover of the innocent and defender of his worshippers, you have joined yourself to him to whom Judas Iscariot joined himself. Therefore, if you cannot deny that shedding the blood of a righteous man is a work of the devil, it is certainly clear that you have performed the devil’s works and have urged us to perform them.

John, most devoted to God, speaks further so that brotherly love may be kept inviolate:

“By this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest. Everyone who is not righteous is not from God, nor is anyone who does not love his brother; for this is the message [Note: [Col. 0904D] Old Latin: “In this the children [of God and of the devil] are manifest … from God … does not love … because … the message which you heard from the beginning.” Greek: ἣν ἠκούσατε, “which you heard,” as does Lucifer, who below has “from the origin” for “from the beginning.”] which you heard from the beginning: that we should love [Note: [Col. 0904D] Old Latin: “Let us love one another, not … was, and killed … And for what reason did he kill [him]? Because his works … but his brother’s … world … because we have passed from … because we love … Whoever does not love.”] one another, and not be like Cain, who [Note: [Col. 0904D] Vatican manuscript: “Cain was of the evil one.” So in Greek, which omits *who*, as Lucifer does a little further below.] was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because [Col. 0905A] his own works were evil, but his brother’s righteous. Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates us. We know that we have passed from death to life because we love the brothers. But whoever does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him” (ibid., 10).

Since, then, everyone found to hate his brother is called a murderous son of the devil, is compared with Cain the fratricide, and is declared to remain in death, why did you compel me to perform this deed, which would have made me, like Cain, a fratricide and a son of the devil, and would have made me remain in everlasting death? You now see that I have passed from death to life, since God has already placed me among those whom he has deemed worthy to call sons.

[Note: [Col. 0905D] From the quoted Johannine text I would read “sons of God.” Galandius.]

Why did you wish me to become Cain, darkness, and a son of the devil? How have I injured you? In what matters have I stood as an enemy to your salvation, that you should desire such harm to be done to me? Why do we repeat these things? Unless it is that you may at last understand how ignorant you are of what is good. For if you knew, you would never yourself have committed so great a crime, nor would you urge us to perpetrate it.

Meanwhile, I beg you, say why you persecute the bishop of God’s house. For the apostle says that whoever hates his brother is a murderer (ibid., 15). If you wish us to bear the name of murderers, why do you hate your brother? Prove Athanasius worthy of hatred; make known what evils he has done, so that he may deserve to be hated even by us all. Certainly you will not produce any unjust deed he has committed which makes him hateful. Since these things are so, it necessarily follows [Col. 0905C] that you hate him for this reason: your work is evil, but Athanasius’s is righteous. For you wish to kill him because he did not imitate you in being wicked, criminal, and sacrilegious.

This is manifestly so. For when the glorious apostle sets Cain and Abel in comparison, you seem to me to be Cain, whereas Athanasius is Abel, saying: “By this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest. Everyone who is not righteous is not from God, nor anyone who does not love his brother, because this [Note: [Col. 0905D] This same Lucifer has above, “This is the message,” and “his own works” instead of “that man’s works.” See [the note].] is the message which you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another and not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because that man’s works were evil, but his brother’s righteous” (ibid., 10).

Nor should you doubt that your works are evil and Athanasius’s righteous. For you are a murderer, a destroyer of God’s religion, a denier of God’s only Son, an assailant of apostolic faith, a founder of Arian idolatry. Athanasius, on the other hand, remains so steadfast in the fear of God that, so far as can be seen, he is found to have committed nothing that could separate him from those most beloved by God.

[Col. 0906A] Since these things are so, we exhort you to love yourself in Athanasius. You remember what is written: “You shall love your neighbour as yourself”; and, “Whoever loves his neighbour has fulfilled the Law” (Matt. 22:39; Rom. 13:8). For as you hate yourself in him, not knowing that it is evil unjustly to hate a righteous man, so you will begin to love yourself in him if this ill will of yours is changed into goodwill. Then you may be delivered from the darkness in which the blessed apostle says that you abide:

“Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates us. We know that we have passed from death to life because we love the brothers. But whoever does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer has life [Note: [Col. 0905D] The same Lucifer above has “eternal life.”] abiding in him” (1 John 3:13).

Do not dare any longer to say, “Condemn [Col. 0906B] the innocent,” you man who have no life abiding in you, you who have not yet passed from death to life. For if you had passed over—that is, if you had believed in God’s only Son as we do—you would not have chosen to be a murderer, lest you should plainly begin again to return to death. Thus, in a twofold manner, being without hope of life, you have deigned to command God’s priests to kill an innocent man.

But perhaps you think [Note: [Col. 0905D] “You try.” Latin [version] and Galandius.] to say: “I love those who love God, and I hate those who hate him.” Yet you cannot say this of Athanasius, since it is rather established that you hate God, because you have abandoned him and passed over to idolatry.

Therefore, because you persecute no fault in God’s priest, but righteousness alone, God’s religion alone, it remains for you further to see what this blessed apostle John commanded us—whom you urged to kill innocent persons—to be [Col. 0906C] toward our fellow servants:

“He laid down [his] life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren” (ibid., 16).

[Note: [Col. 0905D] Old Latin: “For us,” and omits “our.” Sabatier read *propter*, “for,” alone in his copy.]

The apostle commands me to lay down my life for a brother, while you, a slave of antichrist, command me to kill my brother. And again: “Let us have [Note: [Col. 0905D] Sabatier reads “We have.” Old Latin: “We have … whatever we may ask … because we keep his commandments … [and] do what is pleasing to him in his sight,” etc.] confidence before God, and whatever we ask we shall receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do before him what is pleasing in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, [Note: [Col. 0905D] The Latin adds: “And this is his commandment, that we believe [Col. 0906D] and love,” etc. So the Old Latin and Vulgate, in which after “believe” occur the words “in the name of his Son Jesus Christ,” which Lucifer cites after “we do.”] and let us love one another, as he gave us commandment …” (ibid., 21).

But how shall I be heard by him in every prayer, when I do not keep his commandment? For he commanded me to love my brother, not to kill him. And below: “Beloved, [Note: [Col. 0906D] Old Latin: “Most beloved, let us love one another, because love …”] let us love one another, because love is from God” [Col. 0906D] (ibid. 4:7).

And again: “Whoever does not love his brother [Note: [Col. 0906D] “Brother” is absent from the Old Latin, which reads thus: “Whoever … because God is love. In this the love [of God] was manifested … because … [he sent his] only-begotten [Son] into this world … him … love—not that we loved, but because he loved us and sent … a propitiator for sins … Most beloved,” etc.] does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God was manifested in us: God sent his only Son into the world, that we might live through him. In this is love: not that we loved [Col. 0907A] God, but that he loved us [Note: [Col. 0907C] Sabatier omits “us.”] and sent his Son as the expiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we too ought to love one another” (ibid., 8).

Again: “If anyone says [Note: [Col. 0907C] Old Latin: “Should say, ‘I love God.’”] that he loves God and hates his brother, he is a liar. For whoever does not love his brother, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen” (ibid., 20).

[Note: [Col. 0907C] Greek: ἑώρακε, “has seen.” The Latin corrects it to *videt*, “sees,” from the Vulgate and Old Latin, in which: “For whoever does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God whom he does not see?”]

Again: “We have this commandment from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother” (ibid., 21).

And again: “By this [Note: [Col. 0907C] Vatican manuscript: “And again: By this,” etc.] we know that [Note: [Col. 0907C] Sabatier reads “because.”] we love the children of God: when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God [Note: [Col. 0907C] The Latin adds, from Greek, Old Latin, and Vulgate: “that we keep his commandments,” etc., which Lucifer later [Col. 0907D] cites almost in the same place. Galandius supposes that the repeated words “his commandments” caused a copyist to omit the preceding words; but one should not too readily attribute to a copyist omissions which Lucifer himself knowingly made.]: and his commandments are not burdensome” (ibid. 5:2).

Consider these few things out of many, and you will discover into what darkness you have dragged us, you man of darkness. “By this we know,” he says, “that [Col. 0907B] [Note: [Col. 0907D] The same Lucifer above has “when.”] we love the children of God: when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments” (ibid.). Yet you deign to drive me to scatter these commandments and to establish against them other commands, set forth through you by the devil’s prompting. How can I be found to love God when through you I am found to have become an enemy of his commandments?

From what deeds do you seem to me to be anything other than one of those tares destined for fire, of which the Lord says: “Therefore, just as the tares are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather [Note: [Col. 0907D] Old Latin: “will collect.”] out of his kingdom all stumbling-blocks and those who commit iniquity, and they will cast [Note: [Col. 0907D] Vatican manuscript: “they cast.”] them into the furnace [Note: [Col. 0907D] Til[lius] and the Latin [version], with Greek, Old Latin, and Vulgate, read *caminum*, “furnace,” rather than *in camino*, “into the furnace.” Tillius’s objection to *in camino* is pointless: grammatically one may perfectly well say *in camino*. The editor supplies instances: Plautus, *Amphitruo*, *in mentem fuit*, and *Bacchides*, “Does it come to your mind?” Aulus Gellius, Book I, chapter 7, cites this passage and defends Cicero’s wording in *For the Manilian Law*: “when you know that your harbours were in the pirates’ power”; and in *For Quinctius*: “the affair came to be in a legal summons.” Petronius: “the affair is in dispute,” a phrase Turnebus calls elegant and Ciceronian. [Col. 0908C] Manilius, Book V: “when he came into the region,” as Cicero says, “I came into the Senate.” Plautus, *Epidicus*: “to cling in love,” as Camerarius reads; Henri Estienne defends Plautus’s phrase *in mentem fuit* at length. Read Taubman on Plautus’s *Amphitruo*. Read him also on the same comedy, where he defends *interrumpam in aedibus*, “I shall interrupt in the house,” and *pergam in aedibus*, “I shall proceed in the house.” Ulpian: “suppose that the woman remained in precarious possession.” Tertullian, *On the Prescription against Heretics*, chapter 8: *foris actum*, “done outside”; Junius reads *foras*, “outward,” in the phrase *quem in focum*, but Pamelius reads *foris* from the ancient copies. In Holy Scripture occurs “let decay enter into my bones.” Thus the ancients used these nouns indifferently; from this usage [Col. 0908D] Lucifer said, “They will cast them into the furnace of burning fire”; and below: “Had you forgotten that the Lord said to Blessed Peter, ‘Put your sword back in its place’?” La Cerda.] of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father” (Matt. 13:[Col. 0907C] 40).

You see that, if at your heretical urging [Note: [Col. 0908D] Equivalent to *satagente*, “urging vehemently.” La Cerda.] I condemned the innocent, I should be destined to Gehenna with you. For we could not attain God’s kingdom, in which we might shine like the sun [Note: [Col. 0908D] After the word “sun,” inserting a comma where the old edition had a full stop, we have joined the separated clauses into one sense on the authority of Latinius, who substitutes *aut*, “or,” for *autem*, “but.”], if [Col. 0908A] we had either committed murder or violated the apostolic faith.

Rejoice still [Note: [Col. 0908D] Latin [version]: “Rejoice still.”] to live amid these evils; refuse to recognize the evils you do; and you will undoubtedly find yourself among those wicked persons whom the Lord designates as destined for fire, saying: “The angels will go out [Note: [Col. 0908D] Old Latin: “will go out … from the midst of the righteous … them … burning fire.” The Claromontanus manuscript cited by Sabatier has *exient*, “will go out”; Greek and all other manuscripts lack “burning,” as does Lucifer’s version.] and separate the wicked from the company of the righteous, and cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth” (ibid., 49).

You, a member of the devil, count it as nothing to persecute the servants of God’s only Son, supposing that you could lead the whole holy Church into scandal. But consider what God promises you and all your fellow-sacrilegious persons:

“Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me; but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, [Col. 0908B] it would be better for him to have a millstone hung round his neck and to be sunk in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of stumbling-blocks! For stumbling-blocks must come; yet woe to that person through whom the stumbling-block comes. And if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you” (ibid. 18:5).

[Note: [Col. 0908D] Old Latin: “these little ones … be plunged into the deep … cut off.”]

And below: “See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven” (ibid., 10).

[Note: [Col. 0908D] Old Latin: “of these little ones who believe in me”; but the words “who believe in me” are absent from Greek and Vulgate, as from Lucifer.]

Therefore, you who not only despise those who believe in his divine majesty, but actually kill them—what reward will he whom you deny render to you? He who said that it would be better for you to have an ass’s millstone hung around your neck and be cast into the depth of the sea than to cause one believer in him to stumble, or to despise one of those who will possess the kingdom of heaven—what will he render to you, who for this reason deserved to be cut off from the members of his holy Church: because you are the one through whom [Col. 0909A] the devil has brought scandals into God’s people in our days?

Although you stir up scandals, you have deceived only those who did not know that you had already withered like a stream cut off from its source, like a branch broken from a tree. But we who know you to be outside the Church, who see you as an enemy of God’s only Son, and who know you to be dead, see—with God’s help—your efforts beneath our feet. For we know that the dead cannot rule the living.

But do you say that you live in Christ? How can you prove it, when you deny him? For none can live unless they confess him to be true God and true Son of God. How are you alive when you persecute us precisely because we confess ourselves to be his servants? Or do you persecute us for another reason? Have you perhaps found [Col. 0909B] that we have wronged you, and are therefore so hostile to us? We do not recall having sinned against you. For how can it be proved that we have sinned against you, when we repeatedly urge you to come from death to life?

[Note: [Col. 0909C] For *saepius urgemus*, “we urge repeatedly.” Tillius and La Cerda.]

Yet, if you think that we have wronged you, receive what the Lord commanded you to do toward us:

“If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between yourself and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not listen to you, take with you one [Note: [Col. 0909D] Vatican manuscript, with Greek and Old Latin: “with you still one.”] or two others, so that every word may stand by the mouth of two or three witnesses. And if he does not listen to them, tell it to the Church; and if he does not listen to the Church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector” (ibid., 15).

Since you have not done what the Lord commanded to be done, since you not only [Note: [Col. 0909D] Latin [version]: “You alone [did not act] between yourself and us.” Better: “Since you not only did not admonish between yourself and us, proving, in the presence of those persons—that is, ourselves—that Athanasius, one of us, was guilty, but compelled,” etc. Latinius thinks *convinceres*, “you might prove,” should be read for *convincens*, “proving”; but the participle can quite properly be retained. Galandius follows Latinius.] did not admonish between yourself and us, proving in our presence that Athanasius, one of [Col. 0909C] us, was guilty, but compelled him to be condemned unheard by us, his fellow priests; since you deprived him of a hearing, how can you justly accuse us, when we have sinned against you, though you have fulfilled none of these commands of the Lord?

[Note: [Col. 0909D] Constantius did not summon Athanasius to the Council of Milan. Athanasius, having little confidence in letters of Pope Liberius brought to him at Alexandria, since there was suspicion that the Arians had forged them, did not even come into Italy. Fearing that traps were being prepared for him in the emperor’s palace, he sent envoys to Constantius to reconcile him to himself—but in vain. For, as Athanasius himself testifies in the *Letter to the Solitaries*, Constantius compelled bishops in individual cities—namely in Gaul and Italy—to change their judgment in the case of Athanasius; and, after refusing him a hearing at the Council of Milan, ordered the bishops to subscribe against Athanasius.]

Why do you persecute us so fiercely, when you are rather guilty of transgression? You did not act toward us as God’s only Son gave you commandments, but did everything as our enemy the devil pleased. For such counsel is his, such a will is his: that a man should be condemned unheard, that one absent should be killed, that innocent blood should be shed—when, I say, [Col. 0910A] you did not handle the matter in the way the Lord commanded you to handle it.

You dared to bring a charge before the blessed Church; you dared to say: “Athanasius has sinned, and must be condemned by all, [and cut off from] communion.” But what will you try to say? “He sinned against God.” Yet it cannot be found that he sinned against God, since neither you nor your fellow-sacrilegious sons of the whorish Arian heresy can be admitted as witnesses against a Catholic bishop. For the Lord spoke of three Catholic witnesses, servants of his majesty, so that the blessed Church might believe them—not you profane men, born of adultery from a harlot.

Otherwise, if we do not understand this command of the Lord in this way, worshippers of Saturn and of every idol could also be admitted as witnesses against members of God’s household; and your fellow blasphemers, Jews abandoned by God and placed [Col. 0910B] without light, as you are, could be admitted as well. For if you heretics—indeed, those of every sect—are to be admitted as witnesses against Christians, Gentiles and Jews must be admitted too. For whether Jews, Gentiles, or you heretics, you stand outside the Lord’s Church without God, just as all those then stood who were not in the ark of most holy Noah. For as those who stood outside the ark could not be saved, so neither can you; but you will perish thus unless, believing in God’s only Son, you remain with us in his holy Church.

Therefore, since neither you nor your fellow blasphemers can be witnesses, how did you, most foolish king, bring it about that a man of utter innocence was condemned, and indeed by his fellow priests? I add this: you had already accused him of being a murderer at Sardica, in a synod of Catholics, [Col. 0910C] and your iniquity could not prove it.

[Note: [Col. 0910D] At the Council of Sardica in the year 347, Athanasius, already repeatedly accused by heretics of killing Bishop Arsenius, was acquitted by the fathers of the synod.]

I add that you yourself gave letters to the Church of the Alexandrians affirming that he was a righteous man and a Catholic bishop.

[Note: [Col. 0910D] These letters survive in Athanasius, *Apology II*, and in Socrates, Book II, chapter 23. In them Constantius writes that he is restoring to them a man universally known for uprightness of life and moral integrity—when Athanasius, who had been exiled in Gaul, was recalled to the Alexandrian Church.]

Finally, even if [Note: [Col. 0910D] That is, “if.”] Athanasius had sinned, he should have been expelled by the people committed to his charge, so that that people might seek from among its own body another worthy to be made bishop for them; he should not, however, have been sought with the sword by you, the emperor.

But when [Note: [Col. 0910D] This passage is corrupt, though its sense is readily apparent. Tillius. Latinius emends it thus: “But when you, fearing no injustice, restored nothing, and sent in place of the Catholic [bishop],” etc. Yet it seems preferable to interpret the passage thus: “When you, in place of the innocent Athanasius—against whom a Catholic, that is, a Catholic bishop, had established nothing true, that is, nothing among the accusations brought against him by the Arians—sent,” etc.] you sent your fellow-sacrilegious George in the place of the innocent man, against whom no Catholic had established anything true, and inflicted such outrages and punishments upon those unwilling to be stained by his sacrilege, that you outlawed many, sent them into exile and to the mines, killed very many also, and even today do not cease to do things which scarcely even enraged enemies, most savage barbarians, would do to those unwilling to accept your blasphemy, which is also George’s—how do you suppose that you can be regarded as a Christian, when you appear fiercer than the most savage wild beasts and more brutal than every animal?

[Note: [Col. 0910D] See what has already been said about George, and what we shall say a little below. On the devastation inflicted upon the Catholics of Alexandria who recoiled from communion with George, Athanasius says in *Apology I*: “One could see, after the week of Easter, virgins thrown into prison, bishops led away bound by soldiers, houses of widows and orphans plundered … Christians dragged away by night and houses sealed up, and clerics’ brothers brought into danger in place of their brothers … in the week after holy Pentecost … on the very Lord’s Day … virgins brought close to the fires of a blazing pyre … all the others whom they seized, together with the virgins … they banished … bodies of the dead left unburied … bishops from Egypt and Africa compelled to flee and go into exile … whom they carried off with such harshness that some met death on the road, others in exile.” These acts took place in 356, after the Council of Milan and Athanasius’s expulsion from his see.]

You dared to say that Athanasius ought to be struck down, not seeing that you Arians were then punished, and indeed by God’s power, when you planned to introduce idolatry into the Lord’s Church.

But perhaps you will still say: “Athanasius wronged me.” Leaving aside the fact that you are a liar even in this, did you not know what is written about how the Lord commanded you to deal with those who wrong you, that you should persecute him with the sword?

Then Peter came to him [Col. 0911B] and said to him: “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? Up to seven times?” He said to him: “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to [Note: [Col. 0911D] He omits *up to* a little below, as Tertullian also does in *On Prayer* and *On Patience*. Old Latin: “I shall forgive him … Jesus said to him … seventy times.”] seventy times seven.”

(Ibid. 21). Are you ashamed to hear Athanasius called your brother? If you profess yourself a Christian, you ought to call all Christians brothers—indeed, not Athanasius alone, but even those whom you see begging for alms. For all who are established in the Church of the Lord are one in him, with whom there is no respect of persons. Yet you would do well if you did not wish him to be called your brother. For since you are a son of pestilence and he is one of the sons of light; since you are the slave of our enemy and he is the servant of God, it is most unjust that you, the forerunner of Antichrist, should be called the brother of a man of God.

If you saw that he had committed any offense against you, you ought immediately to have forgiven him, so that God might forgive you your own sins. But now, since because of your obstinacy and malice you could not forgive, receive, you who have made void the Lord’s command, what may be set before you:

Then Peter came to him and said [Note: Above, “said to him”]: “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? Up to seven times?” He says to him: “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but seventy times seven. Therefore the kingdom of heaven has been made like [Note: The Old Latin version omits “has been made like”] a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. And when he began to settle accounts, one was brought before him who owed ten [Note: Most manuscripts in Sabatier: “ten thousand,” with Lucifer; Greek: μυρίων, “ten thousand.” Old Latin: “one hundred.”] thousand talents. But since he had nothing [Note: Old Latin: “He had … his lord … that he might repay … he besought his lord … But moved with compassion … forgave him the debt. Having departed … And his fellow servant fell down … and all … were greatly [troubled], and related … had happened … him … ought you not therefore … to have mercy [the word “also” also omitted] … on your fellow servant?”] with which to repay, his lord ordered him to be sold, with his wife, children, and all that he had, and the debt repaid. Then that servant fell down and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’ But the lord of that servant, moved with pity, released [Note: With the Greek: ἀπέλυσεν αὐτὸν, καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ, “he released him and forgave him the loan.” Old Latin has only: “forgave him the debt.”] him and forgave him the debt.

“But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and, seizing him, he choked him, saying: ‘Pay what you owe.’ Then that servant fell down and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’ But he would not; rather, he went and put him into prison until he should repay the debt. When his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were deeply grieved; and they came and reported to their lord all that had happened. Then his lord summoned him and said: ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Ought you not also to have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?’ And his lord, angered, delivered him to the torturers until he should repay the entire debt. So also my Father who is in heaven will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from your hearts” (Ibid.).

What do you answer to this—you whose mind’s eyes have been altogether unable to see what the Lord commanded to be done? Where do you place the fact that Athanasius has sinned neither against you nor against God, but suffers persecution because he holds the apostolic faith, because he refuses to become sacrilegious as you are? You have resolved to kill the preacher of truth, desiring to place yourself in that rank in which are those whom the Lord in the Gospel identifies as killers of the prophets—and as those who would stretch out impious hands even against himself—when he declares:

“There was a householder who planted a vineyard and set a hedge [Note: Old Latin: “a hedge around it … in it a tower … his servants” (omitting “tenants”) … “another” … “he sent other servants, more than the first” … “Perhaps they will reverence” … “Let us kill him” … “They said” … “he will destroy [them], and the vineyard,” etc.] around it; and he dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to tenants, and went abroad. When the season of fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive his fruits. But the tenants seized his servants: one they beat, another they stoned, and another they killed. Again he sent to them more servants, and they did likewise to them. Finally he sent to them his only son, saying: ‘They will reverence my son.’ But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves: ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and [Note: Sabatier omits “and.”] we shall have his inheritance.’ And they seized him, killed him, and cast him [Note: In Calmet’s *Commentary on the Gospels*, among variant Gospel readings, “him” is omitted at this point in Lucifer’s text.] outside the vineyard. When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” They say [Note: Vatican manuscript: “He says to them.”] to him: “He will utterly destroy those wicked men, and lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will render him its fruit in their seasons” (Ibid., XXI, 23).

You greatly desire to be one of these, and you urged us to become partners in your crimes. For your counsels differ in no respect from the wicked counsels of those who are found to have slain the prophets and, finally, to have stretched out impious hands against the only Son of God. This is especially so because you reduce to nothing the sufferings of those blessed men sent to the tenants, maintaining that they were killed for him who “was when he was not”; whereas the sacred Scriptures proclaim that the only Son of God has always reigned and reigns with the Father. The divine writings reveal that the Father and his only Son possess one divinity [Note: Latin and Galland, deceived by faulty punctuation, read “having”; the text should be read: “he reigns with the Father; the Lord’s writings reveal [them] to possess one divinity.”]; yet you say that he for whom the glorious prophets were killed was made from nothing.

For if what you say is true, it follows that the blessed prophets were killed for a creature. And where then is the statement that the Lord is greatly angered against those who serve the creature rather than the Creator? If the blessed prophets were killed for a creature, how does God hold them most dear? How, because the Jews did not believe their words, are they today enemies of God? Why are the Jews enemies of God? Why are they found outside the Lord’s vineyard? Is it not because they were killers of the prophets; because the prophets preached the eternal God, Son of the eternal God; and because those who blaspheme with you not only refused to believe the prophets’ prophecy, but also killed those very prophets?

For what do you suppose the Jews persecuted in the prophets, if not the only Son of God—as also in the apostles and martyrs? Learn at least from yourself that what I say is true: for you too persecute the true Son of God in Athanasius and in us [Note: Tilius: “who.” Latin and Galland: “also,” incorrectly; the sense is: “you, who persecute the true Son of God in Athanasius and also in us.”]. Since this is so, you decreed that we should be joined to the murderers of the prophets, the shedders of righteous blood, your fellow-sacrilegious persons—that is, the Jews—since you are plainly their imitator.

For you commanded that, Athanasius having been condemned, we should also accept Arius’s faith, for no other purpose than that we might be equals of the Jews both in shedding the blood of the righteous and in denying the only Son of God—Jews of whom you are now a participant in every respect. For if they killed the prophets who spoke of the coming of the only Son of God, you kill those who believe as the prophets believed. But how long must I speak of these matters with an unbeliever? I have undertaken to show you that you are one of those to whom the Lord says: “Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruit” (Ibid., 43).

For you are not among this nation, which is found to produce the fruits of righteousness; consequently you must be declared one of those whom you hear to have been expelled from God’s kingdom because of their murder of the righteous and their unbelief. Recognize, from what you do, that you are among those whose wickedness the Lord exposes when he says: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son, and sent his servants to call those invited [Note: Old Latin: “to summon the invited.”] to the wedding” (Ibid., XXII, 2).

And below: “But they would not come. Again he sent [Note: Old Latin: “He sent other servants … fattened [animals] … are ready … But that king … burned their city … his servants … all whomsoever … the wedding [was filled] with those reclining … to see those reclining … garment … [Col. 0914D] garment … Then he said … him,” etc.] other servants, saying: ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my bulls and fattened beasts have been slaughtered, and all is ready. Come to the wedding.’ But they disregarded it and went away, one to his farm, another to his business. The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them. When the king heard this, he was enraged; and he sent his army, destroyed [them], those murderers, and burned their cities [Note: Sabatier reads “city.”]. Then he said to his servants: ‘The wedding is indeed ready, but those invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and summon to the wedding whomever you find.’ And the servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, bad and good; and the wedding was filled with guests reclining at table.

“But the king entered to see the guests reclining, and there he saw a man not clothed in a wedding garment. He said to him: ‘Friend, how did you come in here [Note: Later in the same work, Lucifer: “You came in without having a wedding garment.”] without a wedding garment?’ But he was silent. Then the king said to the attendants: ‘Take him by feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth’” (Ibid. 3).

Therefore, since you are without the wedding garment, Constantius, unless you turn back, you will eternally be like that man to whom it is said: “Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?” (Ibid. 12). Thus you will come into the outer darkness. Nor should you doubt that you will come into outer darkness, since you have already been wholly turned into darkness. For those who shed the righteous blood of the prophets and denied the only Son of God are called both darkness and sons of the devil. Since you yourself do these things, you too will remain a son of darkness and of the devil unless you provide for yourself.

“How,” you say, “can I provide for myself?” By ceasing to persecute us and accepting the apostolic faith. Unless you do this, you will always remain, as you now are, among those to whom it is said: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith [Note: “Faith” is carried over at Col. 0914D]. These things you ought to have done, without neglecting those others. Blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel” (Ibid., XXIII, 23). [Note: Latin has “swallowing”; Lucifer himself uses the same reading shortly below, also changing “but” to “and.” Yet without any alteration I would read *contra glutientes*, “against those who swallow,” separately, contrary to Galland, not very satisfactorily.]

If you do not deservedly hear these words with them, where is the just judgment that proceeds from you, who strive to kill a righteous man because he preaches the apostolic faith [Note: Tilius: “because,” in place of “why.”]? Where is just judgment in you, who persecute with all the powers of your empire those whom you see unwilling either to condemn a man unheard or to abandon the catholic faith, while loving those whom you know to have shed innocent blood with you and to have rejected evangelical faith? What mercy exists with you, what mercy established in you, which the holy law commanded to be shown? Surely it is that mercy which tortures, proscribes, deports, sends to prison, leads into exile, consigns to the mines; that mercy which kills by hunger, thirst, lashes, and nakedness; finally, that mercy which punishes by the sword. This, Constantius, is your mercy: it comes not from God’s law but from the devil’s presumption.

“Judgment, mercy, and faith—these,” he says, “you ought to have done, without neglecting the others” (Ibid.). Where is your faith—you who condemned the faith held by the most blessed Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, by all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs [Note: Perhaps read *damnaveris*, “you have condemned”], and decreed that all worshipers of God must accept that faith which the devil vomited forth against this catholic faith through your teacher Arius? By these things you are shown to be one of those recognized as hearing: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These things you ought to have done, without neglecting the others. Blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel” (Ibid.).

Or will you deny that you strain out the gnat and swallow the camel [Note: That is, observe lesser commands while despising greater ones], you who, although you sometimes give alms not only when asked but even freely, nevertheless—as has often been said—proscribe, deport, torture, and finally kill those who confess themselves Christians? Therefore you ought to recognize that you are among those to whom it is said: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful to men, but within are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of uncleanness. So you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly are full of hypocrisy and iniquity” (Ibid. 27).

You are among those murderers to whom it is said: “Serpents, brood [Note: Old Latin: “offspring … behold I … and wise men … and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute … until there comes upon you … righteous,” etc.] of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment [Note: Lucifer below has “judgment,” and *genimina* for *generamina*, “brood”; also: “behold, I send.”] of Gehenna? Therefore behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and persecute from city to city, so that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen, I say to you: all these things will come upon this generation” (Ibid. 33).

By your deeds you are proved to belong to that viperous stock [Note: Perhaps: “than the viperous stock”; Galland. But better: “from that viperous stock.”]. For you are found to be one of those of whom these words were spoken concerning what they were about to do. Or, if you deny that you are one of those who hear from the Lord’s mouth, “Serpents, brood of vipers” (Ibid.), prove that it was not you, but the Jews [Note: This refers to the impious and cruel deeds carried out by the commander Syrianus at Constantius’s command, so that, Athanasius having been expelled or killed, George of Cappadocia might be forced into his place in 356. The Alexandrians recount these events in a petition sent to Constantius, gravely complaining of Syrianus and his crime: “While we were keeping vigil in the Lord’s house and engaged in prayer, because the synaxis was to be celebrated on the day of preparation, suddenly, in the untimely night … during the very reading of the sacred lessons, he broke down the doors … immediately, at his order, some began to shoot arrows … and swords flashed by candlelight; many virgins were trampled under foot … persons struck and pierced by arrows fell; some soldiers, turning to plunder, stripped the virgins naked … Bishop Athanasius at that time sat upon the throne, exhorting all to prayer … while he was dragged this way and that, he was no less torn apart … and we do not know what became of him … then they ordered the soldiers to hide the bodies of all the slain in secret places. But the most holy virgins who had been killed and left there they buried in the tombs … Moreover, some deacons in the Lord’s house itself were beaten down with blows, others were bound with chains … each man, according to his own lust, burst in through broken doors and searched everything, penetrating into places into which it is not lawful for all Christians to enter.” These are their words. Further, from this testimony of Lucifer we learn that the Arians invented the claim that these deeds had been committed in a riot of Jews.] who sent soldiers to Alexandria; that Jewish soldiers besieged the doors of God’s house; that Syrianus was commander of Jewish soldiers. Prove that Jews entered the basilica with arms and killed a definite number of persons.

If you cannot prove this—since it is established that you sent men to assail God’s religion—we most rightly say that you are one of those to whom it was said: “Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?” (Ibid.). You will assuredly not escape the judgment of Gehenna, but will burn there forever with your fellow-serpents, unless you take thought for yourself.

“Then,” he says, “they will deliver you up to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for my name’s sake. Then many will be scandalized, and will betray one another and hate one another. Many false prophets will arise [Note: Old Latin: “will rise up … has abounded … will grow cold.”] and deceive many; and because iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold” (Ibid., XXIV, 9).

If your sacrilegious mind does not know that I suffer persecution from you on account of the only Son of God, you may not belong to that stock, nor be among those to whom it is said: “Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna? Therefore behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify and persecute from city to city” (Ibid., XXIII, 33). But since you do these things today, you will not dare deny that you are offspring of the viper. For in many places you have killed very many Christians; others you keep bound in prisons and workhouses. From this too you can see that you are one of those to whom it is said: “Serpents, brood of vipers” (Ibid.); and below: “Behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes, and some of them you will kill” (Ibid. 34).

For you do not think fit to curse those whom you see, through your abundant iniquity, to have departed from the apostolic faith—those whose love has grown cold—but rather those whom you see remaining in that state of faith in which the blessed prophets, apostles, and martyrs, by remaining, deserved to obtain God’s eternal friendship. You do not curse at Alexandria Macheta [Note: Socrates, II.23, and Nicephorus, IX.21, call him Achetas, as Latinius also observed. He was a deacon when, in 348, he brought Constantius’s letters to Athanasius at Aquileia, recalling him to the Alexandrian see. He had already been admitted to the priesthood when Lucifer reproached Constantius with these matters, along with the presbyter Dydimas—perhaps he should be called Didymus—who had defected from the Catholic side to the Arian. Gallandius thinks the reading should be “Achetas among the deacons,” but offers no argument, whereas Lucifer states that both were presbyters.] and Dydimas, presbyters who are known to have become Arians from Christians; rather, you curse those whom you still know to stand with us.

Or, if this is not so, why do you not now curse Dydimas and Macheta, whom you formerly cursed? Is it not because then they were regarded by you as accursed because they were still Christians, whereas now they are most dear to you because they have begun, plainly, to be what you are: apostates and blasphemers? Yet after so many proofs set before you, we believe that you, being one of those to whom it is said, “Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?” (Ibid. 33), will take pains to heal the very grievous wounds inflicted on you by the devil, since you are both murderer and sacrilegious person.

If you refuse to be freed from these crimes, your blood will be required from you; we shall stand before God clean from your blood, since we have made the truth clear to you in every way. From you will be required not only your own blood, but also the blood of those whom you either led into accepting heresy or enticed to slaughter an innocent man.

But if you say: “I thought that the faith of those whom you call Arians was catholic; if I wavered in the matter of faith; if I did not know that those who profess belief in a creature are heretics, those who say that God does not have a true Son”—did you also not know that it is unjust to persecute an innocent person with the sword? Had it escaped you that the Lord said to blessed Peter: “Return your sword to its place” [Note: Old Latin: “Into its place,” as Lucifer also has in *On Not Sparing Those Who Sin against God*]. “For all who take the sword shall perish by the sword” (Ibid., XXVI, 52)?

What meanwhile will you do, Constantius, who have killed so great a multitude of servants of Christ, the only Son of God? For you see him whom you persecute in us saying that all who take the sword will perish by the sword [Note: Above, Lucifer himself: “shall perish.”] (Ibid.). What will you receive [Note: Vatican manuscript: “What will they receive?”]—you who, unless by believing in him whom you have denied you obtain forgiveness for your crimes, deserve to be struck by God’s sword as often as you have struck those devoted to his mercy? What man are you, who said that a necessity must be imposed upon God’s priests to strike a man in his absence, punish one unheard, or shed an innocent man’s blood? Why did you refuse to allow Athanasius, our fellow priest, to be heard by us? Why did you wish, like robbers, that we should secretly murder a man of God? Is it not because you are among those whose reproach is set forth in these words:

“No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven [Note: Old Latin: “in heaven.” And: “As … so,” etc.]. And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in him may have [Note: Old Latin: “who believes in him may not perish, but may have,” etc. Lucifer agrees with Cyprian, *Testimonies*, II.] eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son [Note: Old Latin: “only-begotten … believed … He who believes” (omitting “therefore”) … “but he who does not believe” (omitting “in him”) … “only-begotten,” etc.], that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him. Therefore he who believes in him is not judged; but he who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of God’s only Son.

“And this is the judgment: that light came into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, for their works were evil. Everyone who does evil hates the light [Note: Vatican, Latin, and Greek add: “and does not come to the light”; but these words are also absent from the Old Latin, which reads: “For everyone who does evil … that [his works] may be exposed,” etc.], that his works may not be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be made manifest, because it has been done [Note: It should be “have been done.” In the old manuscript it was written in the singular: “that his work may be exposed” and “that his work may be made manifest.” Lucifer does not always observe genders and numbers in the customary manner. Tilius and La Cerda add: “Such usage is extremely frequent in other learned writers.” Greek: Φανερωθῇ, ἐν θεῷ ἐστιν ἐργασμένα, “may be made manifest, [that] they have been wrought in God”; Lucifer has evidently rendered the Greek words excessively literally. Galland. Old Latin: “But he who does … [comes] to the light … because they have been done in God.”] in God” (John III, 13).

If you knew yourself to be a servant of the only Son of God, you would never deny his majesty; you would never command that his servants be murdered, now secretly and now publicly. But because you are a lover of darkness—indeed, darkness itself, because your works are evil—you refused to have the case you brought fully investigated by God’s priests. Why did you refuse? Is it not because you feared that your serpentine work would be made public?

“For while we are in the body,” says the apostle, “we are absent from the Lord [Note: Old Latin: “from God … through faith … will” (omitting “good”) … “all of you,” etc. Lucifer in *On Dying for the Son of God*: “Placed in the body, we are absent from the Lord,” expressing the sense rather than the exact words.]; for we walk by faith, not by sight. We are confident, having good will, and prefer to be absent from the body and present with the Lord; and we strive, whether absent or present, to please him. For we must all be made manifest before Christ’s tribunal, that each may receive the things proper to the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil” (II Cor. V, 6).

And you, Constantius the heretic, say: “Condemn, Christians, a Christian.” Why do you say this? Is it not because you judge it best to shed the blood of the righteous, even to abandon God, and to embrace idolatry? But again, most pious Emperor, I beg you to recognize that, since you both deny the only Son of God and persecute those who believe in him, you are not unlike those whose wickedness is described in the Acts of the Apostles:

“When there was great [Note: Old Latin: “But when a great dissension arose … lest he be torn to pieces … by them … [the tribune], descending, commanded [the soldiers] to take him from their midst and bring him into the barracks.”] dissension among them, the tribune, fearing that Paul might be torn to pieces by them, ordered the troops to go down and take him into the barracks. But on the following night the Lord stood by him and said: ‘Take courage [Note: With the Greek, θάρσει, “take courage.” Old Latin: “Have confidence … in Jerusalem … and in Rome … when the Jews had assembled, they bound themselves by a vow.”]; for as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must testify also in Rome.’ When day came, some of the Jews gathered and bound themselves by a vow, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul. There were about [Note: Old Latin: “more than forty … had made … who, having come.”] forty who had formed this conspiracy. They went to [Note: Old Latin: “to the chief priests and elders, saying: ‘We have bound ourselves under a vow to taste nothing at all’” (omitting the rest).] the chief priests and declared: ‘We have bound ourselves by a vow to taste nothing at all until we kill Paul. Now therefore you convene the council and make it known to the tribune, so that he may bring him down to you as though you intended to inquire more carefully about him; but we, before he comes near, are ready to kill him’” (Acts XXIII, 10).

Unless you sought Athanasius, a priest of God, in this manner; unless you pretended to do one thing and intended to accomplish another—can you deny that you too are driven by the same hostile spirit by which the Jews were driven and are driven? For unless you had been stirred by that spirit against us who serve God, you would never have commanded an absent and innocent man to be condemned. Yet I repeat these things often, as though you yourself, when you are sometimes free from the goads of frenzy, did not consider how in every way you have so far departed from the rule of justice [Note: “Gone astray,” “turned aside,” “departed from the rule of justice.” Tilius.] that you could not even see in the Acts of the Apostles that, when the Jews sought to kill blessed Paul, the Gentile governor Festus did not grant the Jewish assembly its assent [Note: “Gave consent,” or “consented to the Jews.”], but promised that he could hear both them and Paul together. A Gentile observed the law of equity; you destroyed it.

Or is it equity to condemn a man unheard, kill a man absent, and deny a hearing to that righteous man concerning whom all God’s people are witnesses that he was falsely accused by you and your Arian Christians? Therefore, as I began to say, hear what Festus did concerning the Jews and blessed Paul.

Festus [Note: Several words are lacking here and must be inserted altogether from the Old Latin for the sense to stand, as Tilius and Latinius also observed: “Therefore when Festus had come into the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem. Then the chief priests and leading Jews informed him against Paul and begged him, asking a favor against him, that he should summon him to Jerusalem, laying ambushes, that,” etc. Galland judges that the intervening words were omitted through an inattentive copyist or printer who moved his eyes from the preceding occurrence of “Jerusalem” to the next. But the printer is not at fault, since Tilius affirms that those words were omitted in the manuscript itself.] when he came into the province as governor, went up to Jerusalem, while they were laying ambushes to kill him on the road. Festus therefore [Note: Old Latin: “Festus therefore … to be kept” (omitting “indeed”) … “was about to depart.”] replied that Paul was indeed kept at Caesarea, but that he himself would depart shortly. “Therefore let those [Note: Latin and Galland, from the Vulgate, add “powerful.” Old Latin: “Let those among you who are powerful, he says, go down; and if there is … any unlawful act,” etc.] among you go down, and if there is any charge against the man, let them accuse him.” After remaining [Note: Old Latin: “But he remained … not more than eight days … going down into … on the next day, taking his seat, he ordered Paul to be brought. When he arrived … those from Jerusalem” (omitting “the Jews”) … “bringing many serious accusations against Paul, which they could not prove … For neither … nor … have I sinned in anything.”] among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the following day he sat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be summoned. When he had been brought, the Jews who had come down from [Note: Sabatier reads “from.”] Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges which they could not prove. But Paul made his defense: that he had sinned in nothing either against the law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar (Acts XXV, 1).

The pagan followed the path of equity between blessed Paul and your fellow-murdering Jews, while you, wishing to obey the desires of your evil designs, decreed that equity and justice must be removed from our minds. But how could we have done what you compelled to be done against justice, when we remembered what is written: “Do not judge according to appearance [Note: With the Cambridge manuscript in Sabatier. Old Latin: “face.”], but judge righteous judgment. Condemn the man unheard” (John VII, 24)? When you said this, why did you not remember that Nicodemus said: “Does our law judge a man [Note: Old Latin: “Does [it] judge a man unless it first hears from him and first knows what he has done?”] unless it first hears from him and knows what he has done?” (Ibid. 51).

Why did you refuse to hear the man whom you declared guilty of death, except because you had brought false accusations? The Lord says to the Jews: “He who speaks falsehood speaks from his own [Note: Old Latin: “from his own things … because … as also his father.”], because he is a liar and his father [is a liar]” (Ibid., VIII, 44). And when you have been shown to be a liar [Note: “Since it is clearer than light that you are a liar and have spoken falsehood against Athanasius.” Tilius.], do you suppose that you are not a son of a liar? Do you, a son of a liar, dare deceitfully to resist the truthful priests of the Lord? Do you, a sacrilegious man, dare [to resist], when we recognize you to be that thief and robber whom the Lord foretold, saying: “Amen, amen, I say to you: he who does not enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs in by another way, is a thief and a robber” (John X, 1)?

You have indeed stretched out your hands against Christ’s sheep in order to claim them for Antichrist; but, being recognized as a thief and robber, you have been avoided and rejected. Why you, or your fellow-sacrilegious George [Note: How strongly the Alexandrians recoiled from communion with George, they themselves testify in the petition mentioned a little above: “If the Emperor’s edict is that persecution should be carried out against us, we are all ready to undergo martyrdom … and we beg that we may obtain this: that it not be permitted to them to introduce another bishop. We resisted lest this should happen, desiring the most reverend Athanasius, whom God gave us from the beginning in accordance with the succession of our fathers, and whom the most religious Augustus Constantius himself sent here with letters and oaths.” What followed]

…there are massacres, exiles, confiscations of property, and proscriptions throughout almost the whole diocese of the Alexandrian bishopric, for nearly six full years until Athanasius’ return. These sufficiently show that those Catholics were prepared to undergo every extremity of suffering rather than enter into any communion in religion or sacred rites with George.] Have not God’s sheep followed? Why do they follow the man whom, to your great grief, you admit to be bishop of the Alexandrians? Unless it be because God appointed him bishop for them, whereas the devil sent you and George to slaughter them, as thieves and robbers.

“He who enters through the door,” he says, “[Col. 0921B] is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice; he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out; and when he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him because they know [Note: [Col. 0922D] Old Version: ‘They know … but a stranger … from him,’ etc.] his voice. They do not follow another, but flee from him, because they do not know his voice” (John 10:2).

[Note: [Col. 0921D] Old Latin and Galland, as in the Old Version, which reads: “[Col. 0922D] But when he has brought out the sheep … he will go before them.” Greek: ἐκβάλῃ, “brings/drives out.”]

Therefore, because you have not entered the Church through the door, you are seen to be a robber and a thief. For you do not know the Son of God, so as to say that you entered through the door. Indeed, he called them thieves and robbers because they were not then believing in his divine mercy, nor would they believe thereafter, and would attempt to mislead his sheep.

Therefore, since you scatter this insane teaching—since, because you have not believed in him, you are certainly that robber and thief whom you were already then foreshadowed to be—you are proved most plainly by [Col. 0921C] your blasphemies [Note: [Col. 0922D] “Blasphemies.” Id.] to be such. The following words of the declaration prove this [Note: [Col. 0922D] “The following prove,” or “the following,” treated as feminine. Id.]: Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I say to you: I [Note: [Col. 0922D] Old Version: “For I am the door … all who.”] am the door of the sheep. All who came before [Note: [Col. 0922D] Thus the Greek, πρὸ ἐμοῦ, “before me,” which is absent from the Old Version.] me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them. I am the door [Note: [Col. 0922D] Old Version: “Gate. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; and he will enter and go out and find pasture.”]; if anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and will enter and go out and find pasture. The thief does not come except to steal” (ibid. 7).

You, then, are a thief, who are found to have entered God’s sheepfold for this purpose: namely, to steal and kill. With what voice can you still say, “Athanasius ought not to be bishop of the Alexandrians, but George,” when you see that you, George, and all your fellow-sacrilegious men are nothing but thieves and robbers? [Col. 0922A] God wished his servants to be shepherds over the flock, so that, recognizing you and yours as robbers and thieves, they might drive you out. But for this reason you judged that you and yours ought to preside over the Lord’s flock—after we, ordained by God’s judgment, had been driven out—so that you might freely ravage God’s flock.

Since you are such a man, we cannot wonder that you said a worshipper of God, though absent, ought to be punished. For you could not have retained what the Lord said: “If you love me, keep my commandments [Note: [Col. 0922D] Old Version: “Keep my precepts … Spirit … this world … because … him, nor knows him; but you know him, because,” etc.]; and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate, that he may be with you for ever: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive because it neither sees nor recognizes him; but you recognize him, because he remains with you and is in you” (ibid. 14:15).

But tell me, I beg you: how could the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, dwell in us if we had done your will or your father’s will? Further below he says: “He who hears my commandments [Note: [Col. 0922D] Lucifer below: “commandments,” and “we shall abide with him.”] and keeps [Note: [Col. 0922D] Old Version: “Keeps them … and I shall reveal myself to him … not Judas Iscariot, but another … why do you begin to reveal yourself to us … he says to him … has kept … him, and to him … we abide … does not keep.”] them, he is the one who loves me. And he who loves me shall be loved by my Father, and I shall love him and reveal myself to him.” Judas—not Scarioth [Note: [Col. 0922D] Sabatier reads “Iscariot.”]—said to him: “Lord, what has happened, that you reveal yourself to us and not to this world?” Jesus answered and said to him: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and we shall come to him and abide with him. He who does not love me does not keep my words” (ibid. 21).

From these declarations of the Lord one may infer how great an enemy you have proved to be: “He who hears my commandments and keeps them, he is the one who loves me” (ibid.). How could we show that we loved him if, like you, we trampled on his commandments? For you trample on the Lord’s commandments; and whereas he decreed that they should be kept, you command not merely that they should not be kept, but that he himself should be denied. Or how could his Father love me because I had kept the commandments of his Son, if I condemned an innocent man?

The Son of God says: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we shall come to him and abide with him” (ibid. 23); and you, food for the fire, apostate, say: “Condemn the innocent man.” In what way would we have been found to love the Son of God if, against his commandments, we murdered a righteous man? How could it come about that the Father loved us, and that Father and Son came and deigned to dwell in us, if, annulling the Lord’s commandments, we kept your sacrilegious commands? See, Constantius, from what glory that envious lover of your will, the devil, tried through you, his client, to drive us—unless the Lord’s mercy had come to our aid. Regarding you no longer as a human being whom God made in his own image and likeness, but as the filth of every sewer, we trampled underfoot your sacrilegious orders.

[Note: [Col. 0923C] That is, “unless we trampled upon you,” etc.]

For who, unless more wretched than you Arians, would not wish to be loved by the only Son of God? Who would not wish to be loved by his Father? Who would refuse to be the temple of the Father and his only Son? Yet one who, like you, is both a murderer and sacrilegious cannot attain these things. You too may indeed attain them, if you turn back and truly repent.

The Lord says again: “This is my commandment [Note: [Col. 0923C] Old Version: “Precept … because with love … Greater than this love … which I command,” etc.], that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has a greater [Note: [Col. 0923C] “Although I give no warning, no one will fail to correct this passage of Lucifer,” says Cotelerius in his notes on the *Apophthegmata Patrum*, p. 621 of *Monumenta Ecclesiae Graecae*, since, in accordance with the Greek reading, μείζονα ταύτης τῆς ἀγάπης, it should be translated “greater love than this.” Sabatier reads *hac* in Lucifer himself. The Fossat manuscript, cited by Sabatier, prefers *hanc*.] [Col. 0923B] love than to lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. I no longer call you servants, but [Note: [Col. 0923C] “But friends” is absent from the Old Version; it is read in the Major Monastery manuscript cited by Sabatier and in Cyprian, Epistle 63. See [Col. 0923D] what we noted, p. 119, n. 8.] friends” (John 15:12). And again: “You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed [Note: [Col. 0923D] Old Version: “Ordained … that whatever you ask the Father in [my] name.”] you to go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain, so that whatever you ask my Father in my name, he may give it to you” (ibid. 16).

How can we be friends of the only Son of God if, against his merciful prohibition, we condemn one who is absent and kill an innocent man? How can our fruit yield increase and growth? How shall we receive from the Father whatever we ask in his name if, as you compelled us, we not only punished his worshipper but also denied him himself?
