Had you not found that the blessed Apostle wrote to Titus, a man devoted to God, concerning the irreproachable office of a bishop, that you desired to make us murderers? “For this reason I left you in Crete: that you should correct what was lacking and appoint elders in the cities [Note: [Col. 0923D] “Elders.” Latin from the Greek. Old Version has “presbyterium,” with Lucifer. But nothing should be altered: Mill observes, both here and in the *Prolegomena* to the New Testament, §777, that Lucifer’s reading occurs in some manuscripts. Galland.], as I directed you. If anyone is without accusation, the husband of one wife, having believing children, not accused [Col. 0924A] of debauchery or insubordinate [Note: [Col. 0923D] Sabatier reads “not insubordinate.” Old Version: “not insubordinate.”]: for a bishop must be without accusation, as God’s steward—not arrogant [Note: [Col. 0923D] Sabatier has “proud.”], not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain [Note: [Col. 0923D] Lucifer attempted to render the Greek αἰσχροκερδῆ, “greedy for shameful gain.” Galland.]; but hospitable, kind, sober, just, holy, self-controlled, holding fast the faithful [Note: [Col. 0923D] Old Version: “faithful word.”] word according to the teaching, so that he may be able both to exhort in doctrine [Note: [Col. 0923D] “In sound doctrine,” Galland from the Vulgate; Old Version: “and to exhort in sound doctrine.”] and refute opponents. For there are many who are also insubordinate, idle talkers, and deceivers [Note: [Col. 0923D] Greek: Φρεναπάται, “deceivers.” Old Version: “seducers.”], especially those of the circumcision, whom it is necessary to rebuke, since they overthrow whole households, teaching for the sake of shameful gain what ought not to be taught” (Titus 1:5).

Since he wished a bishop to be made such a man, living by this path of righteousness, by what authority have you deigned to give new commands that exclude the commandments of the blessed Apostle—commands plainly known to have arisen from the devil’s will? [Col. 0924B] The Apostle wishes me to be neither quick-tempered nor violent, and do you wish to make me a murderer? From these facts it may be inferred that the Holy Spirit spoke through the mouth of the blessed Apostle, but an evil spirit through the mouth of you Arians.

Meanwhile you see that the Apostle commanded that you who resist the truth should be “broken by the intervention of a bishop” [Note: [Col. 0923D] This word is corrupt; I think it should be restored as “by the intervention of a most upright bishop,” or something similar. Til. and La Cerda. Cange in his *Glossary* emends this passage of Lucifer thus: “that you who resist the truth should be *indeptemini* by the intervention of a bishop,” from *indeptare*. Yet the sense remains obscure. It is therefore better to retain *indentemini*, derived from *indentare*, “to break with the teeth.” Pacian, bishop of Barcelona, uses it in Epistle 2, cited by Cange: “concerning such persons, whom the Apostle says must be *indentari*.” The sense is that Arians are to be broken or crushed by sound doctrine and the authority of the kind of bishop described by Paul in his Epistle to Titus.]—so that by sound doctrine your blasphemy might be punished.

I did not bring forward the blessed Apostle’s saying, that a bishop must be without accusation, in order to deny that I am a sinner. I know my own conscience, and I hear righteous Job say: “For who is clean [Note: [Col. 0924C] This testimony of Job occurs in chapter 14 of that book [Col. 0924D] in the Septuagint. Origen likewise gives almost the same words as Lucifer in many places: “No one is clean from defilement, not even if his life on earth is one day long”—namely, in Book IV of *On First Principles*, Homily 8 on Leviticus, Homily 3 on Numbers, *Selections on Psalm* 129, Book 3 on the Song of Songs, Homily 5 on Jeremiah, Homily 14 on Luke, and Tome 15 on Matthew. The author of *Questions to the Orthodox*, question 88, likewise says: Τίς γὰρ καθαρὸς ἔσται ἀπὸ ῥύπου; ἀλλ᾽ οὐδεὶς, ἐὰν καὶ μία ἡμέρα ὁ βίος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς—“For who shall be clean from defilement? No one, even if life on earth lasts but one day.” Old Version: “Who then shall be clean without defilement? Not even one … whose life … is upon earth.”] from defilements? No one, even if his life on earth is one day long” (Job 14:4). I also observe blessed John saying: “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves [Note: [Col. 0924D] In agreement with the Greek πλανῶμεν, “we deceive.” Old Version: “We mislead ourselves.”] and the truth is not in us” (1 John 1:8).

I therefore put forward the Apostle’s command not in order that I, who remember that I am a sinner, might proclaim myself without defilement, but so that you might see how evil is what you commanded to be done. “Likewise urge young men,” he says, “to be sober in all things [Note: [Col. 0924D] “In all things” is absent from the Old Version. Jerome, on Titus 2:6, observes that it should be read as in Lucifer’s version; but Lucifer repeats, “in every respect show yourself,” etc., where the Old Version has “in all things,” which, with the Greek, belongs to verse 7.], showing yourself [Col. 0925A] in every respect as a pattern of good works: in teaching, in integrity, in seriousness, in [Note: [Col. 0925D] Old Version: “In teaching, in integrity, seriousness, having sound speech … so that he may have,” etc.] sound speech beyond reproach, so that an opponent may be ashamed, having nothing evil [Note: [Col. 0925D] Sabatier omits *quid*, “anything.”] to say of us” (Titus 2:6).

How could I have furnished others with a pattern of good works if I had shed the blood of God’s servant? How would God’s people know me to be preaching the uncorrupted teaching handed down by the Apostles if I had embraced your heresy—if, finally, even under the hypocritical pretext of your [Note: [Col. 0925D] “Attendants,” Til. and Latin. Either *satellitus satelliti*, or, as I think, *satellitis*, an abbreviated form, as we call it; for later he plainly says “those attendants of yours.” La Cerda. Thus Lucifer’s style uses *satellitis* for *satellitibus*. Galland.] Arian pseudo-bishop attendants, I had joined in communion? How could my speech be offered as sound and irreproachable if, abandoning the evangelical and apostolic faith, I had adopted your blasphemy? How could an adversary have been ashamed? How could he have nothing evil to say of me, when, if I had judged that I must comply with you, he would have found me both a murderer and [Col. 0925B] sacrilegious?

Again, when he was instructing servants that they should be subject to their masters, he said: “For the grace of God our Saviour has shone forth [Note: [Col. 0925D] Old Version: “of God the Saviour for all,” etc.] for all people, instructing [Note: [Col. 0925D] Sabatier here reads “teaching.”] us that, renouncing impiety and worldly desires, we should live soberly, godly, and justly in this age, awaiting the blessed hope in [Note: [Col. 0925D] “And the appearing,” Latin from the Greek and Vulgate, and the Old Version.] the appearing of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, to free us from all iniquity and cleanse [Note: [Col. 0926D] Til. has *mundaret*, “might cleanse,” in place of *mundet*. Latin and Old Version: *mundet*, with Lucifer.] for himself a people abundant, zealous for good works” (ibid. 11).

When he commanded us to walk in these good works, why did you judge that we should be summoned to commit murder? How could we appear to have renounced impiety and to live godly and justly if we had shed an innocent man’s blood with you? But when he says that the Lord gave himself for our sins precisely in order to rescue us [Col. 0925C] from the works of Satan and establish us as zealots for good works, if we had committed this work of yours with you, in what party would we be except Cain’s?

“For the grace of God our Saviour has shone forth for all people, instructing us that, renouncing impiety and [Note: [Col. 0926D] “And worldly desires … and godly and justly.” The same Lucifer above.] worldly desires, we should live soberly, justly, and godly in this age” (ibid.). Yet you, Emperor Constantius, deign to say that we should be impious, criminal, lost, malicious, iniquitous, unjust. Where shall I find that blessed hope which the blessed Apostle teaches me to await, if I not only kill the servants of him who is able to bestow every blessedness, but also deny him himself? For you do both, Constantius: you persecute [Col. 0925D] and kill his servants, and, abandoning him, you have judged that you must enslave yourself to idols. Why do you do these things, except because the grace of God our Saviour has not shone upon you? For if it had shone, you would remember the Apostle’s commandments:

“See, therefore, how carefully [Note: [Col. 0926D] With the Greek ἀκριβῶς, “carefully,” which is absent from the Old Version.] you walk, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not become foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is” (Ephesians 5:15).

If the Lord’s will is to kill an innocent man and abandon evangelical faith, not only this section but the entire body of the blessed Apostle’s letters can support your decrees. But if no portion of the sacred Scriptures supports your decrees, it is clearer than light that you live under the power of darkness. Hence it has come about that you have drawn nothing from the fountains of the sacred Scriptures which could remove you from such great perils.

For if the power of darkness had not reduced you under its dominion, you would certainly retain what the Philippians hear: “Be fellow-imitators of me, [Col. 0926B] brothers, and observe those who walk in this way, as you have us for a pattern. For many walk, of whom I often [Note: [Col. 0926D] With the Greek; Old Version: “always.”] told you, but now tell you even weeping: enemies of Christ’s cross, whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame [Note: [Col. 0926D] Thus the Greek, ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ, “in shame.” Old Version: “confession.”], who set their minds on earthly things” (Philippians 3:17).

I wish you to say, most prudent emperor, in what respects we ought to become fellow-imitators of the Apostle. Teach us, apostate. Was the Apostle a murderer, a blasphemer, a destroyer of evangelical faith, a sacrilegious man? For he confesses that he committed all these things before he believed in the only Son of God. But you, who do today the things which he did before recognizing the only Son of God—for what reason have you dared to command us, the Lord’s priests, to condemn an innocent man, to embrace your heresy, and [Col. 0926C] reject the apostolic faith? For what reason did you command these things to be done—things contrary to the Apostle’s pattern—unless because you are among the enemies of Christ’s cross, among those whom the holy Apostle had already marked out?

Should we listen to you and yours, whose end the Apostle says is destruction? Should we listen to those attendants of yours who, abandoning the pattern of teaching and the rule of faith handed down through the Apostles, surrendered themselves to you for shameful gain; who made more of the abundance of your table than of the things the Lord promises his own; who chose to be your table-companions rather than companions of patriarchs, prophets, Apostles, or martyrs? To them it is most rightly said: “Your god is your belly.”

The Apostle says: “Test [Note: [Col. 0926D] “Test everything,” Latin, with the Greek, Old Version, and Vulgate.] everything; hold fast what is good; hold yourselves back from every appearance of evil [Note: [Col. 0926D] Old Version: “Abstain.”]” (1 Thessalonians 5:21). And because we saw your Arians’ accursed work and avoided it, we suffer hatred. Yet how beautiful and pleasant it is to be hated by you and loved by God!

You expelled us from the office entrusted to us, supposing that you could [Col. 0927A] destroy what God built. “But to each of us,” writing to the Ephesians, he says, “grace was given according to the measure of Christ’s gracious gift [Note: [Col. 0927C] “Gift.” Id., Latin with the same witnesses. I alter nothing, for *dignatio* is frequently used for *donatio* by Tertullian, Cyprian, and other Fathers. See Cange’s *Glossary*, s.v. *Dignatio*. Galland.]. Therefore it says: ‘Ascending on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to people.’ Now what does ‘he ascended’ mean, except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth? And he who descended is the same who also ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things. And he gave some as Apostles, some as prophets, others as evangelists, others as pastors and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of Christ’s body, until we all attain the unity of faith and knowledge of God [Note: [Col. 0927C] Vulgate: “and knowledge of the Son of God,” as the Greek text has: Καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, “and of the knowledge of the Son of God.” Yet the reading τοῦ υἱοῦ, “of the Son,” is absent in Lucifer, as also in Clement of Alexandria, *Paedagogue* 1.5. Galland. Old Version: “into unity of faith and knowledge of the Son of God.”]—to a perfect man, to the measure of the maturity of Christ’s fullness—so that we may no longer be little children, tossed about and carried [Col. 0927B] by every wind of doctrine, through human malice, through craftiness toward the device [Note: [Col. 0927D] Greek: πρὸς τὴν μεθοδείαν τῆς πλάνης, “toward the scheming of error.” Vulgate: “toward the deceiving of error.” On this passage Mill observes that the old translator rendered *μεθοδεία* as *remedium*, “device/remedy,” here and at Ephesians 6:11, and that this translation passed into the writings of many old Latin authors. In the *Prolegomena* to the New Testament, nos. 568 and 866, he judges the reason to be that at that time *remedium* signified a kind of deception by which poisoners or wandering charlatans, using drugs and potions, emptied the purses of the simple. Since this sense had long become obsolete and *remedium* acquired an altogether different meaning, Jerome substituted *circumventio*, “deception”; and at Ephesians 6:11, in place of the Old Italian’s *remedia diaboli*, “the devil’s devices,” he wrote *insidias diaboli*, “the devil’s snares.” Galland.] of error. But, speaking the truth in love, let us grow in every way into him who is the head, Christ, from whom the whole body, fitted and joined together through every supporting joint, according to the measure of each part, produces the body’s growth for its own building up in love” (Ephesians 4:7).

When you read that these things are so, why did you dare to remove the shepherds whom God wished to preside over his flock? Why? Unless [Note: [Col. 0928C] The passage seems defective or wholly corrupt, so that it cannot suitably be explained. Til.] so that God’s shepherds might carry you about with every wind of doctrine over the Lord’s flock, rather than themselves being carried about as little children by every wind of doctrine? When people came to the faith, you removed [Note: [Col. 0928C] That is, you removed or deposed Catholic bishops and appointed Arians. Til. and La Cerda. Athanasius also complains bitterly of this in the *Apologies*, in the Letter to the Solitaries, and in the Letter to the Bishops of Africa. “What Church,” he writes in the *Apology for His Flight to Constantius*, “does not grieve at the snares which those Arians have set for its bishops? Is not Antioch in mourning because Eustathius … was taken away? Balanae because of Euphration; Paltus and Antaradus because of Cymatius and Carterius; Adrianople because of Eutropius and then Lucius; Ancyra because of Marcellus; Beroea because of Cyrus; Gaza because of Asclepas,” etc.] bishops [Col. 0927C] from the peoples over whom we preside by divine gracious gift, in order that you might teach not apostolic doctrine but heretical doctrine—lest, through the craftiness of you utterly wicked men and the devices of the devil, your prince [Note: [Col. 0928C] That is, snares, in the sense just explained from Mill. Galland.], they should fall away from apostolic and evangelical faith.

Woe to you, wretch, through whom Satan does these things. Wise man that you are, you found a fitting pretext for your deceit: a way in which you might keep God’s sheep for your father [Note: [Col. 0928D] That is, preserve them for the devil. Galland would prefer *deferre*, “hand over.”], who, in order to keep you lingering in these evils, struck [Note: [Col. 0928D] “He struck your heart,” “pierced your heart.” He uses the active in place of the passive, which is not idiomatic Latin. Til.] your heart with those darts by which he wounded the minds of Eve and Adam, in order to establish you in this wickedness.

[Col. 0928A] Wise man, I say, you found a fitting pretext for your deceit: a way to ravage the Lord’s flock by saying, “Athanasius sinned; therefore whoever kills him with me shall be bishop, and whoever judges that he should be retained shall not be. And those who condemned Athanasius were joined to pseudo-bishops of your Arian doctrine.” If any, fearing your anger, had done this, through you—a murderer and sacrilegious man—they incurred a threefold crime: condemning an innocent man; Catholics communicating with heretics; and allowing you wolves to enter God’s flock. For the Apostle says that shepherds were given so that every doctrine of demons, proclaimed through you heretics and all adversaries of the Church, might be excluded; and so that God’s servants, running in truth, might remain [Col. 0928B] steadfast until they reached the height of perfection. Yet you, darkness, deigned to remove the shepherds established by God’s judgment, so that you, a wolf, might turn them all into prey for the devil, your beloved.

“So that we may no longer be little children, tossed about and carried by every wind of doctrine, through human malice, through craftiness toward the device of error. But, speaking the truth in love, let us grow in every way into him who is the head, Christ” (ibid. 14). How could we grow in him if we had followed you, darkness, when you deny that he is true God, say that he was not begotten from the substance of the Father, and assert that he was made from nothing? How could we [Note: [Col. 0928D] Latin: “could.”] grow in him when we were not going to walk in truth, since we had followed you, an apostate?

Then, when he says, “Speaking the truth [Col. 0928C] let us grow in love” (ibid. 15), and it is manifest that Athanasius, God’s priest, was attacked by you and yours with false accusations, if we had done what you command, how could we have been seen to proceed either in truth or in love? We should have extinguished the love which we hold with our fellow bishop Athanasius; and, because we had complied [Note: [Col. 0928D] “Who.” Id.] [Note: [Col. 0928D] For *obtemperassemus*: “we had complied with the false charge brought against Athanasius.” Til., Latin, La Cerda, and Galland.] with a false accusation and joined you, yourself a deceiver, in killing an innocent man, we should have deserved to be struck by divine indignation.

Is God’s house, then, Constantius, built by deception, by the shedding of innocent blood, by blasphemous preaching? Woe to you, who live so that the devil may perpetrate all these evils through you. You tell me: “Punish the innocent man; abandon the Catholic faith; receive the poisons of my heresy.” But the Apostle says: “This therefore I say and testify in the Lord: that you no longer [Note: [Col. 0929D] Old Version: “that you no longer walk thus.”] walk as the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their mind, darkened in understanding, alienated from the life [Note: [Col. 0929D] Sabatier here reads “way.”] of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their hearts” (Ephesians 4:17).

Which of you shall I obey—yourself or the Apostle? You, an apostate and sacrilegious man, or him who is found already to have shed his blood for the only Son of God? Which of you shall I follow—you, a temple of demons, or him, a temple of God? You, who by your [Col. 0929B] deeds show yourself to be either Jew or Gentile, or him who, through the faith which you curse, has already attained the kingdoms of heaven?

For if you do not make yourself known as a Gentile by your deeds, you may defend the claim that these things are not deservedly said against you. First, because you deny the Son of God, you are to us a Gentile or a Jew. Then, when you proscribe, deport, torture, burden innocent people with false accusations, and kill, you cannot be found to be a Christian, known as a man of God by his manner of life. Rather, you are certainly one of those of whom God’s Spirit says through the Apostle that they are vain in their mind, foolish [Note: [Col. 0929D] Lucifer himself above: “darkened in understanding … through the ignorance that is in them, because of blindness.”], alienated from God’s life through the blindness of their hearts (ibid. 18).

Therefore, since the Apostle’s words show that the things you do are done with a blinded heart, with what face do you dare to say to men sound in [Col. 0929C] heart and mind, “You have erred,” or, deceiver that you are, “You are liars”? The Apostle says: “As truth is in Jesus, put off [Note: [Col. 0929D] Old Version: “that you put off according to the former,” etc.] the old man according to your former manner of life, which is corrupted according to the desires of error [Note: [Col. 0929D] Greek: ἀπάτης, “deceit.” Old Version: “seduction.”]. Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who was created according to God in righteousness [Note: [Col. 0929D] Old Version: “in righteousness and holiness and truth. Therefore … with his neighbour.”] and holiness and truth. Putting away falsehood, speak truth, each one to his neighbour.”

Where did you neglect [Note: [Col. 0929D] It seems that *praetermisissemus*, “we had neglected,” should be read, and the passage punctuated thus: “If we had neglected these saving admonitions which the Apostle urges us to keep, how …?” This emendation is favoured by the words that follow: “we should have been seen,” “we should have extinguished,” “we should have begun to bear.” Galland. But the particle *etenim* prevents the first question from being joined with the second; and the first “where,” etc., applies more suitably to Constantius, whom he asks how he forgot the Apostle’s admonitions, who forbids falsehood to everyone, especially bishops.] these saving admonitions which the Apostle urges us to observe? For how could we have been found to have put off the old man and put on the new man who is according to God? How could we have been seen to remain [Col. 0930A] in righteousness, holiness, and truth, when, committing injustices with you, we would have extinguished that new man created according to God, and begun again to bear the old man, corrupted according to the desire of error, just as he was corrupted before he began to know God?

For all these things which you do are done not by members of God’s household, but by the attendants of Antichrist: “Putting away falsehood, speak truth, each one to his neighbour, because we are members of one another” (ibid. 25). If you had been one of the members of God’s Church, believe me, you would never have brought falsehood into the Church. But because you are the man of him who deceived Adam and Eve by deceit, you brought falsehood in order to ensnare us as [Col. 0930B] the devil ensnared the first-created human beings.

You said: “Condemn Athanasius, because he has sinned grievously; otherwise you will be under the greatest guilt before God. Accept Arius’s faith and you will live for ever.” Consider what he who loved you so dearly did to Adam and Eve, and you will find that you are now doing to us what he then did to them (Genesis 2:25).

“In Genesis,” Moses says, “Adam and his wife were both naked then [Note: [Col. 0930D] “Then” is omitted by the Old Version, which has “they were not ashamed” for “they were not confounded.”], and they were not ashamed. But the serpent was wiser [Note: [Col. 0930D] Old Version: “most prudent,” and adds “than all things which are upon the earth.” Jerome, in the *Hebrew Questions*, reads “wiser,” with Lucifer.] than all the beasts [Note: [Col. 0930D] “Beasts.” Til.] that were.” And below: “The serpent said to the woman, ‘Why [Note: [Col. 0930D] *Quid quia*, “why,” in place of *cur*. Id.] did the Lord God say [Note: [Col. 0930D] Old Version: “God said: You shall not eat from every tree of paradise?”] that you should not eat from every tree that is in paradise?’ The woman said to the serpent, ‘We shall eat from [Note: [Col. 0930D] Old Version: “From the fruit of the tree … You shall not eat … nor touch it.”] every tree that is in paradise; but concerning the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of paradise [Col. 0930C] God said: “You shall not eat from it, nor even touch it, lest you die.”’”

We say to you, who stand in the serpent’s place and urge us to condemn one unheard, to murder an innocent man: the Lord commanded that an innocent and righteous man must not be killed. “And the serpent said to the woman: ‘You shall not die [Note: [Col. 0930D] Old Version: “You shall not die by death … for on the day … from it … your eyes … like gods.”]’” (ibid. 4). “For God knew that on whatever day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil.”

Accordingly, this serpent—speaking through you to us, “You will be more righteous if you shed righteous blood; you will be more blessed if, anathematizing apostolic and evangelical faith, you embrace Arian perfidy”—is now, by God’s favour, being trampled down in you by us, who know his deceit. [Note: [Col. 0930D] Something is missing here to complete the sense of the accusative *dicentem*; alternatively, with a solecism admitted, it must be construed with *calcatur* (“is trampled”). We have nevertheless altered nothing.] Yet God is witness that we grieve for you, because through you he has set himself to ensnare us. For it is established that at that time, in person…

[The serpent] attacked Adam and Eve. I entreat you not to take harshly what is said for the sake of your salvation. For I suppose that you are grieved because I said that the serpent attacked us through you, and because in many places I have placed you among those who have been called serpents. Consider your own work and theirs; and if you do not discover that you and they are one body, tell me that I do not say these things justly. You surely hear that your teachers in impiety—the Jews—are often called serpents by the Lord in the holy Gospels: “Serpents, brood of vipers” (Matt. 23:33). On what account did they deserve to be called by this name? Certainly because of their wicked work; certainly because of their unbelief.

Thus John the Baptist too says to them, “Offspring of vipers” (ibid. 3:7): “Who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come? Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance.” [Note: Most manuscripts cited by Sabatier’s Old Latin Version have “will show” and “fruit worthy.” Lucifer himself, above p. 120: “Who showed . . . [how to flee] from the wrath to come? . . . fruit worthy of repentance.”] Accordingly, just as from among those who believed in the only Son of God and corrected their ways, some deserved to become children of light, while others are called serpents, so you also—unless you produce fruits worthy of repentance, unless you correct your ways—will be called a son of the viper and of the serpent. For what servant of God, seeing that you are a murderer and a blasphemer, would not call you by the name by which the Jews are called? [Note: Perhaps “not” should not be removed. Latin.] Who among those who fear God would hesitate to declare what you are, when he sees that the scribes, Pharisees, and rulers of the Jews are called serpents precisely because they shed the blood of the prophets and denied the only Son of God? [Note: We have corrected this passage thus in accordance with the Latin and Gallandi; in the Tilius edition it read: “Who will doubt that you are God-fearing, what you are to declare,” etc. The editors of the Lyons *Bibliotheca Patrum* had corrected it thus: “Who among those fearing you will assert God, because you are able to declare,” when he sees the scribes, etc.]

Since these things are so, it remains for you to repent of your deeds, bearing in mind that God has bestowed the mercy of his clemency upon all who turn away from evil ways. You have the example of the Ninevites, whom, if you imitate, you must likewise obtain the help of mercy. Therefore hear what happened, and what they themselves, terrified by Jonah’s preaching, did.

Holy Scripture says: “The whale was commanded, and it cast Jonah up upon the dry land” (Jonah 2:11). [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “He commanded . . . and it cast [him] . . . upon dry land. And the word . . . a second [time] . . . Nineveh . . . according to the former [preaching] . . . Nineveh, as he had spoken to him . . . great before God, about a journey of three days’ travel . . . to enter the city about a journey [of one day] . . . Yet three days,” etc.] “And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying” (ibid. 3:1): “Rise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it according to the former preaching which I spoke to you.” [Note: Sabatier reads *Niniven* here and below.] And Jonah rose and went to Nineveh, according to what the Lord had spoken to him. Now Nineveh was a city so great as a journey of three days. [Note: Sabatier has “great before God” in place of “so great.”] And Jonah began to enter the city, as a journey of one day, and he preached and said: “Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.” [Note: The Tilius edition and the Old Latin version read “yet three days”; this reading was rightly retained in the Paris edition of the *Bibliotheca Patrum*. But the Lyons edition, not only contrary to the authority of the first exemplar but through a gross error, gives: “yet fifty days.” Lucifer, as was his custom, followed the Septuagint, where Jonah 3:4 reads ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι, “yet three days.” Nor did earlier Fathers differ from Lucifer. Yet in Origen’s Hexapla the ancient Greek translators Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion consistently have ἔτι τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέραι, “yet forty days,” as do the Hebrew, Syriac, and Chaldee [versions]. For this diversity of readings, commentators on the sacred Scriptures should be consulted. Gallandi. Sabatier also reads here: “Yet fifty days.”]

And the men of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and clothed themselves in sackcloth, from their greatest to their least. [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “in God . . . and they clothed themselves in sackcloth from the greatest to the least.”] [Note: The Vatican manuscript has *cilicia* (“haircloth garments”).] And the word reached the king of Nineveh; and he rose from his throne, took off his robe, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and sat upon ashes. [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “The word came to . . . from his throne . . . and he was covered with sackcloth . . . in ashes.” Sabatier reads *cilicio*, “with sackcloth.”] And it was proclaimed by the king of Nineveh and his officials, saying: “Let neither men nor cattle, oxen nor sheep, taste anything; let them neither eat nor drink water.” [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “It was proclaimed in Nineveh by the king and all his great men, saying: . . . and cattle . . . let them taste nothing, nor feed.”] And men and cattle put sackcloth about themselves, and men cried earnestly to God; and every one turned from his evil way and from the iniquity of his hands, saying: “Who knows whether God will repent and turn away from the wrath of his anger, so that we shall not perish?” [Note: Sabatier also reads *cilicio* here. The Old Latin Version has: “Men and cattle were covered with sackcloth, and they cried mightily to the Lord; and [each] turned . . . from [his] way . . . which was in their hands, saying.”] [Note: “And cattle” should be transferred upward, thus: “men and cattle put sackcloth about themselves,” as also in the Old Latin Version; nor should “men” after “cried” therefore be removed, as Latinius and Gallandi wished, although it is absent from the Old Latin Version.] [Note: With the Greek, *metanoēsei*, “will repent.” The Old Latin Version has: “Who knows whether God will turn and change his mind and turn away . . . and we shall not perish?” The word “change his mind” is absent from the Greek as from Lucifer. Sabatier reads: “Who knows whether God will turn and forgive, and turn back,” etc.] And God saw their work, because each had turned from his evil way; and God repented of the evil which he had said he would do to them, and did it not. [Note: Sabatier has “works.” The Old Latin Version has: “their works, because they turned from . . . and God had mercy concerning the evil which he had said that he would do,” etc.] [Note: Sabatier reads “which.”]

But Jonah was grieved with great grief and was distressed; and he prayed to God, saying (ibid. 4:1): “O Lord, were not these my words when I was still in the land? Therefore I hastened to flee to Tarshish, because I knew that you are compassionate and gracious, patient and merciful, repenting of evils.” [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “greatly, and he was confounded; and he prayed to the Lord and said . . . these . . . my words . . . in my land? Therefore I anticipated . . . for I know that you are merciful and compassionate, patient and of much compassion, and repenting concerning evils.”] And below: God said to Jonah (Jonah 2:9): “Are you greatly grieved over the gourd?” [Note: Latinius and Gallandi supply “And he said, ‘Greatly,’” from the Greek, Old Latin Version, and Vulgate. The Old Latin Version has: “And the Lord God said . . . ‘Are you greatly grieved over the gourd?’ And he said: ‘I am greatly grieved,’” etc.] He said: “I am greatly grieved, even unto death.” And the Lord said: “You spared the gourd, for which you did not labor or nourish it, which came up in a night and perished in a night. But shall I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which dwell more than one hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left?” [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “over the gourd, for which . . . in a night, and in a night it perished . . . shall I spare Nineveh, the great city,” etc.] [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “more than twelve myriads of persons, who do not know their right from their left, and much cattle?” Sabatier has: “who do not know what is between right and left.”]

And if God sees, Constantius, that you have rejected your wicked course; if he beholds your ruined ways corrected; if he sees you reformed in all things—believe me—you will begin to be among the servants of God in great blessedness.

You have, moreover, the example of the most blessed Apostle Paul, lest perhaps, as he did, you commit these things through ignorance; for as soon as you are converted to confess the only Son of God, forgiveness of your crimes will be granted to you, as it was to him. Follow him; take hold of his path; hear him speaking to the Philippians, and hear what he was before knowledge and how great a blessedness he deserved to attain after knowledge.

“If anyone thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the Law, a Pharisee; according to zeal, persecuting the Church; according to the righteousness which is in the Law, living without reproach. [Note: Greek from the Codex Boernerianus: *Ei tis de*, “If anyone else,” etc. The Old Latin Version has: “If any other,” etc.] [Note: Sabatier reads: “Circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe,” etc.] [Note: “Living” is absent from the Old Latin Version, which has “without fault” for “without reproach.”] But the things that were gain to me, these I counted loss for Christ’s sake. [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “But indeed I also reckon . . . losses . . . of my Lord.”] Indeed, I count all things loss because of the surpassing worth of the knowledge of Christ Jesus our Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things; and I count them dung, that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the Law, but that which is through faith in Jesus Christ, the righteousness which is from God in faith: that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being *cooneratus* [burdened together; the reading is textually uncertain] with his death, if by any means I may attain to his resurrection from the dead.” [Note: The Old Latin Version has: “I have made all things loss.”] [Note: The Old Latin Version omits “Jesus.”] [Note: The Old Latin Version omits “his.”]

[Note: The Old Latin has “to death”; the Latin text, following Greek συμμορφούμενος, has “conformed to death.” The reading *cooneratus* is very remarkable, and also occurs in Latin versions of the two very ancient codices Claromontanus and Sangermanensis. The source of this translation, unknown to Mill in the *Prolegomena to the New Testament*, §776, was explained by Krüster at the end of his preface to the revised Mill edition. For, he says, instead of συμμορφούμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ, “being conformed to his death,” as the modern Greek text of Philippians 3:10 reads, the Alexandrian and Colbert manuscripts have συμμορφιζόμενος. From this latter word arose another, corrupted and similar in sound, συνφορτιζόμενος, as it is read in the Greek-Latin Codex Boernerianus: συνφορτιζόμενος, *cooneratus*. Hence, the learned man adds, I am persuaded that συνφορτιζόμενος is to be attributed to scribal error in Greek manuscripts. Since this error subsequently spread into several Greek manuscripts, it is not surprising that Latin translators encountering such manuscripts formed their *cooneratus* from it. In any case, that this reading is inept is sufficiently clear from the sequence of words, as Wolf argues in his *Curae Philologicae et Criticae*, vol. IV, p. 141. Gallandi.]

As has already been said, imitate this man, follow him. Since he too had been what you now are—that is, a persecutor of the Church and a denier of the only Son of God—may you likewise be found converted from impiety to the embracing of the catholic faith, for the attaining of the heavenly kingdoms; may you likewise have made the passage from death to life.

Moreover, receive further proof, as Timothy reveals it, that he persecuted the Church through ignorance of God:

“We know that the Law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully, knowing this: that the Law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the unjust and disobedient, the impious and sinners, the wicked and profane, murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, murderers, the sexually immoral, men who lie with males, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine, according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God which was entrusted to me. [Note: Sabatier omits “is”; above p. 133, where the following words vary in Lucifer himself: “and for the disobedient . . . wicked,” with “murderers” omitted. See there Old Latin Version, note 1.] And I give thanks to Christ Jesus the Lord, who strengthened me, because he considered me faithful, appointing me to ministry—I who was formerly a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent man. [Note: As in the Greek, *Christō*, “to Christ,” etc. The Old Latin Version has: “strengthened me in Christ . . . our [Lord].”] But I obtained mercy because I acted ignorantly in unbelief. [Note: With the Greek, *en apistia*, “in unbelief.” The Old Latin Version has “into unbelief.”] And the grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.”

So you also, from being a persecutor, an insolent man, and a blasphemer, can become blessed and truly beloved of God, if, like blessed Paul, you believe Jesus Christ to be the true Son of God; if you confess that he has always reigned and will reign with the Father—that is, without beginning and without end; if you do not resist the sacred Scriptures when they proclaim that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit possess one eternity; and, finally, if you believe that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit possess one deity.

[Note: Lucifer employs a similar expression elsewhere, and in the book *On Not Agreeing with Heretics* affirms that the Father and Son are one deity. Petavius demonstrates from the Latin Fathers, and from Lucifer himself in book 4, chapter 14 of *On the Trinity*, that these words signify the highest unity and a single divine substance. Moreover, in book 8, chapter 8, he confirms that deity is a μονάς, that is, a most perfect and numerical unity. But see what we discussed concerning this expression in the Preface.]

Believe me: you will be among the choir of patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs. Otherwise, when you begin to see yourself tortured with the devil and all his attendants, God will charge you with having despised these our most health-giving warnings.

[Col. 0935]

# LETTER OF FLORENTIUS TO LUCIFER, BISHOP OF CALARIS. (C)

## LETTER

Florentius to the most kindly lord Lucifer.

[Col. 0935A]

A certain man presented to our lord and august [Col. 0935B] emperor, in your name, a codex [Note: That is, of the books which Lucifer wrote on behalf of St. Athanasius. See our Preface.]. He ordered that it be conveyed to Your Holiness, [Col. 0936A] and desires to know whether the same codex was sent by you. You must therefore write back what is true concerning the matter, and return the codex, so that it may be offered again to [Col. 0936B] His Eternity [Note: Thus the impious Constantius arrogated to himself the title “Eternity,” though, in defending Arius, he did not fear to diminish the Son of God, one of whose blasphemies, among others, was that there had been a time when the Son did not exist. Papebroch, vol. 4 of May, *Acta Sanctorum* of the Bollandists, commentary on ch. 2 of the History of St. Lucifer. Athanasius also mocks the designation αἰώνιος, “eternal,” applied to Constantius in the Sirmian Formula of the year 359, in his book *On the Synods*.].

[Col. 0935]

# LETTER OF LUCIFER, BISHOP OF CALARIS, TO FLORENTIUS. (C)

## LETTER

Lucifer, bishop, to Florentius, Master of the Offices [Note: The highest dignity in the imperial court, presiding over the Palatine officials and the emperor’s servants, and especially handling embassies from foreign peoples. See Valesius, notes on Ammianus Marcellinus, bk. 26, ch. 5. Florentius still held this office in 360, as Ammianus testifies, bk. 20, ch. 2; and in the following year Emperor Julian drove him into exile on the Dalmatian island of Boas, as the same Ammianus writes, bk. 22, ch. 3.].

[Col. 0935C]

The bearer of the codex whom Your Excellency mentions as having approached the emperor in my name was sent by my humble self; and the codex itself, as you have graciously informed me, was carefully examined and delivered to Bonosus, [Col. 0936C] an *agens in rebus* [Note: The *agentes in rebus* made up a Palatine administrative body, one of whose duties was to investigate throughout the provinces whether any criminal plot was being formed against the emperor; and this is why Lucifer’s books were delivered to Bonosus. See Valesius on Ammianus Marcellinus, bk. 15, ch. 3.], to be conveyed. Your devout prudence, most dear son, was to be instructed in these matters [Note: I think the reading should be *informanda*, “to be informed.” Tillemont correctly has this. Baronius, year 356, no. 67: *his informanda*.]. It will now be for your nobility, once this has been acknowledged by me, to defend it without any hesitation. For, by God’s favor, when he begins to examine the reasons why I have written in such a manner [Note: Papebroch, in the cited place, reads *talia*, “such things.”], he will find us joyfully standing against those things prepared for our death.

[Col. 0935]

# ONE BOOK OF OUR HOLY FATHER LUCIFER, BISHOP OF CALARIS, ON NOT SPARING THOSE WHO SIN AGAINST GOD, ADDRESSED TO EMPEROR CONSTANTIUS. (C)

[Col. 0935C] When you saw yourself, Emperor, defeated on every side by the servants of God [Note: Here Lucifer refers not only to what Catholic bishops had most steadfastly done against the threats and deceits of Constantius and the Arians—among whom Lucifer played a large part—but also to what they subsequently did with unconquered courage, both through books written against Constantius and through fortitude in enduring punishments and even death itself, rather than yield to the opinion of heretics. He says that Constantius was defeated in every respect [Col. 0937C], because the Catholic bishops never allowed themselves either to profess the Arian blasphemy, or to communicate with Arians, or to subscribe to the condemnation of Athanasius. The Arians had attempted by every means to extort these three things at the Council of Milan, and especially [Col. 0937D] from the legates of the pope.], you said that you had suffered and were suffering from [Col. 0937A] us an insult contrary to the admonitions of the sacred Scriptures. You say that we have behaved insolently toward you, whom it was fitting to honor. If any worshiper of God spared apostates [Note: That is, did not pursue apostates so that they might either return to the true worship of God or cease attacking true religion.], then what you say about us is true.

From where shall we begin, in order to prove that all wanderers have been rebuked by worshipers of God as you are now rebuked by us? From where, except from the acts of Moses, servant of God? We read in Exodus that Moses went up the mountain after the covenant had been delivered to him, and slew very many of them for the guilt of idolatry. “Moses,” it says, “stood [Note: Sabatier reads: “Moses stood at the gates of the camp and said, ‘Who is for the Lord? Let him come,’” etc.] at the gates of the camp and said: ‘Who is ready for the Lord? Let him come to me.’ And all the sons of Levi gathered to him. And he said to them: ‘Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let every one put his sword upon his thigh, and pass through and return from gate to [Col. 0937B] gate through the camp; and let every one kill his brother, every one his kinsman, and every one his neighbor.’ And the sons of Levi did as Moses said to them. And there fell from the people that day about three thousand men. And Moses said to them: ‘You have filled [that is, consecrated] your hands today to the Lord, every one against son or brother, so that a blessing may be given to you’” (Exod. XXXVI, 26) [Note: Sabatier reads: “You have consecrated your hands today . . . against his brother, that a blessing may be given to you”; but our edition agrees here with the Greek: ἐπληρώσατε, “you have filled,” and δοθῆναι ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς εὐλογίαν, “that a blessing be given upon you.”].

We are insulting to you as Moses was to that foolish people. Nor did they like what Moses said or did, once they had chosen not to serve God, who had delivered them from Pharaoh’s power, but that calf which fire had cast for them. So you too, now enslaved not to God but to the idolatry of Arius, because you are charged with error, bear it indignantly; you call us obstinate and say that we have committed an unworthy offense toward you, [Col. 0937C] daring to say to the emperor of the Roman realm: “Constantius, you do wrong to introduce idolatry into the Church.”

Moses, that first of the prophets, most devoted to God, pursued with the sword those whom you have made yourself their imitator; and am I held to be obstinate by you because I said that you had abandoned God and enslaved yourself to idolatry? The sacred Scripture further declares that the children of Israel committed fornication with the daughters of Moab, that they were invited by them to eat things sacrificed to idols, and that they worshiped those same idols. Because Phinehas the priest, inflamed with the zeal of devotion, burned so fiercely against them—especially because he slew the idolaters [Note: *Idololatras*, “idolaters”: the Latin text.] with the sword in the midst of the assembly—he so pleased God that it is written that, through this deed, the wrath of the indignant Lord was stilled and that Phinehas himself became preeminent before the Lord:

“And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: ‘Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, restrained [Col. 0938A] my wrath from the children of Israel [Note: The Old Latin version: “Turned away my fury.”], because he was zealous with my zeal among them [Note: Closer to the Greek: ἐν τῷ ζηλῶσαί μου τὸν ζῆλον ἐν αὐτοῖς, “in being zealous with my zeal among them.” Old Latin: “In that he emulated my zeal among them.”], so that I might not destroy [Note: The Vatican manuscript has *ut non ἐξανέλουσα*, “so that I might not kill.” In an old codex it reads *ut non ἐξανήλωσα*, with “kill” added above the line by another hand. Tillemont: this is the Greek reading, ἐξανήλωσα, “I consumed”; the word was corrupted in the Vatican codex. Old Latin: “and I did not consume.”] the children of Israel in my zeal. And behold, I shall give him my covenant, a covenant of peace, to him and to his seed after him, a covenant of everlasting priesthood, because [Note: Old Latin: “Because he emulated his God and did not entreat,” etc. Lucifer agrees with the Greek: ἐζήλωσε τῷ Θεῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξιλάσατο, “he was zealous for his God and made propitiation,” that is, interceded.] he was zealous for his God and interceded for the children of Israel’” (Num. XXV, 10) [Note: Old Latin: “As I said: Behold, I give him the covenant of peace, and it shall be to him and to his seed after him a covenant,” etc.].

And do you judge us obstinate because we tell you the truth when you err? Do you suppose that, when we displease you, we then do not please God? But I ask [Col. 0938B] you, Constantius: by what authority did you wish us to abandon the way of the righteous patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs, and embrace this new way of yours, which the devil established through Arius? Were you perhaps warned in a dream and told that you must not allow us to hold the way of Christ—the way held by Abel, Enoch, Noah, Melchizedek, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Joshua son of Nun, Job, the Judges, and the other kings, namely David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, and Josiah; the way held by all the prophets, apostles, and martyrs; the way held by all who are found to have pleased God?

If this was said to you by the prince of demons, hear what God decreed through the glorious prophet Moses should be done to you:

“If a prophet arises among you, or one dreaming a dream, [Col. 0938C] and gives you a sign or wonder, and the sign or wonder comes to pass [Note: Old Latin: “And it comes to pass, and he says: ‘Let us go,’” etc. The Greek has πρὸς σέ, “to you,” as Lucifer does.], and he says to you: ‘Let us go and serve other gods [Note: Old Latin: “Let us go . . . after other gods whom you do not know; do not listen to the word . . . of that dreamer, because,” etc.], whom you do not know,’ you shall not hear the word of that prophet or dreamer, because the Lord God tests you [Note: Old Latin: “The Lord your God, to know whether with all your heart,” etc., “you fear God.” Greek: εἰδέναι, εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε (Κύριον τὸν, from the Alexandrian and Oxford manuscripts) Θεὸν ὑμῶν—“to know whether you love the Lord your God”—as in Lucifer.], to see whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul. You shall go after [Note: Old Latin: “After God,” etc. The Greek agrees with Lucifer.] the Lord your God; you shall fear him, keep his commandments, hear his voice, and cleave to him. And that prophet [Col. 0939A] or dreamer of dreams [Note: With the Greek, ἐνύπνιον ἐνυπνιαζόμενος, “one dreaming a dream.” Old Latin: “dreamer.”] shall die [Note: The Latin, following the Greek, reads: “that one shall die,” ἐκεῖνος ἀποθανεῖται. Old Latin: “He shall die.”], for they have spoken in order to lead you astray from the Lord your God” (Deut. XIII, 1) [Note: Old Latin: “For he has spoken in order to lead you astray from the Lord your God.”].

Do you recognize what you have been commanded to suffer? Whether you say that you were warned in a dream, or whether you wish to assert yourself to us as a prophet, you are an enemy of God, since you wish us to abandon the apostolic faith and accept that faith which denies the only Son of God. For it is evident that all those whom I have named became so great and such men because they believed in the only Son of God. For “he who does not believe in the Son does not have the Father; but he who believes in the Son has both the Father and the Son” (I John) [Note: Old Latin: “He who denies the Son has neither the Son nor the Father; and he who confesses the Son has both the Son and the Father.”].

Since this is the utterance of blessed John, and since the choir of the holy apostles agrees with him, you ought certainly to understand that the patriarchs [Col. 0939B] and prophets had believed beforehand just as the apostles believed, as likewise did all who are known to have been honored for the merit of faith. For you cannot prove to me that Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob believed one way, while John and all his fellow apostles believed another. For if the apostles did not believe as the patriarchs believed, why does blessed Paul urge all to embrace Abraham’s faith?

But you say: “I charge you with being insolent, with having been insulting to the emperor,” [Note: Especially by publishing books on behalf of St. Athanasius.] “and you recount the question of faith.” It is indeed a question of faith: that I may prove you sacrilegious, that I may prove that you have wandered from the way of truth. This is why I seem insulting to you: because I tell you that you have abandoned the path of all worshipers of God and taken up that path which those have held and still hold who served and still serve not God, but a phantom.

Hear, then, what God decreed through Moses should be done concerning you, who urge me to depart from God [Col. 0939C]:

“If your brother, born of your father or mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife who lies in your bosom, or a friend equal to your own soul, secretly urges you, saying: ‘Let us go and serve foreign gods [Note: Sabatier reads: “other gods, whom neither you nor your fathers know”; Old Latin: “other gods whom you do not know . . . among the gods . . . which are near you or far away.”], whom neither you nor your fathers know, among the gods of the nations around you, whether nearby [Col. 0940A] or far away [Note: The Latin, following the Greek, adds: “from one end of the earth to the other”; but these words are absent from the Oxford Greek manuscript cited by Sabatier.], you shall not be willing to go with him or listen to him. Your eye shall not spare him, nor [Note: Old Latin: “nor shall you pity him.”] shall you greet him, nor conceal him. You shall certainly report him; your hand shall be first against him to put him to death [Note: As in the Greek, αὐτόν· καὶ αἱ χεῖρες . . . ἐπ’ ἐσχάτῳ. The Old Latin omits “him” and has “the hand of all the people last.”], and the hand of your people afterward. You shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away [Note: “He sought to turn you away.” Old Latin: Ἀποστῆσαί σε, Greek.] from the Lord your God” (Deut. XIII, 6).

You are commanded to be put to death, since you invite me to abandon God; yet in ignorance you say: “Lucifer insults me.” Or will you deny that you invited us to embrace idolatry? [Note: By this expression one may understand either the letter or edict issued in Constantius’s name, especially to the Catholic bishops at the Council of Milan, that they should subscribe to it against the Nicene faith; or simply the Arian heresy, which Constantius vigorously supported throughout his life.] If you think it should be denied, the expositions [Note: That is, the Arian formulas of faith which the teachers and defenders of this sect issued over about nineteen years. Petavius enumerates fourteen of them in bk. I, *On the Trinity*, ch. 9; the last appears to have been composed at Antioch in 360. They differed from and contradicted one another to such an extent that, continually minting new formulas and rejecting and condemning the former ones, they proposed others as though making testaments. Athanasius reproaches them with this in Oration I against the Arians; they made themselves an object of universal ridicule and contempt. As Petavius says in the place cited, all their decrees, made obsolete and rejected not by others but by their very authors, stain their authors with the disgrace of sacrilegious falsehood and faithlessness, no. 13.] of the bishops of your sect—your fellow blasphemers—will convict you; the documents read out by you and given at Rome even to Catholic bishops will convict you, [Note: On Lucifer’s meaning here—whether he refers to what Constantius did at Rome for the Arians, or to the Sirmian Formula of 357, or to the Ariminian or Acacian formula published at the Council of Constantinople held at the end of 359 and the beginning of the following year—see what we have discussed in the Preface, and compare note 6 below, p. 54 [here col. 820, note h].] namely, in order that your blasphemy might be strengthened everywhere.

Do you not perceive into what [Col. 0940B] darkness of errors you have fallen? Do you not see how you may perish, when you observe why Achan, one man from among the people, was punished with death: because, contrary to the divine commands, he stole from Jericho a certain portion of a garment, silver, and gold? Consider what awaits you, who deny the eternal divine majesty of the only Son of God. Hear what was done in Achan’s case; and finally take thought for your salvation. Return to God’s Church, from which that fugitive serpent, who also deceived Adam and Eve, drove you away through the Arians [Note: That is, “from which that fugitive serpent drove and expelled you,” the serpent who deceived Adam and Eve; *abigavit* is used for *abegit*, “drove away.” Tillemont, La Cerda, and Du Cange, *Glossary*.]:

“And,” it says, “the Lord was with Joshua [Note: Thus the Greek consistently reads. Sabatier has *Josue* in Lucifer.], and his name was over all the earth” (Josh. VI, 27). “And the children of Israel committed a great offense [Note: The Latin, following the Greek: “a great offense.”], and fraudulently took something from what was devoted to destruction; and the Lord was angry with the children of Israel. And Joshua sent men to Ai, which is [Col. 0940C] near Bethel, saying: ‘Examine Ai.’ And the men went up and examined Ai; and they returned to Joshua and said to him: ‘Let not all the people go up, but let two or three thousand men go up and destroy the city. Do not bring all the people there [Note: Instead of “Do not lead all the people against them”: Lucifer very frequently inverts expressions in the manner of the Greeks, which makes him seem more obscure and rough. Tillemont and La Cerda. But the better correction is “do not bring [them] there,” as in the Latin and Sabatier, following the Greek.], for they are few.’ So about [Col. 0941A] three thousand men went up with him, and they fled before the men who were in Ai. And the men of Ai killed thirty-six of them, pursued them from the gate [Note: The Latin, following the Vulgate, adds: “as far as Shebarim.”], struck them on the descent, and the heart of the people was dismayed and became as water.

“And Joshua tore his garments, and Joshua [Note: Joshua is omitted by Sabatier but is found in the Greek.] fell on his face before God until evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust upon their heads. And Joshua said: ‘I beseech you [Note: Sabatier reads differently in Lucifer: “Alas, Lord God, why did you will to bring this people across the river Jordan, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorite and destroy us?” Yet our text agrees with the Greek: Δέομαι, Κύριε, ἱνατί διεβίβασεν ὁ παῖς σου τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὸν Ἰορδάνην παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῷ Ἀμοῤῥαίῳ ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; “I beseech you, Lord, why has your servant brought this people across the Jordan, to deliver him to the Amorite, to destroy us?” Sabatier then has: “Would that, as we began, we had remained beyond the Jordan,” which is closer to the Greek: Καὶ εἰ κατεμείναμεν, καὶ κατῳκίσθημεν παρὰ τὸν Ἰορδάνην, alternatively πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.], Lord, why has your servant brought this people across the Jordan, to deliver him to the Amorite, to destroy us? If we remained in the land, we dwelt by the Jordan! What shall I say, when Israel has turned its back before its enemy? The Canaanite and all who inhabit the land [Note: From the Greek, τὴν γῆν, “the land.” Sabatier: “in the land.”] will hear, surround us, and [Note: Sabatier: “And they will blot out our name from the earth; and what will you do for your great name?” The Greek is nearly as in our edition: Καὶ ἐκτρίψουσιν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς· καὶ τί ποιήσεις τὸ ὄνομά σου τὸ μέγα;] drive us from the land; and what will you do for your great name?’

“And [Col. 0941B] the Lord said to Joshua: ‘Rise; why have you fallen upon your face? The people have sinned and transgressed my covenant, which I established for them. They have stolen from what was devoted to destruction and put it [Note: Sabatier: “And hid it among their vessels.”] among their vessels. The children of Israel will not be able to stand before their enemies; they will turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become a thing devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove the devoted thing from among yourselves. Rise, sanctify the people, and say [Note: Sabatier: “Say to them, ‘Be sanctified tomorrow.’” “To them” is absent from the Greek.]: “Let them be sanctified tomorrow. For thus says the Lord God of Israel: A devoted thing is among you. You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among yourselves. Come together in the morning, tribe by tribe [Note: “By your tribes,” as in certain Greek manuscripts. Sabatier.]; and the tribe which God indicates in the morning shall be brought by clans; the clan which the Lord indicates shall be brought by man; and whoever [Col. 0941C] is indicated by the Lord shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he transgressed the covenant of the Lord and committed iniquity in Israel.”’

“And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought the people forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was indicated. They were brought forward by clans, and the clan of Zerah was indicated. He brought forward the clan of Zerah by households, and the household of Jambri was indicated [Note: Zambri in the Latin, as in the Hexapla with an asterisk.]. And the household was brought forward man by man, and Achar [Note: Thus in the Oxford Greek manuscript: Ἄχαρ υἱὸς Χαρμί, “Achar son of Charmi.” Sabatier consistently has Achan. Cotelerius, on bk. II, ch. 10 of the *Apostolic Constitutions*, proves that Achar is the correct pronunciation of this name.] son of Charmi, son of Jambri, was indicated.

“And Joshua said to Achar: ‘Give glory today to the Lord God of Israel, make confession, tell me what you have done, and do not conceal it from me.’ Achar answered Joshua and said: ‘Truly I sinned before the Lord God of Israel. This and this I did: among the spoil I saw a beautiful multicolored garment, [Col. 0942A] two hundred shekels of silver, a didrachm, and one gold bar of fifty didrachms. I coveted it [Note: “It”: the Latin, as in the Greek.], and took it; and behold, these things are hidden in my tent, and the silver is hidden beneath them.’

“Then Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and these things were hidden in the tent, with the silver beneath them. They took them from the tent, brought them to Joshua and the elders of Israel, and placed them before God. And [Note: “And” is omitted by Sabatier.] they seized Achar son of Charmi, and brought him into the valley of Achar [Note: The same Sabatier has Achor.], together with his sons and daughters, his calves, his yoke-beasts, his sheep, his tent, and all that was his; and all Israel was with him. They brought them to Mecachor. And Joshua said to Achar: ‘Why have you destroyed us? May the Lord destroy you as on this [Col. 0942B] day.’ And all Israel stoned him with stones [Note: Sabatier has the singular, “stoned,” and “a heap of stones”; the Greek has the plural, ἐλιθοβόλησαν.], and they piled a great heap of stones over him. And the Lord ceased from the indignation of his wrath” (Josh. VII, 1).

Consider, Constantius, by what example you will perish unless you yourself take heed, and what punishments you will pay eternally. Achar suffered such things because he transgressed the commandments; from this you may understand what you deserve, since you are an apostate. For if he was punished with so great a destruction because he took from what was devoted to destruction, how much more, without doubt, will you be punished more severely, since you have become anathema by denying the Son of God!

In this, before you, we are wicked; in this proud, obstinate, and insolent: because we tell you, “You have committed sacrilege by becoming a denier of the only Son of God”; because we say, “Take thought for yourself; rescue your soul from the snares of the devil.” What new thing do we bishops do [Col. 0942C] if we tell you what you deserve to hear? For we find that Samuel, that most holy priest of God, said to King Saul what you will read below:

“Pains and groans shall be brought upon you [Note: In the book *On the Apostate King*, this is translated “you have brought”; here it agrees with the manuscript version of Fleury cited by Sabatier.]. Because you have treated the word of the Lord as of no account, the Lord will treat you as of no account, that you may not reign” (I Reg. XV, 23).

And again: “Because [Note: Old Latin: “Because you have despised the word of the Lord, the Lord will despise you.”] you have treated the word of the Lord as of no account, God will reduce you to nothing, that you may not be king over Israel” (ibid., 26).

And below: “The Lord will tear [Note: See the same passages in *On the Apostate King*, p. 33 [here col. 798].] your kingdom from Israel out of your hand today, and give it to your neighbor, who is better than you” (ibid., 28).

If he said these things to Saul because Saul had disregarded the Lord’s commandments, why do you think that we could not [Col. 0943A] openly say that you are sacrilegious, and that unless you turn yourself to God, he will reduce you to nothing? If we had not exhorted you, if we had not called you to repentance, you would rightly say that we hated you. But when you hear us say, “Repent, Emperor; correct your ways, that you may find a place for mercy,” you ought, I think, to consider that you are cherished and loved by us. Yet you curse us for remaining in the apostolic faith; you return evil for good.

We do not wonder that you, since you depart from God’s will and do not cease to perform the devil’s desire, return evil to those who ask and desire God to do good to you. For wrong-doing has become innate in you, since you have passed from good to evil—that is, to the devil.

[Col. 0943B] If you persecute us while we love you and desire every highest good to befall you, this is neither great nor new, since Saul also persecuted that prophet and priest of the Lord, Samuel. He persecuted the man through whom he himself had been anointed king and whose prayers were continually directed to the Lord in unceasing entreaty for the safety of that very persecutor. If you do not believe us, God’s priests, that we grieve for you because you have absorbed such darkness of errors and are thus slaughtering yourself, believe God speaking to Samuel concerning Saul: “How long [Note: In the same place Lucifer has *quousque*, “how long,” for *usquequo*.] do you mourn for Saul? Behold, I cast him out from reigning over Israel” (I Reg. XVI, 1).

And above: “And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: ‘I repent that I made Saul king, because he has turned away from me and has [Col. 0943C] not kept my words.’ And Samuel was grieved and cried to the Lord throughout the night and until dawn” (ibid. XV, 10) [Note: See the same passage in the same book, p. 32 [here col. 797], where *Samuelem* appears for *Samuel*, and “to God” for “to the Lord.” The final words are likewise punctuated: “throughout the night and until dawn.”].

Although the priest Samuel did these things for the welfare of King Saul, Saul afterward persecuted Samuel, wretchedly failing to recognize that he was persecuting the Lord’s prophet and priest. So you also, ignorant of what you are doing, persecute us, who desire you to please God; and you love those who drag you with themselves to eternal death, to the Lord’s perpetual offense. You are angry because you hear the truth, though you see that Samuel, priest of the Lord, did not flatter [Note: Tillemont says that the passage is corrupt and corrects it, with the Latin: “did not flatter the king. Or perhaps,” etc. Yet expressions of this kind are not alien to Lucifer’s style. The passage may be retained if read: “that the mind did not flatter the king,” for “the king’s mind.” Gallandius agrees with Latinius.] the king’s mind.

What ought our predecessors to have done differently from us? Because we tell you the truth, we seem proud to you. What have you heard from us? Surely, that you are a murderer. If we lie, then we are rightly called insulting and proud [Col. 0943D] by you; but if we speak the truth, we are not insulting, but imitate those who, by not flattering those entrusted to them but by giving them salutary warning, deserved to become most beloved by God.

When the king of Israel sent to kill the prophet Elisha, if you had not read that Elisha said to those who were with him, “Have you seen that the son of that murderer [Col. 0944A] has sent [Note: Old Latin: “to take away my head.”] to take away my head?” (IV Kings VI, 32), you would rightly charge me as guilty of wrongs. Filled with the Holy Spirit, the prophet called the king of Israel the son of a murderer—that is, the son of the devil—not because he called that king’s carnal father a murderer, but because he meant the devil. The king showed himself to be the devil’s son by daring to kill the servants of God, the prophets of his mercy, just as you now reveal yourself by your actions.

The devil urges your hearts to do all these things. That this is so, receive the Lord’s words to the Jews in the Gospel: “You were born of your father the devil, and you wish to do the desires of your father; for he was a murderer from the beginning” (John VIII, 44) [Note: See the same passage in bk. II on behalf of St. Athanasius, p. 118 and note 1 [here col. 884 and note c, col. 883].].

I say that the prophet of the Lord, full of the Holy Spirit, calls the king of Israel the son of a murderer, that is, of the devil, [Col. 0944B] and yet you think that we insult you because we call you a killer of God’s servants, an executioner of our bodies, a man whose whole purpose is injustice, a destroyer of religion, a denier of the only Son of God? What we see you do, that we say [Note: Our text, with Latinius, reads: “these things we say.” Tillemont: “This we have learned.”]; what you are, that we proclaim you to be. You call us insolent because we tell you what you are.

Tell me, I ask, why the king of Israel deserved to hear such things from the Lord: “Because you have done what is good before me, and have done according to my heart and according to my soul to the house of Ahab, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit for you upon the throne of Israel” (IV Kings X, 30). Tell me, then, why did he deserve to hear this from God? Because he spared God’s enemies? Or because he pursued them even with the sword most fiercely? Or because he killed [Col. 0944C] the idolatrous son of Ahab and his forty sons? It pleases God that he cast down Queen Jezebel, when slain, to the dogs; that he destroyed by the sword the servants of Baal, together with all the priests and prophets of confusion; and that he destroyed the images.

What ought we to have done toward you, that you might not mark us as guilty of insult against you, when we see you holding the ways of Ahab and Jezebel? What you do is not new: you act against God, attack his house, and persecute his bishops, through whom he warns you to take thought for yourself and, while there is room for repentance, draw yourself back from evil.

Before your time there were men like you in sacrilege, serving idols after abandoning the God of their fathers. In the Second Book of Chronicles we read [Note: Read *legimus*, “we read,” with Gallandius.] that Amaziah king of Judah was warned by God through [Col. 0944D] a prophet not to take with him to war men from the children of Israel, whom he had hired for a hundred thousand talents [Note: “Thousands” is omitted from the Latin, following the Vulgate, II Chron. XXV, 9, and the Greek.] of silver, because God had abandoned Israel: for they had abandoned God and served idols. The king obeyed the prophet’s words and believed that the threat was from God.

[Col. 0945A] What does he do here? [Note: Thus correctly with the Latin. Previously it was read: “because he does this here,” etc.] After subduing his enemies, he thought that their idols should be removed and transferred to his own kingdom, and should themselves be worshipped. Because that man of God told him that he had acted wrongly in abandoning God to worship the idols of the nations, this king vigorously persecuted the prophet of the Lord. You see that, once you have turned to apostasy, you have always had one purpose: to persecute those who wish you well.

And, Holy Scripture says, it came to pass, after Amaziah came to smite Idumea, that he brought thence the gods of Mount Seir and set them up as gods for himself; before them he worshipped, and to them he sacrificed. And the anger of the Lord came upon Amaziah, and he sent to him the prophet Benaiah; and Benaiah said to him: “Why have you sought the gods of the people, who did not deliver their own people [Col. 0945B] from your hand?” And it came to pass, while he was speaking to him, that he said to him: “Have I appointed you the king’s counsellor? Take heed lest you be scourged” (2 Chronicles 25:14 ff.). [Note: “Upon him” is omitted by the Latin and is absent also from the Greek.] [Note: The same Lucifer reads *be silent* somewhat below; but “take heed for yourself” is more suitable. Greek: πρόσεχε, “take heed.”]

You see, Constantius, how mad you become after it pleases you to live as servants of the devil; after it pleases you not to know God, who is all-powerful; after you choose, as an insult to God, to establish idolatry. For just as he said, “Have I appointed you the king’s counsellor? Take heed lest you be scourged” (ibid., v. 16)—[Note: The same Lucifer omits *in* above and a little below.]—so you too say: “Have I chosen you as my counsellors, that I should not act as pleases me, that I should not hold the way which Arius held?” Do you not see by what example Arius perished, and how divine vengeance was taken upon him? [Note: “Was taken,” Vatican manuscript.]

Meanwhile, because you say that we are insulting to you, see that this man of God did not spare that king of yours, your fellow-sacrilegious man; but, after he had been told, “Be silent, lest you be scourged” (ibid.), he said to him: “I know that the Lord God will destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my counsel.” [Col. 0945C] In what respect do you regard us as insulting? Surely because we say to you: “We know that, unless you take care to turn to God, the Lord will condemn you to eternal punishment” (ibid.). This is the insult, this the whole injury: that God’s bishops tell you that you will perish eternally unless you reform your ways.

That king did not believe the man of God. Holy Scripture tells us what immediately befell him:

“And at the time when Amaziah departed from the Lord, they rose against him in revolt. And he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish, and they killed him in Lachish” (ibid., v. 27).

Thus could the deeds of your evils [Col. 0945D] preserve, protect, and defend you, just as they did him who said to the man of God speaking for his salvation: “Have I appointed you the king’s counsellor? Be silent, lest you be scourged.” [Note: The same Lucifer above has *I gave* in place of *I appointed*.]

It is not we who first acted in this way when we say to you, wandering from the truth, resisting God’s ordinance, and labouring to establish new ways: “You do wrong not to follow the way by which all worshippers of God have reached the heavenly kingdoms.”

You have read of King Uzziah, rebuked by the priests of the Lord because he had dared to do what was unlawful:

“And, Scripture says, he entered the temple of the Lord to put incense upon the altar; and Azariah the priest entered after him, and with him thirty priests of the Lord, sons of valour, and they stood against King Uzziah and said to him: ‘It is not lawful for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been consecrated, to burn it. Depart from the sanctuary, because you have departed from the Lord; and this shall not be to your honour from the Lord God’” (2 Chronicles 26:16 ff.). [Note: The copyist altered these names: for the old codex reads “King Odias” and calls the priest Uzziah rather than Azariah. Tillemont: *Odias*; Vatican and Latin: *Odias*, the one called King Uzziah in the Vulgate.] [Note: The same person as Azariah in the Vulgate.] [Note: “Eighty,” Latin from the Greek.]

Do you say that the Lord’s priests were insulting to that king, or not? [Note: “Them,” Latin.] If they were not insulting, neither should we seem so to you, since you hear from us things like those he heard: “It is not lawful for you, Constantius, to join with the Arian the people of God. It is not lawful for you, author of the idolatry of the Arian heresy, denier of the only Son of God, to judge God’s priests—sacrilegious as you are, pretending to be a Christian while you are the forerunner of Antichrist.” [Note: “Sacrilegious,” same source. “Sacrilegious, pretending”: this is better.]

“It shall not turn out well for you to remove the orders of God’s priests and appoint in their place [Col. 0946B] his enemies—namely, associates in your sacrilege.” [Note: This concerns Arian bishops whom Constantius ordered to be set over Catholic churches, as has already been stated in the preceding books.]

When you hear this, you are angry with us. King Uzziah too was angry then with those priests of the Lord. But observe that those consecrated to God retained forever the honour of their station, whereas Uzziah was immediately stained, unto everlasting reproach, by the disfiguring blot of leprosy:

“And Uzziah was angry, and in his hand was an altar [Note: Galland contends that in Lucifer’s Greek exemplar θυσιαστήριον, “altar,” was wrongly written for θυμιατήριον, “censer,” as the Septuagint has it.
