Yet perhaps the sense is that he held the altar in his hands; Sabatier has the same reading.] in order to burn incense on the altar; and leprosy appeared on his forehead in the sight of the priests in the house of the Lord” (ibid., v. 19). [Col. 0946C] [Note: “On his altar,” Vatican.]

These things are so; and do you suppose that you, a stubborn transgressor, will not incur offence before him who has commanded us forever to perform the duties of priesthood before his majesty? What is this pride of ours, Constantius, or what arrogance? Is it because we see you sick, pestilential—because you are an Arian—and see in you the leprosy which Arius had; because we urge you to withdraw from the people of God, as those priests of the Lord compelled Uzziah to leave the temple; because we thus compel you to give honour to God?

For if God’s priests expelled Uzziah from God’s court because they remembered the divine command that lepers were forbidden to enter the temple before purification, [Col. 0946D] how much more rightly should we—see this [Note: “You see,” Latin.]—expel you from Christ’s Church, from the Lord’s house, since it is not lawful for a heretic to join with Catholics, a madman with the sane, one full of unclean spirits with those in whom the Spirit of God dwells!

What insult is this, if the priests of the Lord, inflamed with the zeal that has always animated our predecessors, tell you what conduces to our salvation and yours? “Lucifer is insolent,” you say. Insolent for this reason: because I urge you to reject Arius’s leprosy, and to obtain, through the faith preached by the most blessed apostles and which, as you see, we hold, health for your mind; and, wholly rescued from the snares of the devil, to rejoice that you yourself have been gained for God forever. [Note: “Having obtained the health of your mind,” same source. I judge the text ought more correctly to be amended thus: “having obtained health for your mind,” so that the sense is: “and, having obtained through this faith … health for your mind, and being wholly rescued … you may rejoice,” etc.]

You who accuse us of excessive haughtiness, have you found written what King Josiah of Judah did to your fellow-sacrilegious men, to men such as you are seen to be today—how he persecuted very many of them even after death, consuming their bones by fire? [Note: “What,” same source.] [Col. 0947B] [Note: “If,” same source.]

But it befitted that king to pursue God’s enemies with such zeal; whereas it was improper for us bishops, us priests of God, to resist you when you introduced idolatry into the Church! He killed your fellow-sacrilegious men with the sword; he pursued even remains long buried, desiring to be found a most faithful worshipper of God. But we, on the contrary, ought not even to resist you in word—you, friend of God’s enemy; you, most dear to all the angels who turned to apostasy; [Note: By this name he implies the bishops who had deserted the Nicene faith, as John the Apostle in the Apocalypse also bestows this title of honour and dignity upon bishops; nevertheless, perhaps he here means apostate angels, that is, demons.] you who by this blasphemy of yours have become God’s enemy.

Receive therefore from the Fourth Book of Kings what Josiah, servant of the Lord and king of Judah, obtained because of what he did concerning your unclean associates; [Note: “Juda,” Latin.] and at last cease to say of us, “They are proud and insulting.”

“He did,” Scripture says, [Col. 0947C] “what was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father David, and did not turn aside to right or left” (2 Kings 22:2).

Again below, after he restored the houses of the Lord and the priest had sent the book of the Law to the king:

“And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the book of the Law, that he tore his garments” (ibid., v. 11). “And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying: ‘Seek the Lord for me and for all Judah concerning the words of this book which has been found, for the great wrath of the Lord has been kindled against us because our fathers did not heed [Col. 0948A] the words of this book, to do according to all that is written for us.’

“And Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, [Note: Galland corrects from the Greek Alexandrian Codex: “son of Thecue, son of Harhas,” etc.] keeper of the garments; and she dwelt in Jerusalem. And they spoke to her according to these things. And she said to them: ‘Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man [Note: Sabatier reads: “Say to the man who sent you to me: Thus says …”] who sent you to me, says the Lord: Behold, I shall bring evils upon this place and upon its inhabitants, according to all the words of this book which the king of Judah has read, because they abandoned me and attended to foreign gods and provoked me by the works of their hands. My wrath is kindled against this place and shall not be quenched.

“‘And to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, you shall say: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: “Because you heard my words and were moved before [Col. 0948B] me, because you heard what I spoke against this place [Note: As in the Greek, ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τοῦτον, “against this place”; Vatican and Sabatier. “In this place,” Sabatier.] and its inhabitants, that it should become a desolation [Note: “A desolation,” Sabatier.] and a curse; and because you tore your garments and wept before me, I also have heard, says the Lord of hosts. Therefore I will take you away [Note: Sabatier: “I will gather … and you shall be gathered to [Col. 0948C] your grave in peace, and they shall not see,” etc. Galland corrects *I bring you*; but *I take you away* should be retained, that is, “I take you away from the place of affliction to your fathers.”] to your fathers, and you shall be gathered in peace, and your eyes shall see [Note: Galland adds *not*, without Greek support, following Sabatier.] all the evils that I am bringing [Note: With the Greek ἐπάγω, “I bring”; Sabatier: “I shall bring.”] upon this place and its inhabitants.”’” [Note: “Its inhabitants,” Vatican.]

And she returned an answer to the king. Then King Josiah sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah in Jerusalem (ibid., 23:1), and the king went up to the Lord, and all the men of Judah, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. And the king read in the ears of the people all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord. And the king stood by the pillar and established the covenant which had been found [Note: “Which had been found,” same source with Sabatier.] in the house of the Lord, before the Lord: [Col. 0948C] to go [Note: Greek: τοῦ πορεύεσθαι, “to go.” Sabatier: “that they should go … and observe,” etc. Here, as often elsewhere, Lucifer adheres to the letter. Galland.] after the Lord and to observe his commandments, testimonies, and precepts with all his heart [Note: “With their heart … They should establish,” Sabatier.] and all his soul, to establish all the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people entered into the covenant which the king established from the book.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the keepers of the ephod, to cast out from the house of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and Asherah [Note: Not erroneously, as Galland observes. Selden, *De Diis Syris*, syntagma 2, chapter 2, proves Asherah to have been a Sidonian divinity; Beyer confirms this in additions to Selden’s book. Or *Asherah* may mean wooden images dedicated to Ashtoreth, a Sidonian divinity, as Selden himself observes there. There is merely an orthographical error, and it should be written *Asherah* or *Ashera*.] and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the burning-place of the brook Kidron. [Note: Sabatier: “in the valley of Kidron.” Yet “in the burning-place” is correctly read, denoting the place where corpses of the dead were burned. Galland.] And he took their ashes and scattered them into the brook, [Col. 0949A] and went to Bethel.

And he burned the priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed [Note: “Of Judah, and in the high places,” Sabatier.] to burn incense in the high places of the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem—to those who burned incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven. And they brought out from the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, [Note: Greek: εἰς τὸν χειμάρρουν, “to the torrent.” Sabatier: “to the valley,” omitting “outside.”] and he ground the ashes fine and threw them into the burial-place of the common people. And he drove out the sons of those who were in the house of the Lord, whose women ministered there for garments. And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the sanctuaries where the priests burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; and he pulled down their high places. [Note: Clearly a printer’s error: correct, with Sabatier, “from Geba to Beersheba”; Sabatier also reads “destroyed” for “pulled down.”]

And below: “And he defiled Topheth [Note: I correct Lucifer in this word: it should be written *Pheth*, which was in Gehenna, or Gehennam, Gehennom, Gehenennom. The valley is designated by these names. Lucifer apparently read τὸ φὲθ τὸ for Τόφεθ τὸ, as in the Complutensian edition. Cotelerius, *Constitutiones Apostolicae*, book 2, chapter 22.] which was in Gehenna” (2 Kings 23:10), because they led each one his son and daughter through fire to Molech. [Note: “He had led,” and “into the fire,” in Sabatier.]

The kings of Judah had placed [Note: These words are partly corrupt through a copyist’s fault, partly different and drawn from an unknown source. Read thus from Sabatier: “He also removed the horses which the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the temple of the Lord, beside the chamber of Nathan-melech the eunuch, which was in Parvarim; but the chariots of the sun he burned with fire.” Cotelerius corrects this passage, *Patres Apostolici*, vol. I, note 27 on *Apostolic Constitutions*, book 2, chapter 57: “And he removed the horses which the kings of Judah had placed for the sun from the entrance of the house of the Lord to the pastophorium of Nathan, the king’s eunuch, which was in Pharurim (or Farvadim). And he burned the fountain of the sun with fire.” Or: “And he burned the horses which the kings of Judah had placed for the sun from the entrance of the house of the Lord to the pastophorium, which the king’s eunuch, who was in Pharurim, had placed,” etc. (for *Nathan*, as a proper name, signifies “he placed”). In Greek: “Καὶ κατέκαυσε τοὺς ἵππους οὓς ἔδωκαν βασιλεῖς Ἰούδα τῷ ἡλίῳ ἐν τῇ εἰσόδῳ οἴκου Κυρίου εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον Ναθὰν βασιλέως τοῦ εὐνούχου ἐν Φαρουρίμ· καὶ τὸ ἅρμα τοῦ ἡλίου κατέκαυσεν πυρί” — “And he burned the horses which the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, at the treasury of Nathan, the king’s eunuch, in Pharurim; and he burned the chariot of the sun with fire.” Bochart, *Hieroz.* reads [Col. 0950C] κατέπαυσε ἵππους, “he stopped the horses.” Γαζοφυλάκιον may be translated *pastophorium*, as the ancient scholiast notes on Ezekiel 11:17, or *exedra*, as Jerome observes there. Hence the copyist’s error in Lucifer, where *pastorium* stands for *pastophorium*; and, for ἅρμα, “chariot,” Lucifer read νᾶμα, “fountain.” Others read in Greek ἐν πυρί, “with fire,” as Lucifer himself does.] for the sun, at the entrance of the house [Note: As in the Greek, οἴκου, “house.”] of the Lord, up to the *pastorium*; three horses [Note: “Mares,” Vatican.] which were in Faradin; and he burned the fountain of the sun [Col. 0949B] with fire in the house—the house which the kings of Israel had built for that high Baal and for all the host of heaven.

And the shrines [Note: Sabatier here has a different text: “He also destroyed the altars which were upon the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the temple of the Lord … into the torrent Kidron.” [Col. 0950D] The Greek has “house” rather than “temple,” as in our edition.] were upon the upper buildings, which King Ahaz of Judah had made; and the shrines which Manasseh made in the two buildings of the house of the Lord, the king pulled down and cast out from there, and threw their ashes into the brook Kidron.

And the high places [Note: Again Sabatier: “And the high places which were in Jerusalem, on the right side of Mount Amissa, which Solomon had built … and to the idol Chemosh.” Galland says *Mulcro* should be read *Moloch*; I rather think Lucifer wrote *Milchon*, as Theodotion translates it, whence the copyist’s error is easier.] which had been built facing Jerusalem, on the right of Mount Amissa, which Solomon the king had built for Astarte, the image of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the idol, and for Mulcro, the image of the sons of Ammon—the king defiled them. And he shattered the pillars and filled their places with human bones.

And the shrine [Note: “Which was,” Sabatier; but *was* is also absent from the Greek.] at Bethel, the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nabat, by which he caused Israel to sin—that shrine and high place he pulled down, shattered its stones, ground them to powder, and [Col. 0949C] burned [Note: “Burned,” Vatican; κατέκαυσε in Greek.] their groves. And King Josiah turned and saw the tombs which were there on the mountain. And he took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the shrine, and [Col. 0950A] defiled it, according to the word which the man of God had spoken when Jeroboam stood by the altar on the feast day.

What do you recognize, Constantius, to have been done by a king who worshipped God? And because we strike you with words for introducing idolatry into the Church, you say: “Lucifer insults me!” Though, had you been a man of that time, you could have been destroyed by the sword; or, had you already died, your bones too, as those of a sacrilegious man, would have been committed to fire and reduced to nothing. He strikes the guilty of such great wickedness with the sword; were we not even permitted to wound you in word?

Meanwhile, see in this passage also that those kings, your fellow-sacrilegious men, introduced into the city of God, into the Lord’s house, and into his temple, the idolatry which this most devoted King Josiah extirpated. Do not suppose that you alone have undertaken this work against God. Therefore do not say, “If I were doing wrong, God would already have inflicted vengeance upon me.” Rather, I beg you, see that you are held captive by the devil and live in his power, just as did those kings whose work King Josiah pursued.

Why, because we abhor your blasphemies and resist your wicked conspiracies, do we seem injurious to you? So too the most holy prophets and most blessed apostles seemed insulting and proud to the Jews, whose imitators you are.

In the book of the prophet Amos:

“And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: ‘Amos is making an assembly against me [Note: “Against you,” Vatican and Sabatier.] in the midst of the house of Israel; the land cannot bear his words. For [Note: With the Greek διότι, “because.” Old Version: “For these things … from his land.”] Amos says this: “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led captive from its land.”’ And Amaziah said to Amos: ‘Go, [Col. 0950C] depart to the land of Judah, dwell there, and prophesy there. But in Bethel you shall no longer [Note: The Old Version has “further” for “now,” and “house of the kingdom,” [Col. 0951C] omitting “shall be.”] add to prophesy, because it is the king’s sanctuary and shall be the house of the kingdom’” (Amos 7:10 ff.). [Note: Old Version: “You who see, go out, depart … and live there,” etc.; Galland believes these words were carelessly omitted by the copyist, though who can assert this with certainty?]

And Amos answered and said to Amaziah: “I was not a prophet [Note: “I was no prophet, nor son of a prophet; but a shepherd plucking sycamore figs.” Same source.] nor am I a son of a prophet; but I was a shepherd of goats, plucking [sycamore fruit], and the Lord took [Note: “And he took … from the sheep; and the Lord said … and prophesy to my people,” etc. Same source.] me from the sheep and said to me: ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’ And now hear the word [Note: “The saying … Do not prophesy over Israel, nor gather hearers against the house of Jacob.” Same source.] of the Lord. You say: ‘You shall not prophesy in Israel, and there shall be no gathering in the house of Jacob.’ Therefore [Note: “Therefore … says the Lord: Your wife … shall become a prostitute … your sons and daughters … shall fall by the sword, and [your land] … shall be divided … from the land,” etc. Same source. In Greek, καταμετρηθήσεται, “shall be measured out,” as Lucifer has [Col. 0951D] *metetur*, “shall be measured.”] thus says the Lord God: ‘Your wife shall prostitute herself in the city; your sons and daughters shall fall by the sword; your land shall be measured by the line; you shall die in an unclean land; and Israel shall be led captive from its land.’” [Note: Sabatier here reads “into its land.”]

When you see these things done by him who wished truth and correction to be announced to his erring people, why do you call us insolent and insulting because we tell you, as you wander, what is true? Because we do not heed your voice [Col. 0951B] saying: “Do not believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs believed; instead believe as Arius handed down”? In what matters are we found proud before you, except in abhorring your sacrileges and avoiding your commands as swords and poisons?

This was not first done by us. All those who have already pleased God, holding the faith which we preach, did this. No one among his servants feared to undergo death for God; none of his servants reflected on the kinds of tortures which you tyrants inflict, but each held his commandments before his eyes.

Thus the glorious Tobit was found especially approved before the Lord, because he did not fear the edict of your utterly ruined king, but only God who is all-powerful. Believe Tobit himself speaking thus:

“When King Sennacherib came, fleeing from Judaea [Col. 0951C] because of the defence which the Lord had made from them, because of the blasphemies which he had blasphemed, and in his wrath killed many of the children of Israel, I was secretly taking away their bodies and burying them. [Note: Old Version: “Whom King Sennacherib had killed … the Lord of heaven from him, because of his blasphemies; for in his wrath he killed many of the children of Israel. I wrapped their bodies; and the king sought them and did not find them.” The words in Lucifer, “which he blasphemed” and “I was secretly taking away,” agree almost with the Royal Swedish manuscripts, which read “which he blasphemed,” and the German manuscript, “I secretly carried [them] away.” Sabatier reads *Sennacherib* in Lucifer.] And it was reported to the king that I bury them, and he sought to kill me. [Note: Sabatier reads: “because I was burying [them].” Old Version: “And it was reported to him that I was burying them, [and he sought] to kill me.” The German manuscript has “the king.” Greek θάπτω, “I bury,” as in Lucifer.]

“But I fled, and all my property was plundered; and nothing [Col. 0952A] remained to me except my wife Anna and my son Tobias. [Note: “And Tobias,” Old Version. Sabatier reads “wife Anna,” omitting “my.”] And it came to pass after forty-five days that the king’s sons killed him, and his son Arcedonossar reigned in his place there. [Note: Old Version: “And it came to pass, while he was laying siege … his two sons [killed him], and fled to Mount Ararat. And Archedonassar reigned after him … in his place.” The German manuscripts agree with Lucifer: “And it came to pass that after forty-five days his sons killed that king.”]

“And when I had come into my house, my wife Anna and my son Tobias were restored to me. [Note: Almost with the Greek: Ὅτε δὲ κατῆλθον εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου, καὶ ἀπεδόθη, ‘But when I came down into my house, and [she] was restored,’ etc. The Old Version, after adding certain other words omitted also by the Vulgate: “And I came down to Nineveh, to my house.”] On Pentecost, our feast day, which is holy from the weeks, [Note: With the German manuscript, “from the weeks.” Old Version: “At Pentecost … from seven years, and … many dishes.”] a good meal was prepared for me” (Tobit 2:1). “And I reclined to dine, and a table was set before me, and I saw very many dishes. And I said to my son Tobias: ‘Go and bring whomever you find among our brethren, poor captives in Nineveh, who nevertheless have God in mind [Note: Thus the German manuscript, which also has “and let him eat.” Old Version: “who has … that he may eat together with us.” Sabatier reads *has* also in Lucifer.] with all his heart. Bring him, and let him eat this meal with me. Behold, my son, I wait for you until you come.’

“And Tobias went out [Note: These words agree with the German manuscript: “And Tobias went out to seek”; with the Greek: εἷς ἐκ τοῦ γένους ἡμῶν, “one of our race.” Old Version: “Tobias went to seek … and I said … and he said to me … one of our brethren … lies cast out in public. And I sprang up … anything from it,” etc.] to seek some poor captive among our brethren, [Col. 0952B] and returned and said to me: ‘Father.’ And I said: ‘What is it, son?’ And he said to me: ‘Behold, one of our nation, slain with a noose thrown about him, lies cast out.’ And I went out, leaving my meal before tasting anything from it; and I took him from the street to a place with me, until the sun should set, that I might bury him. [Note: This agrees with the German manuscript: “And I take him from the street to one place with me.” Old Version: “And I took him … into the house,” etc. Sabatier seems to read “I took” also in Lucifer.]

“And when I returned, I washed and ate my meal with mourning. And I remembered the words of the prophet Amos, which he spoke in Bethel, saying: ‘Your feast days shall be turned into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation.’ [Note: Old Version: “Which he spoke in Bethlehem … all days,” etc.] And I wept. And after the sun set, I went and dug and buried him. All my neighbours mocked me, saying: ‘How is this man not afraid? He has already been sought for this deed in order to be killed; he fled, [Note: “And lost his property” is added in the Old Version, though absent also from the Greek. The same version has “be killed” for “be murdered.”] and has begun again to bury the dead.’”

Therefore, when you see that God’s servants have never feared, and cannot now fear, your cruelty as tyrants, but have considered, and do consider, the Lord’s commandments, how do you deign to judge us insolent? Surely because, by God’s action, we trample your power as mud. This is not done by our strength, but is granted by the mercy of him whom you deem worthy to be abhorred in us.

God says to the prophet Ezekiel [Col. 0953A] (Ezekiel 2:3): “Son of man, I send you to the house of Israel, because they themselves and their fathers have embittered [Note: That is, they have provoked and exasperated me, made me bitter toward them. He uses this verb very often, also in the participle, as follows a little below: “because it is a house that embittereth.” Tillemont.] me until this present day. And you shall say to them: ‘Thus says the Lord: Whether they hear or are afraid—for they are a house that embittereth—they shall know that you are a prophet in their midst. And you, son of man, do not fear them or be afraid of their face, because they will rage and run upon you round about, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions. Do not fear their words or be afraid of their face, because they are a house that embittereth. And you shall speak my words to them, whether perhaps they hear or are terrified, because they are a house that embittereth.’”

We seem stubborn to you, just as that prophet, consecrated to God alone, seemed so to those whose darkness you follow. Indeed, Ezekiel the prophet seemed stubborn to your fellow-apostate Jews, and proud to the kings of Israel, because he fulfilled the Lord’s [Col. 0953B] commands and spoke to them what God had commanded him to speak.

You rightly call us proud—us through whom he willed all his commandments to be conveyed to the knowledge of believing peoples. Rightly, I say, you brand us, God’s bishops, as insolent, if we tell you what God has willed to be said to you. You hate those who love you; you persecute those who desire your good. But we cannot fear the gnashing of your slaughter-house.

For you hear the Lord say: “And you, son of man, do not fear them or be afraid of their face, because they will rage and run upon you round about, [Note: “Round about upon you,” Vatican, as a little above it has “you dwell … and of their face,” for “you dwell … of their face.”] and you dwell in the midst of scorpions. Do not fear their words; do not be afraid of their face, because they are a house that embittereth” (ibid., v. 6).

No, I say, we cannot fear the threats [Col. 0953C] of your imperial power, because your scorpion-like powers [Note: Galland incorrectly emends the text to “you are a scorpion.” Nor does the Tilian edition read “you are scorpion-like,” but *scorpiaces*, that is, “your scorpion-like powers.” I would rather read *scorpiacae*, namely, like a scorpion, which strikes secretly but severely [Col. 0954D]; yet it is not unusual for Lucifer to coin new terms.] have no force against us: you see us protected by God’s power and perceive that God is our defender and protector.

Therefore we shall not cease to press upon you the Lord’s commandments, reserving fear for him alone who says: “Son of man” (ibid., 3:4), “go in to the house of Israel and speak my words to them. For you are not sent to a people of lofty speech, to Israel; nor to many peoples of another voice or another tongue, nor to those difficult in speech whose words you cannot understand. Had I sent you to such people, perhaps they would have heard your words; but the house of Israel will not [Note: As in the Greek, μὴ θελήσουσιν, “will not.” Sabatier: “do not wish.”] hear you because they will not hear me, because the whole house of Israel is contentious [Note: Likewise with the Greek, φιλόνεικοί εἰσι, καὶ σκληροκάρδιοι, “they are contentious and hard-hearted.” Sabatier: “It is contentious and hard-hearted.”] and hard-hearted. Behold, I have made your face strong [Col. 0953D] against their faces, and I will strengthen your steadfastness against their contention. You shall be firmer than rock forever. Do not fear them or be terrified before their face, because they are a house that embittereth.”

Who among us can fear you, when you see us established and strengthened by God’s power, standing with fixed step to blunt your stubbornness, immovable as mighty rocks are accustomed to withstand the swelling sea? [Col. 0954A] For this reason you judge us your enemies: because we urge you to become God’s servant instead of a scorpion.

Now, indeed, that you are one of the scorpions cannot be doubted from those concerning whom you heard the Lord say to the prophet: “And you, son of man, do not fear [Note: “Them” is added above.] or be afraid of their face, because they will rage and run upon you round about, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions” (ibid., 2:6). For this reason we are injurious to you, because you see yourself called a scorpion by us. If God had not said that you were a scorpion, you would rightly call me insulting. But now by your actions you show yourself to be a scorpion, and you cry in vain that you suffer insult from us. God says that you are a scorpion, [Col. 0954B] and are you angry with me because I call you by that name?

What insult is it if one says to you: “Unless you turn to God, you shall always be one of the scorpions, as you now are—one of God’s most destructive enemies”? Read through the rest of the prophet Ezekiel and dare to call me insolent, proud, insulting, stubborn:

“And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: ‘Son of man, behold, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. You shall hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me. When I say to the wicked man, “You shall surely die,” and you have not distinguished it to him, nor spoken so as to distinguish to the wicked man that he should turn from his ways and live, that wicked man shall die in his injustice, and I will require his blood from your hand. But if you distinguish it to the wicked man and he has not turned away from his wickedness and his way, that wicked man shall die in his injustice, but you [Col. 0954C] your soul.
you shall save your life. And when the righteous man turns away from his righteous deeds and commits sin, I will set punishment before his face; he shall die, because you did not warn him. He shall die in his sins, and his righteous deeds shall not be remembered; and I will require his blood at your hand. But if you warn the righteous man not to sin [Note: [Col. 0954D] *Delinquat* (“sin”), in both places in Sabatier. Perhaps our edition contains an error.], and he does not sin, that righteous man shall surely live, because you warned him; and you shall save your life.

What, Constantius, do you say to these things? Must God’s priests keep silent and conceal the divine commands from you? Or is it right that all the Lord’s precepts should be laid open to you? Shall we convey to you every will of God concerning those entrusted to us? Or shall we withhold it, to our own destruction, from you? For the Lord says that He will require your blood from me. Indeed, if you do not obey God—whose divine warnings we press upon you—you, wicked man, shall die in your wickedness, and the salvation of your soul will no longer be required of us, because we have not been frightened by your threats, but have feared only Him who commanded that no one besides Himself should be feared. For the purpose of rescuing you from your accursed paths, we assembled in the name of the Lord God [Note: [Col. 0955B] This may rightly be understood of the meetings of the Council of Milan at which Lucifer was present.].

Lest I should seem to you, the emperor, to be insulting you [Note: [Col. 0955B] Perhaps *videremur* (“we should seem”), so that it corresponds to the preceding *conveniremus* (“we assembled”). Galland. But he punctuates differently: “We assembled, lest I should seem,” etc. What ought I to do, etc.], what ought I to have done at the time when I judge that you were born to turn us servants of God from the way of truth? When Nebuchadnezzar had sent Holofernes, the chief of his forces, and he was besieging Jerusalem, what did Judith pray God to do? Surely, that He should destroy the enemies of Israel. Did she say, “Preserve those who rise up against Your house”?

“O Lord, God of my father Simeon, to whom You gave a sword for vengeance upon foreigners, who violated a virgin’s womb for defilement, uncovered her thigh for disgrace, and polluted her womb for reproach; for You said, ‘It shall not be so,’ and You did it. Therefore You delivered their rulers to slaughter, and their marriage-bed which received the beloved woman to blood; You struck their servants upon their mighty men, upon their thrones; You gave their women as plunder, their daughters into captivity, and all their spoil for division among Your beloved children, who were zealous with zeal for You, abhorred the defilement of Your race, and called upon You for their aid: ‘My God, hear me, a widow.’” [Note: [Col. 0955D] Old Latin: “All the spoils . . . and they abhorred . . . their blood . . . for their help: Lord . . . hear,” etc. The Corbie manuscript has “all spoil” with Lucifer; Sabatier likewise has “hear” for “will hear.”]

[Note: [Col. 0955D] For *abominati sunt* (“they abhorred”). Tilius, as in the Old Latin.]

[Note: [Col. 0955C] Old Latin: “To whom You gave into his hand a sword for vengeance . . . in defilement . . . a thigh in shame . . . in reproach . . . because they acted against a virgin’s blood, and You gave . . . and her bed, which received . . . and set servants . . . upon thrones,” etc. German manuscript: “To whom You gave him a sword . . . in reproach . . . because . . .” Corbie manuscript has the plural, “they struck servants”; Greek: *ἐπὶ θρονούς αὐτῶν*, “upon their thrones.” Sabatier read with Lucifer: “You gave him a sword for vengeance . . . because” (omitting *quod*, “that/because”) “You gave,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0955C] Galland says that the Tilian reading here is corrupt, supposing it copied from the authors of the Lyons *Bibliotheca Patrum*: “and you did,” therefore. But either they wrote *fecistis* (“you did,” plural) at will, or a typographical error occurred. For the genuine reading of Tilius’s edition, which I have before me, is “and You did, therefore,” with *quod* (“that/because”) added from the corrections printed at the end of that edition.]

“For You made their former things with them [Note: [Col. 0955D] “Their former things with them,” with the German manuscript; and “the things afterward, and now, and those to come,” with the Greek: *Καὶ τὰ μετέπειτα, καὶ τὰ νῦν, καὶ τὰ ἐπερχόμενα*. Old Latin: “Their former things, and the latter things, and the things now to come,” with other additions partly absent even from the Vulgate.], and the things afterward, the things now, and those that are to come. For all Your ways are prepared, and Your creation is in providence [Note: [Col. 0955D] Old Latin: “And Your judgments.” The German and Pech manuscripts, with Lucifer, have “Your creation.” Sabatier reads in Lucifer “of Your creation.”]. Behold, the Assyrians have been filled with their strength; they have exalted themselves in horse and rider; they have gloried in the arm of their infantry; they trusted in shields, in the stretched bow [Note: [Col. 0955D] Galland argues that one should read “and spear and bow”; but we prefer the Old Latin reading, which agrees with Lucifer.], and in slings [Note: [Col. 0955D] *Fundibalis*, “slings,” Old Latin.], and did not know that You are the Lord who will crush wars; Lord is Your name. [Note: [Col. 0956B] The German manuscript, with Lucifer: “Frustrate Your holy things . . . the tabernacle of Your rest and of Your honorable name, to seize,” etc. Old Latin: “Crush their strength, eternal God; break their multitude by Your power, shatter their power . . . for they planned to defile . . . and pollute . . . the rest of Your majestic name, and cast down,” etc.]

“Cast down their strength, O Eternal One; crush their multitude by Your power, and bring down their obstinacy in Your wrath. For they planned to frustrate Your holy things, to defile the tabernacle of Your rest, of Your honorable name, and to seize with the sword the horn of Your altar. Look upon their arrogance [Note: [Col. 0956C] Old Latin: “their pride,” adding: “and send wrath upon their heads.” “Upon their heights,” German and Corbie manuscripts.]; give to me, a widow, the strength I have conceived in my hand [Note: [Col. 0956C] With the Greek, *ἐν χειρί μου*, “in my hand.” Old Latin: “into my hand.”], and strike their mouth with the lips of my persuasion against the ruler, and the ruler against his servant; shatter his substance by the hand of a widow [Note: [Col. 0956C] Old Latin adds: “that all kingdoms may know that You are God.”].

“For Your strength is not in a multitude, nor is Your power, nor Your gift, in the strong [Note: [Col. 0956C] With the Pech manuscript: “Your strength, but not power”; with the German manuscript: “supporter of the weak.” Old Latin: “It is Yours, nor in power, nor . . . does it prevail in the strong . . . helper of the weak, supporter of the humble, and,” etc. *Praevalet* (“does it prevail”) is absent from the Greek, as from Lucifer.]; but You are the God of the humble, helper of the weak, supporter of the weak, savior of those without hope, indeed the God of my father and God of Israel’s inheritance [Note: [Col. 0956D] Thus in Greek: *ναὶ, ὁ θεὸς τοῦ πατρός μου*, “indeed, God of my father.” The rest agrees with the German manuscript. Old Latin, which punctuates differently with Sabatier: “Therefore, O Lord God . . . hear,” etc.]. O Lord, Master of heaven and earth, Creator of the waters, King of all creation, hear my entreaty. Give craft and persuasion in the wound and bruise of those who have devised hard things against Your covenant, Your holy house, the heights of Zion, and the house of possession of Your children [Note: [Col. 0956D] The Greek nearly agrees with Lucifer here: *Δὸς λόγον μου, καὶ ἀπάτην . . . οἳ κατὰ τῆς διαθήκης σου . . . καὶ οἴκου Κατασχέσεως . . . ἐβουλεύσαντο*, etc. Old Latin: “And give cunning in persuasion, and their wound and bruise, who are against Your covenant . . . and the house of possession . . . who devised hard things. Look and make known upon every nation and every tribe.”]

[Note: [Col. 0956D] Galland writes that this has undoubtedly been corrupted by an ignorant copyist, and should be restored in accordance with the Vatican Greek: “They devised hard things. And make,” etc., closer to the Old Latin.]; make known upon every nation and every tribe that You are God of all power and might, and that there is no other defender of Israel’s race besides You” (Judith 9:2 ff.).

What, in view of these things, will your prudent mind deign to think? After this prayer poured out to God against the enemies of religion, will you be able to say that we oppose you in an evil manner because we say to you: “Either correct your crooked ways and do not delight in the power of your empire, or recognize that you will come to nothing”? What else do we, servants of God and priests of His divine majesty, do today, except what those did whose imitators we desire to be found?

For I think it right not to abandon, in this great persecution inflicted by you, the peoples entrusted to us, but to exhort them that, since He whose servants we are is able to rescue us from the hands of His enemies, you are not to be feared as an enemy of God’s house; and to remind them that you are nothing, because our God and Lord, almighty over all, will reduce to nothing all your impious enterprises directed against His house [Note: [Col. 0957C] Perhaps: “that, since God whose servants we are is mighty,” etc., Galland. But Lucifer often uses *quod enim* for “because”; the sense here is: “but to exhort them, because He is mighty,” etc., “that you are not to be feared,” etc. Under Galland’s interpretation one would moreover have to read: “but to exhort them; that, since,” etc., “you are not to be feared,” etc.].

What injury is done to you here by us? What insult is directed against the Roman emperor by the bishops of the living God, if you are urged to obtain eternal life, or are told that, because you have taken up arms against God’s house, unless you correct yourself you will perish in a terrible destruction? Why, indeed, do we hold before you the ruin of all enemies of God’s house, except that, either terrified by fear of God, you may change yourself, or, when by your own fault you have made yourself punished for eternity [Note: [Col. 0957D] Galland reads “you shall know yourself to be punished,” less correctly; for the sense is: “when you shall already have been condemned for eternity through your own fault,” etc.], we may triumph securely on every side: both because your blood cannot be required by God from us, and because we shall have seen the destruction of the adversaries of His Church?

Persist, then, in this injustice of yours, and you will find what punishment follows you for such deserts [Note: [Col. 0957D] *Consequentur*, Latin and Galland; *consequuntur*, Tilius; or perhaps *consequitur poena*, “punishment follows.”].

“Lucifer,” you say, “is puffed up with pride because he tells you the truth.” What did you command me to do at this time, when you, the forerunner of Antichrist, raised arms against God’s house in order to kill us? At the time when you proved to be a denier of the only Son of God? Should I have kept silent and allowed you, a wolf coming to ravage God’s flock? Or do you think it would have been proper for us shepherds to go to meet you with dry throats, prepared to swallow those entrusted among us along with ourselves? [Note: [Col. 0957D] The phrase *nobiscum* (“with us”) seems superfluous; perhaps read *nobismet commissos, nobiscum transvorandos*: “those entrusted to ourselves, to be swallowed with us.” Galland. But the correction at the end of the Tilian edition has *nosmet nobiscum commissos*, i.e. “committed among ourselves,” divided among ourselves.]

It would have been enough of a great deed for that woman Judith, desiring to please God, to kill the enemy with her own hand, while we, shepherds appointed by the Lord, should not even have resisted you with a word! The Lord says in the Gospel (John 10:11): “The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep [Note: [Col. 0957D] Greek: *τίθησιν* (“lays down”); Old Latin: *dat* (“gives”).]. But the hireling, who is not a shepherd and whose own sheep are not the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf snatches them and scatters them, because he is a hireling and does not care for the sheep.” [Note: [Col. 0957D] Old Latin: “But the hireling, who is not a shepherd . . . leaves the sheep . . . them, and the sheep are scattered.” Tertullian, *On Flight in Persecution*, has *derelinquit* (“leaves”); Cyprian, in the letter to the clergy of Carthage, has *dispergit* (“scatters”), with Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0957D] The Cambridge manuscript agrees. Old Latin adds: “but the hireling flees, because he is hired,” etc. Greek *μισθωτός*, “hireling,” agrees with Lucifer.]

What, therefore, were we to do, lest we should seem to have insulted you? We recognized you as a wolf; we saw you stretch out your hands against the Lord’s sheep; we observed you attempting at one time to tear to pieces all who call upon the Lord’s name. Would it have been right that we should show ourselves not shepherds but hirelings?

He says to blessed Peter: “Feed my lambs” [Note: [Col. 0958C] Old Latin: “Feed my sheep,” in both places.] (John 21:16). And again: “Feed my little sheep” [Note: [Col. 0958C] Old Latin: “Feed my sheep,” in both places.] (ibid., 17). And you, coming as a wolf, wish those who are found to have become successors of blessed Peter to perform the role of hirelings? Those whom He had long ago promised through Jeremiah to His people, saying: “I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and instruction” [Note: [Col. 0958C] Lucifer said “with instruction,” by which he understood knowledge and teaching. La Cerda.]; and He did not say: “I will give you Emperor Constantius, who can turn you into prey for the devil” (Jeremiah 3:15).

You say that we act wrongly because, protected by God’s power, we resist your sacrilege. Let us see also what was done at the time when your fellow-tyrant Antiochus became a persecutor of our religion, by those who remembered that no one besides God must be feared. But first you should learn what he wrote who is like you; for in this way you will be able to understand that those servants of God, in whose company we desire to be found [Note: [Col. 0958D] The Latin has *quorum* (“whose”).], resisted Antiochus’s sacrilege just as, God being favorable, we resist you.

Holy Scripture speaks thus in the First Book of Maccabees:

“And the king wrote to all his kingdom that all the people should be one, and that each should abandon his own ordinances. All the nations accepted the king’s word, and many from Israel agreed with them and polluted the sabbath. The king sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, directing them to follow the ordinances of a foreign land; to forbid burnt offerings, sacrifice, and libation from the sanctuary; to defile sabbaths and feast-days; to profane the holy place; to set up shrines and idols, to sacrifice swine and common cattle, to leave their sons uncircumcised, and to defile their souls with every uncleanness and abomination, so that they might forget the law and alter the ordinances. Whoever did not act according to the king’s word was to die.” [Note: [Col. 0958D] Old Latin: “King Antiochus . . . should abandon . . . your law.” The Alexandrian manuscript omits “Antiochus,” as does Lucifer. Greek: *τὰ νόμιμα αὐτοῦ*, “his ordinances,” as in Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] Old Latin: “They agreed . . . of King Antiochus.” “Antiochus” is absent from the Greek, as in Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] Old Latin: “They agreed to his service, sacrificed to idols, and defiled,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] “By the hands of messengers into Jerusalem and all . . . that they should follow the laws of the nations of the land,” etc.; the German manuscript agrees completely with Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] Thus in Greek. Old Latin: “And they should forbid sacrifices and propitiations to be performed in God’s temple.” Sabatier reads *prohiberent* (“they should forbid”) in Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] Old Latin: “And they should forbid the sabbath to be celebrated.” Greek, with Lucifer: “in which they might defile.”]

[Note: [Col. 0958D] Sabatier: “And they defiled.” “And he ordered the holy things and the holy people Israel to be defiled,” Old Latin.]

[Note: [Col. 0959B] Sabatier: “They should set up and sacrifice.” The rest agrees with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “And he ordered altars and temples to be built . . . and swine’s flesh to be sacrificed,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0959B] “They should abandon and defile,” in Sabatier. The Greek is nearly the same; the German manuscript agrees completely with Lucifer except for the added “of their fathers.” Old Latin: “Souls to be defiled . . . in all uncleannesses and abominations . . . and that they should alter all God’s ordinances.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959B] It agrees with the manuscript of St. Theodore in Sabatier except for the added “of King Antiochus,” which is also in the Old Latin: “in which they should do so, and die.”]

“According to all these words he sent written orders throughout all his kingdom, and appointed overseers over the people. He commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city; and many of the people gathered to them, all those abandoning the law, and they committed evils in the land” (1 Maccabees 1:43 ff.).

[Note: [Col. 0959C] This agrees with the Greek except *misit scripta* (“he sent written orders”), where the Greek has *ἔγραψε* (“he wrote”), and *ἐπὶ πάντα τὸν λαόν* (“over all the people”) for “over the people.” Old Latin: “He wrote to every . . . and set rulers over the people to compel these things to be done.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959C] Thus also in Greek. Old Latin: “And they ordered the cities of Judah to sacrifice.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959C] Old Latin: “To those who had abandoned the law of the Lord . . . upon the land.” “Lord” is absent from the Greek, which has *ἐν τῇ γῇ*, “in the land,” as in Lucifer.]

[Note: [Col. 0959C] “Every one abandoning,” Vatican manuscript, with Greek, *πᾶς ὁ ἐγκαταλιπών*.]

And below (ibid., 57):

“They built the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and in the surrounding cities of Judah they built altars. They burned incense at the doors of houses and in the streets. The books of the law which they found, they tore up and burned with fire; and wherever a book of the covenant was found, and if anyone consented to the law, the king’s decree put him to death. In their power they treated Israel in this way, those who were found in the cities month after month; and on the twenty-fourth day of the month they sacrificed upon the altar which was on the altar. The women who had circumcised their newborn children they killed according to the command; they hung the infants from their necks, and [plundered] their houses, and killed those who had circumcised them. Many in Israel stood firm and strengthened themselves not to eat common food; they chose to die rather than be defiled by foods and profane the holy covenant. And there was very great wrath upon Israel in those days.”

[Note: [Col. 0959C] With the Greek, *ᾠκοδόμησαν*, “they built.” The rest agrees with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “King Antiochus built the abominable idol . . . of God, and throughout all the cities . . . they built,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0959C] With the German manuscript. Old Latin: “At the doors . . . incense, and they sacrificed.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959C] Nearly thus in Greek: *Καὶ τὰ βιβλία τοῦ νόμου ἃ εὗρον ἐνεπύρισαν πυρὶ, κατασχίσαντες*—“And the books of the law which they found they burned with fire, after tearing them.” Old Latin: “They burned the books of God’s law with fire, tearing them up.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959D] Sabatier reads: “According to the king’s edict they killed him,” from the Old Latin, which further has: “and wherever books of the Lord’s covenant were found, and whoever observed the Lord’s law, according to the king’s edict they slaughtered him.” German manuscript, with Lucifer: “And if anyone consented to the law, the king’s decree killed him.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959D] Nearly with Greek. Old Latin: “They did these things to the people Israel who were found,” etc. Sabatier reads here: “They did these things to the people Israel.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959D] “Fifth,” German manuscript, with which it agrees in the rest. Old Latin: “on the twenty-fifth day, and against the altar.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959D] Thus with the German manuscript, which has “were killed.” Old Latin: “They circumcised their children; they were slaughtered according to the command of King Antiochus.”]

[Note: [Col. 0959D] Sabatier reads: “From their necks throughout all their houses; and they slaughtered those who had circumcised them,” as in the Old Latin. He corrects the Latin: “And they plundered their houses,” as in Greek, “and killed those who had circumcised them.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960B] Nearly as in Greek: *Καὶ πολλοὶ ἐν Ἰσραὴλ ἐκραταιώθησαν, καὶ ὠχυρώθησαν ἐν αὐτοῖς τοῦ μὴ φαγεῖν κοινά· καὶ ἐπελέξαντο ἀποθανεῖν, ἵνα μὴ μιανθῶσι τοῖς βρώμασι*—“And many in Israel were strengthened and fortified in themselves not to eat common food; and they chose to die, that they might not be defiled by foods.” Sabatier thus reads Lucifer: “And many of Israel’s people resolved within themselves not to eat unclean things; and they preferred to die rather than be defiled by unclean foods.” This agrees with the Old Latin except: “And they chose rather to die than to be defiled by foods.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960C] With the German manuscript, which adds, “and they died.” Old Latin: “They would not break God’s holy law, and they were slaughtered.” Sabatier reads *profanare* (“to profane”) for *profanarent* (“they might profane”).]

And (ibid. 2:1), “Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib from Jerusalem, arose, and he had five sons.”

[Note: [Col. 0960C] The same in Greek. Old Latin: “In those days there arose . . . son of Simeon . . . from the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and he settled on Mount Modein.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960C] As Greek, *Καὶ αὐτῷ υἱοὶ πέντε*, “and he had five sons.” The latter words are omitted by Sabatier.]

And below (ibid., 6):

“They saw the blasphemies being committed in Judah and Israel, and he said: ‘Woe is me! Why was I born to see the crushing of my people and the crushing of the holy city, and to sit there while it is given into the hand of enemies, the sanctuary into the hand of foreigners? All her adornment has been taken away; from a free woman she has become a slave. Behold, our holy things, our beauty, and our glory have been made desolate, and the nations have defiled her. Why should we still live?’”

[Note: [Col. 0960C] Greek: *Τὰς βλασφημίας τὰς γινομένας ἐν Ἰούδα*—“the blasphemies occurring in Judah.” “They saw, and in Israel,” with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “They saw the evils being done among the people in Judah and Jerusalem.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960C] Nearly with Greek: *καὶ εἶπεν· Οἴμοι ἱνατί τοῦτο ἐγεννήθην ἰδεῖν τὸ σύντριμμα τοῦ λαοῦ μου, καὶ τὸ σύντριμμα τῆς . . . καὶ καθίσαι ἐκεῖ ἐν τῷ δοθῆναι, αὐτὴν ἐν χειρὶ ἐχθρῶν*—“And he said: Alas, why was I born to see the destruction of my people, and the destruction of . . . and to sit there when she is given into enemies’ hands?” Old Latin: “And Mattathias said: Woe is me, why was I born . . . and to sit there when it is given into enemies’ hands?” Sabatier reads: “Why was I born . . . and to sit there when it is given . . . and in the hand,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0960D] “And the sanctuary,” Latin, with Greek: *καὶ τὸ ἁγίασμα ἐν χειρὶ ἀλλοτρίων*, “and the sanctuary in the hand of foreigners.” Old Latin: “The holy things have fallen into the hand of strangers.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960D] Thus in Greek: *πᾶς ὁ κόσμος αὐτῆς ἀφῃρέθη. Ἀντὶ ἐλευθέρας ἐγένετο εἰς δούλην*—“All her adornment was taken away. Instead of free, she became a slave.” Old Latin reads “her adornment, and she who was free.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960D] With the German manuscript: “Behold, our holy things . . . our glory . . . and they defiled.” With the St. Theodore manuscript, “it/her.” Old Latin: “And behold . . . beauty . . . splendor . . . and they defiled them.”]

[Note: [Col. 0960D] Thus German manuscript. Old Latin: “Why then should we still live?”]

“And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, covered themselves with sackcloth, and mourned deeply. Men sent by the king came and compelled apostasy in the city of Modein, that they might sacrifice; and many of Israel came to them. But Mattathias and his sons gathered together.

“Those sent by the king answered and said to Mattathias: ‘You are a ruler, noble and great in this city, strengthened with sons. Now come first and carry out the king’s command, as all the nations have done, and the men of Judah and those left in Israel. You and your sons shall be friends of the king, and you and your sons shall be honored with silver, gold, and many gifts.’

“Mattathias answered in a loud voice and said: ‘Even if all the nations in the king’s house obey him, so that every one departs from the service of his fathers and chooses his commands, I and my sons shall walk in the covenant of our fathers. May the Lord be gracious to us; we shall not abandon the law and the ordinances. We shall not obey the king’s word; we shall not turn aside from the service due from us, either to the right or to the left.’

“When he had ceased speaking these words, a Jewish man came before the eyes of all to sacrifice at Modein according to the king’s command. Mattathias saw it and was zealous; his inward parts trembled, and he brought wrath according to judgment. Running to the altar, he killed him; and at that time he killed the king’s officer who compelled sacrifice, and destroyed the altar. He was zealous for the law, as Phinehas did against Zimri, son of Salom. Mattathias cried aloud in the city: ‘Let everyone zealous for, and maintaining, the covenant come out after me.’ And he and his sons fled into the mountain, leaving all that they had in the city.”

[Note: [Col. 0961C] Nearly with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “Those sent by King Antiochus came there in order to compel those who had fled to the city of Modein to sacrifice, burn incense, and depart from God’s law.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] Nearly with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “And many of Israel’s people, agreeing, came to them; but . . . stood firm.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] “Those sent by Antiochus answered and said to Mattathias: ‘You are ruler and distinguished . . . in this city, adorned with sons and brothers.’” Old Latin. “They said . . . noble,” with Greek; “answered,” with German manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] “Strengthened with sons and brothers,” Vatican manuscript with Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] Old Latin: “Therefore come first . . . command . . . who remained in Jerusalem, and you shall be . . . among the king’s friends, and be enriched with gold and silver.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] For *gloriabimini* (“you shall be honored”). Tilius; perhaps the printed edition has an error, which Galland also corrects according to Greek, *δοξασθήσεσθε*.]

[Note: [Col. 0961C] Greek: *Πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, τὰ ἐν οἴκῳ τῆς βασιλείας, ἀκούουσιν αὐτοῦ*—“All the nations that are in the kingdom’s house obey him.” Old Latin: “And he answered . . . and if all nations obey King Antiochus . . . depart from the service of the law of their fathers and agree to his commands.” Sabatier reads in Lucifer: “Those who are in the king’s house . . . and agree to his commands.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961D] With the German manuscript except for “in the covenant,” and with “and my brothers” added. Old Latin: “I and my sons and my brothers will obey the law,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0961D] Old Latin: “It is not useful for us to abandon the law and God’s ordinances.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961D] Greek *τὸν λόγον*, “the word.” Old Latin: “We shall not hear the words of King Antiochus, nor shall we sacrifice by transgressing the commands of our law, to go another way.” Greek, with Lucifer: *δεξιὰν ἢ ἀριστεράν*, “right or left.”]

[Note: [Col. 0961D] The German manuscript agrees, except for “before the eyes” and “upon the altar at Modein.” Old Latin: “And when . . . these words . . . a certain Jew . . . to idols upon the altar in the city of Modein . . . command,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 0962C] Thus also in Greek. Old Latin: “He saw . . . grieved . . . and his anger was kindled according to the judgment of the law; rushing upon him, he slaughtered him on the altar.”]

[Note: [Col. 0962C] Entirely with Greek. Old Latin: “And also the man whom King Antiochus had sent . . . at that very time.”]

[Note: [Col. 0962C] Old Latin: “And he was zealous for the law . . . Zimri, son of Salomi.”]

[Note: [Col. 0962C] It agrees completely with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “Everyone who has zeal for the law, maintaining . . . And he himself fled . . . into the mountains,” etc.]

What like deed have you seen done by us, that you should deign to say, “Lucifer insulted me”? He killed with the sword the king’s officer, and also the man whom he saw from his own people obeying the king’s edict rather than God’s [Note: [Col. 0962C] One must supply “rather,” or perhaps “more than”; he often speaks in this way. Tilius.]. Yet I resist you and yours with a word and say: “I do not abandon the apostolic and evangelical faith; I believe as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, believed.” For this reason I am guilty of insults before you.

If you had been in the hands of this Mattathias, zealous for God, or in the hand of Phinehas, to whom God bears testimony in Numbers through Moses, and had attempted to live according to the manner of foreigners, they would without doubt have killed you with the sword [Note: [Col. 0962C] “Without doubt,” etc. I think the first clause was fashioned by a drowsy copyist. Galland. It certainly seems redundant.]. They would have killed you with the sword; I, because I wound with a word that mind of yours drenched in Christian blood, am judged by you guilty of insults.

Why, emperor, do you not avenge yourself upon me? Why do you not deign to defend your insults, to vindicate yourself against a beggarly man? Why are you not zealous in the matter [Note: [Col. 0962C] Galland’s “Why are you not acting?” is less correct; understand rather: “Why are you not *satagens*,” that is, concerned in this matter.]? Not because you do not wish to, but because power has not yet been given to you by Him whose servant I am, confident in whom I speak these things to you freely—things which, in light of your wicked deeds, seem wrong to you.

When you see that we have renounced you, all the riches of your kingdom, and your father also [Note: [Col. 0962C] That is, the devil.], and that we shall by no means depart from the faith, enticed by your promises, you will know that we greatly pity ourselves [Note: [Col. 0962D] Latin has *mirari*, “to wonder”; but *misereri*, “to pity,” is correct, that is, concerning ourselves, because we are not killed for Christ.], since, though you are accustomed to devour those displeasing to you with the sword’s edge, you spare us [Note: [Col. 0962D] “Us nevertheless,” Vatican manuscript.]. I believe that this is because of your compassion, and we may think so of your gentleness. For, from your excessive kindness, I have been able to conclude that you have killed no one [Note: [Col. 0962D] Said ironically. On killings committed by Constantius apart from religious grounds, see much in Ammianus Marcellinus.].

You say, “He is proud.” Why do I seem proud to you? Surely because you hear me say that you are doing the things which enemies of God’s religion have always done. It is my duty to lay these things before you, heretic. Or are you not a heretic? But if you are a heretic, why do you accuse me of insulting you because I do to you what God willed me to do?

The most holy prophet Jeremiah relates that God said to him: “But gird up your loins, rise, and say everything that I commanded you; do not fear their face, nor be dismayed before them” (Jeremiah 1:17). Since this is so, and the necessity of the office imposed on us by God presses us, so that we must say to you, as you act, whatever God commands to be said to you, it remains either that you obey God’s commands, being admonished by me, a servant and priest of His clemency, or that you prove from the sacred Scriptures—perhaps because you are emperor—that I am not permitted to summon you in the Lord’s name to correct yourself.

If you cannot prove that I am forbidden, but instead begin to find that I am commanded to rebuke, reprove, exhort, entreat, admonish, and summon you to please God, why do you say that I insult you? For He gave us, His bishops, authority to rebuke and teach those entrusted to us, so greatly that He said: “Do not fear their face, nor be dismayed before them. Behold, today I have made you like a fortified city and like a firm bronze wall against all the kings of Judah, its rulers, and the people of the land. They shall fight against you, but shall not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.”

What were the things Jeremiah said to the kings of Judah, their rulers, and the peoples of the land? Surely, that they had forsaken the Lord and sacrificed to foreign gods. You too have done and are doing these things: you have abandoned the apostolic and evangelical faith, embraced the Arian heresy, and compel all God’s servants to become idolaters. Because you dare these things, you call proud those who desire to provide for your salvation.

God says to Jeremiah: “But gird up your loins, arise, and say all that I say to you. Do not fear their face, nor be dismayed before them” (ibid.). And do you, Emperor Constantius, become angry because we say to you in your error: “Return to the way of salvation; abandon the error devised through Arius at the devil’s prompting”? God commands that He alone be feared; He has ordered that no one besides Himself be dreaded. Yet you have decreed that things be carried out which remove fear of the Lord and make you feared? God says to Jeremiah: “Behold, today I have made you like a fortified city and like a bronze wall—
bronze, firm, against all the kings of Judah, its princes, and the people of the land; and they shall fight against you, and shall not prevail against you, because I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord” (ibid. 18). And do you think that you can be feared by any of God’s servants? Why do you call me arrogant, proud? Why do you call me insulting? Surely because I have found, from your deeds, that you are one of those of whom blessed John says: “You have heard that Antichrist is coming; now, however, there are many antichrists” (1 John 2:18).

[Note: “[That] he is to come . . . now many Antichrists have arisen.” Old Latin version.]

Thus you brand us guilty of injuries, as though we were the first to resist your introducing idolatry into the Church of God. You have read in the first book of Maccabees:

“And one man said to his neighbour: ‘If we all do as our brothers did, and do not fight against the nations for our life and our ordinances, they will now quickly destroy us from the earth.’ And they took counsel on that day, saying: ‘Every man who comes against us for battle on the sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we shall not all die, as our brothers died in the hiding-places.’ Then a strong assembly, mighty in strength, gathered to them from Israel, every one willingly devoted to the law; and all who fled from evils joined them and became a support to them. They formed an army, struck sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath; and the rest fled to the nations to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went around, destroyed the altars, circumcised in strength the uncircumcised boys whom they found within the borders of Israel, pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands. They recovered the law from the hands of the nations and of kings, and did not give a horn to the sinner” (1 Macc. 2:40 ff.).

[Note: Thus the Greek in the Alexandrian manuscript: “for our life,” ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν. Old Latin: “for our souls.”]

[Note: “In battle.” Old Latin.]

[Note: Sabatier reads in Lucifer here, “strong forces against them”; and in *On Not Associating with Heretics*, “strong assemblies.” See also what we noted on p. 15 (here col. 778, note i).]

[Note: *On Not Associating with Heretics* and the Old Latin add: “They joined them.” Sabatier here reads “against them.”]

[Note: See above, p. 15 (col. 779, line 3 and note a), where Lucifer himself deletes *in*.]

[Note: See ibid. (line 6 and note b), where *went around* appears instead of *had gone around*.]

[Note: With the Greek. Old Latin, preceded by two dots: “and in strength.”]

[Note: “The work prospered in their hand,” with the German manuscript; likewise in that manuscript and in the Greek. Lucifer has “into their hands” above, p. 15 (col. 779), where see no. 4 (note c).]

[Note: Lucifer has “heart” there instead of “horn.” See no. 5.]

What can your mind, wounded by the poisons of Arius, think?

[Note: With the Latin, we print *venenis* (“poisons”) for *venisse* (“to have come”), as it was previously read.]

What can your heart, shredded by the bites of the serpent, devise against this defence of ours?

[Note: “To devise.” The same.] When you observe that they acted thus in those circumstances, ought we to have remained quiet while the blasphemies uttered from your mouth wounded the people divinely entrusted to us? “And Mattathias,” it says, “and his friends went around” (ibid. 45), “destroyed the altars, circumcised in strength the uncircumcised boys whom they found within the borders of Israel, pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands; they recovered the law from the hands of nations and kings, and did not give a horn to the sinner.”

Since those who acted thus became most beloved by God, was it proper that we, by flattering you and running with you in your crime, should become, as you are, God’s bitterest enemies? If for this reason we seem injurious to you, because we could not accept your idolatry, name, I pray, one of God’s worshippers who spared the opponents of His religion.

In the second book of Ezra, when opponents resisted the rebuilding for the Lord of the house, temple, and city in Jerusalem, it says: “The God of heaven himself has prospered us, and we his servants shall arise and build; but you have neither portion nor memorial in Jerusalem” (2 Esdr. 2:20).

[Note: In Sabatier: “You have no portion, right, or memorial.”]

And below, when the adversaries say: “Will they sacrifice? Will they eat in their own place? Will not a fox go up and demolish their stone walls?” (ibid. 4:3).

[Note: Where he says *demoliet*, a form not in use, for *demolietur*, that is, “will destroy and plunder their city’s stone walls.” Til.]

And Ezra, God’s servant, says this to God: “Hear, our God, for we have become contemptible; turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them over to derision in a land of captivity. Do not cover their iniquity, and let not their sins be blotted out from before you” (ibid. 4:4).

[Note: Sabatier reads, “Hear us, our God.”]

What like this have we said concerning you? He whom Ezra prayed to is witness—he whom I too pray to, and whom his blessed Church throughout the whole world prays to—that these are my wishes concerning you: that you may correct your errors and be one of us. Consider meanwhile how God’s people neither feared their adversaries nor ceased, in prayer against the enemies of God’s house, to ask that the strength of the adversaries of God’s religion might be reduced to nothing.

For so also the most holy Moses says to God in the song of Exodus: “Let fear and trembling fall upon them at the greatness of your arm; let them become as stones, until this people whom you acquired passes over” (Exod. 15:16).

[Note: This follows the German manuscript. Old Latin: “Fear fell . . . greatness . . . stone, until your people, O Lord, passes over, until this one whom you acquired, O Lord.”]

They uttered such words to God concerning those delivered to them.

[Note: Galland reads: “concerning those handed over to themselves.”]

Yet because we say to you, “Either turn to God, or be certain that God will reduce all your empty pride to nothing,” you think us insolent.

[Note: For “be certain,” Til. reads: “Know for certain that God will reduce your pride to nothing.”]

Consider further what that most holy man Mattathias, devoted to God, did after those illustrious deeds, and what he said to his sons at the end of his life; and see whether we priests act against you in accordance with God’s rightful order. Holy Scripture says:

“The days of Mattathias’ death drew near, and he said to his sons: ‘Now pride has grown strong, and chastisement, and a time of overthrow, and the wrath of indignation. Now, my sons, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers. Remember the deeds of the fathers, which they performed in their generations, and you shall receive great glory and an everlasting name. Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and was it reckoned to him as righteousness? Joseph, in the time of his distress, kept the commandment and became lord of Egypt. Phinehas our father, by being zealous with the zeal of God, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Joshua, while fulfilling the word, became leader in Israel. Caleb, while bearing witness in the assembly, received an inheritance. David, in his mercy, obtained the throne of an everlasting kingdom. Elijah, while zealous with zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven. Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, because they believed, were delivered from the flame. Daniel, in his simplicity, was delivered from the mouth of lions. Thus reflect from generation to generation: all who hope in him shall not be weakened. Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is in dung and worms: today he is exalted; tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his thought has perished. My sons, be strengthened and prevail in the law, because in it you shall be glorious. And behold Simeon your brother: I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him, and he shall be a father to you. And Judas Maccabaeus, mighty in strength from his youth, shall be your commander in war and shall wage the people’s battle. Bring to yourselves all who practise the law; avenge your people, repay the nations in return, and attend to the commandment of the law’” (1 Macc. 2:49 ff.).

[Note: Old Latin: “The days of Mattathias’ death approached . . . now therefore, O sons, be zealous . . . for the covenant of your fathers.”]

[Note: With the German manuscript. Old Latin: “in their generations.”]

[Note: With the same manuscript. Old Latin: “By zealously being zealous for God.”]

[Note: “While he fulfilled.” Old Latin.]

[Note: “He was received into heaven.” The same.]

[Note: With the Greek. Old Latin: “are weakened.”]

[Note: Nearly with the Greek: εἰς κοπρίαν, καὶ σκώληκας, “into dung and worms.” Old Latin: “Dung and worm is he.” I would prefer to read in Lucifer *stercora* (“dung-heaps”), with Galland. Sabatier reads: “Do not fear . . . and worm.”]

[Note: Thus the German manuscript. Old Latin: “And tomorrow . . . has perished.” The same Lucifer has “and tomorrow” a little below.]

[Note: Thus in the same manuscript. Old Latin: “You therefore . . . act manfully.”]

[Note: Old Latin: “Always listen to him, and he,” etc. Lucifer agrees with the German manuscript.]

[Note: Old Latin: “Commander of the army, and he shall wage the people’s battle.”]

When, therefore, you see that he gave such commands to his sons and ordered them to do what he himself had also done; when he teaches that the patriarchs, prophets, and all the righteous pleased God in this way—what, you dark one, would you have had us do, lest we appear disobedient to you? Should we living persons have yielded to you, a dead man—servants of God to a minion of the devil? For you see this Mattathias saying to his sons: “Thus reflect from generation to generation: all who hope in him shall not be weakened. And do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is in dung and worms: today he is exalted, and tomorrow he shall not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his thought has perished” (ibid. 61).

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “in his dung.”]

Lest we seem injurious to you, should we spare you while you destroy the house of God—you who exist today and tomorrow will be among worms and dung—and incur before God the offence by which we deserve to be reduced to nothing together with you? Learn after this what the sons of this most devout Mattathias also did: whether they feared the hand of your fellow-executioner; whether they kept his army before their eyes rather than our Lord, whom they believed, as we believe, almighty in all things, and trusting in whom they raised themselves against the enemy with all their strength.

“And Judas, who was called Maccabaeus, his son, arose in his place; all his brothers helped him, together with all who had joined themselves to his father; and they fought the battle of Israel with joy. He spread glory among his people, put on a breastplate like a giant, girded on his weapons of war, and engaged in battles, protecting the camp with his sword. In his deeds he became like a lion, and like a lion’s cub roaring for prey. He pursued the lawless, sought them out, and set on fire those who troubled his people. The lawless shrank back in fear of him; all workers of iniquity were thrown into confusion; and salvation prospered in his hand. He embittered many kings, gladdened Jacob by his deeds, and his memory is blessed for ever. He went through the cities of Judah, destroyed all the ungodly from it, turned wrath away from Israel, was renowned to the farthest end of the earth, and gathered together those who were perishing” (ibid. 3:1 ff.).

[Note: Sabatier seems to delete *his*.]

[Note: Old Latin: “They fought.”]

[Note: This is wholly from the Greek as far as “sword,” which has ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ, “with a sword.” Old Latin: “A breastplate . . . he girded himself with his weapons of war in battles and protected the camps with his sword.”]

[Note: From the Greek. Old Latin: “Like” (without *and*) . . . “in hunting.”]

[Note: Likewise from the Greek: ἐξερευνῶν, καὶ τοὺς ταράσσοντας τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἐφλόγισε, “seeking out, he set ablaze those troubling his people.” Old Latin: “He sought out the lawless, and set aflame those who troubled . . . them.”]

[Note: These agree with the German manuscript except for *lawless*, where it has “enemies”; Greek: ἄνομοι, “lawless.” Old Latin: “His enemies were driven back . . . and salvation was directed,” etc.]

[Note: With the German manuscript. Old Latin: “He made glad . . . and for ever.” Sabatier adds *will be* in Lucifer.]

[Note: Ἐν πόλεσιν Ἰούδα, “in the cities of Judah,” in the Greek. The rest agrees with the German manuscript. Old Latin: “the cities of Judah, and he destroyed the ungodly from them.” Sabatier also reads “the cities of Judah” in Lucifer.]

Those men, inflamed with such zeal, acted against the enemies of God’s house; yet ought we not to have risen against you, lest we be called insolent? You would rightly call me insolent if we had not rightly despised your sacrilegious edict.

[Note: On this see more in the Life of Lucifer and in *On Not Associating with Heretics*.]

Consider, then, what commands the leaders of the Jews, your fellow-perishers, gave the apostles, and what the blessed choir of apostles did in opposition; you will find that we are not insolent, but desire the welfare both of you and of ourselves.

“Peter and John were going up to the temple at the ninth hour of prayer. A certain man, lame from his mother’s womb, was being carried; they laid him daily at the temple gate called Beautiful, to ask alms from those entering the temple. When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms. Peter, with John, fixed his gaze on him and said, ‘Look at us.’ And he looked at them, expecting to receive something from them. But Peter said to him, ‘Silver and gold I do not have; but what I have, this I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise and walk.’ Taking him by the right hand, he raised him up; and immediately his feet and ankles were strengthened. Leaping up, he stood and walked; and he entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God. All the people saw him walking and praising God, and recognized that he was the one who had sat for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple; and they were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him” (Acts 3:1 ff.).

[Note: Old Latin: “He was set down and carried.”]

[Note: Old Latin: “Who . . . beginning to enter . . . to receive alms from them.” Some Greek witnesses, as Lucifer, omit “to receive.”]

[Note: With the Greek, ἀτενίσας, “having fixed his gaze,” and βλέψον, “look.” Old Latin: “Looking . . . at him . . . Look upon us.” Sabatier reads: “Look at us.”]

[Note: Greek: Ὁ δέ, “but he.” Old Latin: “Who looked at them.”]

[Note: Old Latin: “Peter said . . . I do not have . . . but what I have.”]

[Note: “Having taken his right hand,” with the royal manuscript. Old Latin: “Taking him by the right hand, he lifted him; immediately his steps and soles were strengthened.”]

[Note: Old Latin: “He walked rejoicing, entered with them . . . leaping and praising God.” *Rejoicing* is absent from the Greek, as from Lucifer.]

[Note: Old Latin: “They recognized him, that this was the one . . . they were filled with astonishment . . . that had happened to him.”]

And below (ibid. 4:1): “While they were speaking these words to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees rose up against them, distressed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead; and they laid hands on them and put them in custody.”

[Note: Old Latin: “The priests and captain of the temple stood over them.”]

[Note: With the Greek: διαπονούμενοι, “being distressed,” and καταγγέλλειν, “proclaiming.” Old Latin: “Being indignant because they taught the people and preached.”]
